title: Software Engineer, Traffic Infrastructure
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Cloud Infrastructure team builds and operates the infrastructure behind OpenAI’s products, including ChatGPT and the API. Within Cloud Infrastructure, the Traffic team owns how traffic enters our cloud environments, moves between services, clusters, and regions, and reaches external dependencies.

Our work spans cloud networking, Kubernetes networking, ingress and egress gateways, proxies, load balancing, and traffic steering. We build the systems, controls, and observability that make these paths reliable, secure, efficient, and straightforward for other engineering teams to use.

 

About the Role

You’ll build and operate the networking and traffic infrastructure that connects OpenAI’s products and services across clouds and regions. The team’s work spans L3, L4, and L7—from IP connectivity, NAT, and transport behavior to service proxies and application request routing.

You’ll bring depth in part of this stack and curiosity about how the whole path works. Projects may include building gateways and control planes, improving cross-region connectivity, diagnosing packet loss or connection exhaustion, and making routing changes safer and easier to operate.

This role combines software engineering with production ownership. You’ll turn ambiguous networking problems into durable improvements, working closely with service owners, infrastructure teams, Security, and cloud providers.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA or Seattle, WA.

 

In this role, you will:

  • Design, build, and operate ingress, egress, and service-to-service connectivity across clusters, regions, and clouds.

  • Develop proxies, gateways, controllers, and automation for routing, load balancing, failover, and traffic management.

  • Build and evolve cloud networking infrastructure, including private connectivity, NAT, and network isolation.

  • Diagnose failures and performance bottlenecks across application, proxy, transport, and cloud networking layers; work with cloud providers when issues extend into their infrastructure.

  • Build telemetry and diagnostic tools that explain traffic paths, identify failing components, and help engineers take effective action.

  • Partner with Security to implement and validate traffic-path protections, including secure service communication, access controls, egress restrictions, and DDoS defenses.

  • Improve latency, throughput, availability, and network efficiency through measurement, testing, and careful production rollouts.

  • Create clear interfaces and safe defaults for service teams, participate in on-call, and turn operational lessons into changes that prevent recurring failures and reduce manual work.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 5+ years of experience building production infrastructure or distributed systems, including substantial work on networking or traffic infrastructure.

  • Have depth in one or more areas such as cloud networking, Kubernetes networking, proxies and gateways, service meshes, load balancing, or global traffic routing.

  • Understand networking fundamentals and can reason about how IP routing, TCP/UDP, DNS, NAT, TLS, and HTTP/gRPC affect connectivity and performance.

  • Have hands-on experience building or operating systems such as Envoy, NGINX, Istio, Cilium, or comparable networking infrastructure.

  • Write production software in Go, Rust, C++, Python, or a similar language, and use software and automation to solve operational problems.

  • Can investigate unfamiliar failures using evidence, test hypotheses, and follow problems through to a verified resolution.

  • Take ownership of design, implementation, rollout, and ongoing reliability, and communicate clearly across teams when a problem crosses ownership boundaries.

  • Care about making infrastructure secure and understandable for the engineers who depend on it.

We value deep expertise and the willingness to learn across boundaries. You do not need prior experience with every technology or networking layer listed above.

title: Integrated Marketing Manager, AI Impact
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Like every team at OpenAI, the Marketing team contributes to our broader mission of ensuring that artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We help people understand what AI makes possible through the experiences of the people, communities, and customers using it.

We work closely with Social, Community, Communications, Creative, Production, and other teams to bring those experiences to life. Our work connects human stories with integrated marketing programs that build understanding and inspiration with our key audience.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Integrated Marketing Manager to identify and curate the strongest proof points of AI’s impact—across people, communities, and society—and turn them into stories and programs that resonate.

You’ll be a builder and storyteller with the curiosity to uncover an extraordinary story and the initiative to make something of it. You’ll seek out people using AI in meaningful ways, build relationships, understand what has changed for them, and help them share their experiences in their own voices.

Working deeply with Social, Community, and Communications, you’ll shape stories together and build the programs, content, and distribution plans that help them travel. That could mean developing a recurring story series, bringing a community’s experience to a national audience, or turning a customer story into a program that invites others to participate.

You’ll combine strong editorial instincts with integrated marketing leadership, taking work from discovery and a clear brief through production, launch, and measurement. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable shaping an ambitious idea, facilitating a conversation with a story participant, and organizing the people and resources needed to bring a program to life.

In this role, you will:

  • Find the strongest proof points: Proactively discover people, communities, and customers using AI in meaningful ways. Evaluate the evidence, human significance, and audience relevance behind each opportunity.

  • Build alongside Social, Community, and Communications: Partner from the outset on story discovery, creative ideas, programming, and distribution. Align on a shared plan, clear roles, and the right moments to bring stories to audiences.

  • Turn stories into programs: Create integrated campaigns, recurring content series, community activations, and partnerships that give strong stories a life beyond a single asset or launch.

  • Connect national reach with local relevance: Adapt stories, formats, messengers, and programs to the audiences and communities they serve. Identify when a local story can resonate nationally and how a national program can become meaningful locally.

  • Lead work from idea to delivery: Own briefs, creative development, production, timelines, budgets, partner coordination, launch, and optimization across social, owned, earned, experiential, community, and relevant paid channels.

  • Champion craft and credibility: Partner with Creative, producers, and agencies to make distinctive, engaging content. Ground stories in demonstrated impact, bring technical ideas to life through human experiences, and represent participants accurately and thoughtfully.

  • Build a repeatable approach: Develop a network of internal and external partners and a practical process for sourcing, prioritizing, developing, and sharing stories. Create formats and programs that can grow while leaving room to act on unexpected opportunities.

title: Camera Software Engineer, Consumer Devices
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Consumer Products team at OpenAI builds end-to-end hardware and software systems that bring AI into the physical world. We work at the intersection of custom silicon, embedded systems, operating systems, and cloud services to deliver reliable, production-ready devices at scale.

Within Consumer Products, the camera stack is a critical sensing component. The team partners closely with electrical engineering, silicon vendors, systems, and higher-level perception and product teams to bring up new hardware, stabilize capture pipelines, and ensure camera systems are robust, debuggable, and ready for real-world deployment. This work spans early prototypes through production, with a strong emphasis on correctness, repeatability, and long-term reliability.

About the Role

As a Camera Firmware Engineer, you will own low-level camera enablement on custom hardware—from early board bring-up through stable production capture. You will develop and maintain the firmware and software that makes camera sensors reliable, controllable, and debuggable, forming the foundation for higher-level camera pipelines and product features.

This role is highly hands-on and systems-oriented. You will work close to the hardware, diagnose real-world timing and integration issues, and build tooling that accelerates iteration across the entire camera stack.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We follow a hybrid work model with four days per week in the office and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In This Role, You Will

  • Bring up new camera sensors and modules on prototype and production boards, including link stability, sensor control, and correct power, reset, and clock sequencing.

  • Develop and maintain low-level camera software, including sensor drivers, board configuration, and camera subsystem integration across hardware revisions.

  • Enable and validate core capture paths for development and production, including RAW capture for debugging, still capture, and hardware-accelerated video encode and streaming with stable timestamps and long-duration reliability.

  • Stand up camera control and repeatability features, including basic 3A loop exposure, manual overrides and locks, and deterministic presets to support validation and debugging.

  • Build and maintain camera bring-up tooling, such as capture scripts, automated sweeps, manifests, and debugging utilities that make issues reproducible and easy to triage.

  • Partner closely with electrical engineering, camera pipeline owners, and systems teams to define interfaces, unblock integration, and keep the camera stack stable as the device evolves.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Deep experience shipping embedded camera systems, including sensor bring-up, driver development, and board-level debugging.

  • Strong C/C++ experience with embedded or Linux-based systems; comfortable debugging across kernel and userspace boundaries.

  • Hands-on understanding of common camera hardware interfaces (for example, MIPI CSI and sensor control buses) and the practical realities of bring-up, including power, reset, clocking, and sequencing.

  • Proven track record of building reliable capture paths and effective debug workflows that accelerate iteration through reproducible failures and well-scoped fixes.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with common mobile or embedded SoC camera stacks and vendor frameworks.

  • Experience integrating and debugging hardware acceleration blocks adjacent to camera pipelines, such as video encode and decode paths.

  • Familiarity building higher-level capture pipelines (for example, GStreamer) on top of low-level camera enablement.

title: IT Software Architect, SaaS Enablement and Governance
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The SaaS and Software Governance team sits within Corporate IT and helps OpenAI scale from startup-speed tooling to mature enterprise architecture. The team owns practical governance for software, SaaS, integrations, APIs, identity, data access, and agent-enabled workflows, with a mandate to improve security, reduce software sprawl, and help business teams move faster through better foundations.

About the Team

OpenAI is scaling from an emerging, high-velocity startup into a mature enterprise operating model. The IT Software Architect will help shape the software, SaaS, Data integration, and agent-enabled architecture that lets the company move quickly while improving security, compliance, data quality, and customer, partner, and employee experience.

This role is not a traditional ivory-tower architecture function. It is a hands-on governance and enablement role that partners with business teams, IT operations, Security, Procurement, Business Platforms, Applied teams and Data Engineering to guide software decisions, reduce unmanaged sprawl, and build reusable enterprise foundations.

Why This Role Matters

OpenAI’s software footprint is expanding rapidly across SaaS, internally built tools, agents, integrations, APIs, third-party platforms, and application systems that OpenAI. The company needs a stronger tools architecture layer that can help teams make good decisions early, avoid duplicate tools, govern sensitive data and identities, and identify where OpenAI should build instead of buy.

The person in this role will help turn software governance from an approval checkpoint into an enterprise capability: a system that improves speed, reliability, security, and business outcomes.

What You'll Do

  • Own the target architecture for enterprise software, SaaS, integrations, APIs, and agent-enabled business systems across Corporate IT. Drive deprecation and consolidate targets for enterprise software.

  • Build lightweight governance patterns that guide teams before software and integration decisions become hard to unwind.

  • Create architecture standards for identity, access, data movement, API usage, admin rights, auditability, observability, and vendor integration.

  • Partner with Security to ensure software architecture addresses SSO, SCIM, MFA, privileged access, non-human identities, secrets, token storage, data residency, encryption, retention, and incident response readiness.

  • Partner with Procurement and Finance to evaluate renewals, rationalization opportunities, enterprise agreements, and build-versus-buy decisions.

  • Partner deeply with application verticals such as GTM, Finance, Legal, HR, Research, Product, and Operations teams to evaluate agentic business workflows and translate them into scalable enterprise system patterns.

  • Review proposed SaaS and internally built tools for overlap, risk, integration quality, ownership, lifecycle, supportability, and long-term fit.

  • Develop reusable architecture blueprints for common capabilities such as intake, workflow, approvals, knowledge management, customer/partner 360, data integration, reporting, content management, learning, surveys, and collaboration.

  • Help define where OpenAI-native GPT or agent-built solutions should replace or enable point SaaS tools.

  • Create clear decision records and architecture artifacts that are understandable by business leaders, engineers, security reviewers, and procurement partners.

  • Drive software catalog maturity by connecting tool inventory, business owner, system owner, integration path, data classification, access model, renewal, risk posture, and support model.

Core Architecture Domains

  • SaaS governance and software catalog maturity

  • Enterprise integration architecture, including APIs, event flows, middleware, and system-of-record boundaries

  • Identity, access, and admin model design across internal and external users

  • Data architecture for SaaS, customer, supplier, employee, partner, product, consumption, and connected business models.

  • Agentic workflow architecture and GPT-built replacement patterns

  • Vendor architecture reviews and enterprise agreement leverage across strategic platforms.

  • Security, compliance, ITGC, audit evidence, and operational readiness

  • Support model design, ownership, SLAs, escalation paths, and lifecycle management

What You'll Bring

  • 10+ years of experience in enterprise architecture, business systems architecture, IT architecture, SaaS governance, integration architecture, or a related technical leadership role.

  • Strong understanding of SaaS operating models, software lifecycle management, software asset management, and vendor/platform governance.

  • Experience designing integrations across systems, experience in large scale SaaS such as CRM, ERP and Marketplace platforms.

  • Practical knowledge of identity and access patterns including SSO, OIDC, SAML, SCIM, RBAC/ABAC, privileged admin models, service accounts, OAuth apps, and token governance.

  • Ability to evaluate software from multiple angles: business value, architecture fit, security posture, data exposure, cost, supportability, user experience, and vendor strategy.

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity, building structure where little exists, and influencing senior stakeholders without relying only on formal authority.

  • Ability to write clear architecture decision records, governance standards, system diagrams, business cases, and executive-ready recommendations.

  • Strong partner orientation: able to help teams move faster while raising the quality of decisions.

  • Curiosity about AI-native enterprise architecture and where GPT, Codex, and agentic workflows can replace or enable traditional SaaS patterns.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience scaling IT or business systems from startup-stage tooling into mature enterprise architecture.

  • Experience with software rationalization, SaaS enablement and deprecation, vendor consolidation, or enterprise license optimization.

  • Experience with architecting systems in a high-growth environment.

  • Experience building governance for internally developed tools, low-code/no-code platforms, agents, or employee-built automation.

  • Experience working closely with Security, GRC, Legal, Procurement, and Finance on cross-functional risk and control programs.

We’re looking for people who will work closely with development teams to ensure secure coding practices are integrated throughout the software development lifecycle, preventing security risks before they emerge. You will also provide security guidance to developers and other stakeholders, fostering a culture of security awareness within the organization.

The role is preferred to be based in San Francisco, Seattle or New York City but may consider remote work. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

  • Perform Security Assessments: Conduct regular security assessments, code reviews, and penetration testing to identify vulnerabilities in applications and software.

  • Develop and Implement Security Tools: Design, develop, and implement security tools, frameworks, and methodologies to protect applications against security threats.

title: Data Scientist, Ads Demand
descriptionHtml:
About the Role

OpenAI's ads business is scaling quickly. As the Data Scientist for Ads Demand, you will build the measurement and insight foundation for understanding demand health and advertiser value across the marketplace. You will partner closely with Ads Sales leadership and Ads Product leadership—along with Marketing Science and product and sales teams—to diagnose advertiser performance, define benchmarks, identify growth opportunities, and turn advertiser feedback into product priorities. Your work will shape demand strategy, improve advertiser outcomes, and help OpenAI build for its most valuable advertisers.

What You'll Do

Demand Health & Measurement

  • Define the North Star metrics, diagnostic framework, and measurement strategy for demand health across the ads system.

  • Build the operating view of demand across spend, active advertisers, retention, budget utilization, delivery, concentration, and mix; identify emerging risks and opportunities.

  • Diagnose changes in demand through cohort analysis, decomposition, experimentation, and causal methods, translating findings into clear actions for Sales and Product leadership.

Advertiser Performance & Benchmarks

  • Own the end-to-end view of advertiser outcomes—including delivery, ROAS, conversion performance, retention, and budget efficiency—for individual advertisers and key cohorts.

  • Establish actionable benchmarks by objective, vertical, advertiser size, geography, maturity, and product adoption, with statistically sound peer comparisons.

  • Develop early-warning signals and opportunity scoring that help sales teams surface under-delivery, performance risk, and advertiser growth potential.

  • Set standards for metric definitions, data quality, and interpretation so leaders can separate real marketplace changes from seasonality, selection effects, and measurement artifacts.

Insights, Adoption & Advertiser Feedback

  • Partner with Marketing Science, Sales, and Product to translate analysis into credible advertiser-facing insights, benchmarks, and best practices.

  • Design measurement plans and experiments that quantify how best-practice and product adoption affect delivery, ROAS, retention, and long-term advertiser value.

  • Build a systematic feedback loop that converts advertiser input into quantified themes and prioritized product opportunities, then measures whether shipped changes improve outcomes.

Strategy, Forecasting & Business Impact

  • Partner with Ads Sales leadership to segment demand, size opportunities, forecast outcomes, and inform demand strategies, sales plays, and investments.

  • Partner with Ads Product leadership to estimate advertiser value, prioritize the roadmap, and measure the business impact of product launches.

What We're Looking For

Required

  • 7+ years of experience in data science or analytics within an ads platform, marketplace, or performance-oriented B2B business.

  • Demonstrated business impact through advertiser demand growth, improved delivery or ROAS, stronger retention, or decisions that changed product and sales strategy.

  • Strong SQL and Python or R, with depth in measurement, experimentation, causal inference, segmentation, benchmarking, and forecasting.

  • Exceptional cross-functional communication and influence with both sales and product leaders, plus a hands-on approach to ambiguous, 0-to-1 problems.

Strongly Preferred

  • Experience at a high-performing ads business where data scientists work broadly across Sales, Marketing Science, and Product rather than in a narrow silo.

  • Hands-on familiarity with ad delivery, auctions, measurement, attribution, conversion signals, and the advertiser lifecycle.

  • Experience turning customer feedback into product priorities and evidence-backed best practices that improve advertiser outcomes.

title: Product Data Scientist - Youth, Families and Learning
descriptionHtml:
About the role

We’re looking for a product data scientist to help OpenAI create more value and drive sustainable growth for young people, families, and learners. You’ll drive product data science across under-18 audiences, emerging opportunities for children under 13, family experiences, and learning and education more broadly.

You’ll help decide where we should invest, what we should build, and how we’ll know it is working. This means understanding distinct audience needs, identifying promising use cases, and turning evidence into a clear product strategy. Your work will connect discovery and early product development with adoption, retention, and sustained user value.

You’ll partner across Chat Product, Growth, Foundations, SafeSys, and other teams, working closely with product managers, engineers, designers, and researchers. The role focuses and owns product value and growth while dedicated teams own policy and safety.

In this role, you will:

  • Shape strategy and prioritize opportunities. Size unmet needs and growth opportunities across audiences, use cases, and product experiences. Help teams choose where to invest and sequence work based on expected user value, reach, evidence, and effort.

  • Define what value and success mean. Develop an audience-specific measurement framework spanning activation, task success, learning progress, satisfaction, and durable retention. Connect these measures to product goals and assess whether repeat use reflects meaningful benefit.

  • Understand users and growth drivers. Analyze journeys, funnels, and cohorts to uncover where people find value, where they struggle, and what helps them return. Combine behavioral data with surveys and user research to explain differences across ages, family roles, and learning contexts.

  • Measure what changes actually cause. Design experiments and holdouts to evaluate product and model changes. Apply causal methods when randomization is impractical, make assumptions explicit, and account for seasonality, audience composition, and effects that differ across segments.

  • Turn findings into product decisions. Work with partners from initial hypotheses through launch and iteration. Recommend what to build, change, expand, or stop, explaining expected impact, uncertainty, and tradeoffs. Follow through to determine whether decisions delivered the intended results.

  • Build reliable measurement. Partner with engineering on instrumentation, dataset quality, and consistent audience definitions. Create reusable analyses and dashboards that make progress visible and let teams answer recurring questions independently.

  • Create alignment across teams. Bring a coherent view of audience value to work spanning multiple roadmaps. Help partners agree on priorities, success criteria, and the next questions to resolve, even when ownership is distributed and evidence is incomplete.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • A record of influencing product strategy and improving user outcomes through hands-on data science, including work from an ambiguous question to a decision and measurable impact.

  • Strong SQL and Python skills, sound statistical judgment, and practical experience with experiments, causal inference, cohort analysis, and measurement design.

  • The ability to develop useful definitions of product value, validate imperfect proxies, and distinguish short-term metric movement from lasting improvement.

  • Clear communication and strong product judgment. You can make a recommendation, explain its limits, and influence collaborators across functions without relying on formal authority.

  • Comfort setting priorities independently across a broad scope, staying close to users, and moving between strategic questions and detailed analytical work.

Helpful experience

Experience with consumer product growth, youth or family products, learning and education, or generative AI would be valuable. We also welcome experience measuring learning outcomes, combining quantitative and qualitative research, or evaluating products whose value emerges over time.

title: Software Engineer, Resilience Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Join the engineering teams that bring OpenAI’s ideas safely to the world!

The Applied Engineering team works across research, engineering, product, and design to bring OpenAI’s technology to consumers and businesses. We seek to learn from deployment and distribute the benefits of AI, while ensuring that this powerful tool is used responsibly and safely. Safety is more important to us than unfettered growth.

About the Role

As OpenAI continues to grow, we are looking for experienced, problem-solving engineers to ensure our systems scale. Our success depends on our ability to quickly iterate on products while also ensuring that they are performant and reliable. You will work in a deeply iterative, collaborative, fast-paced environment to bring our technology to millions of users around the world, and ensure it’s delivered with safety and reliability in mind. Successful candidates will play a crucial role in ensuring the reliability, scalability, and performance of our systems as we continue to expand. As a reliability expert, you will be at the forefront of maintaining and enhancing the stability, scalability, and performance of our rapidly evolving infrastructure. You will work closely with cross-functional teams, including software engineers, product managers, and data scientists, to build and maintain resilient systems that can handle our growing user base and workload.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and implement solutions to ensure the scalability of our infrastructure to meet rapidly increasing demands.

  • Build and maintain the load, chaos and synthetic-testing software leveraged by development teams to make the systems they design and operate more reliable.

  • Build and maintain automation tools to streamline repetitive tasks and improve system reliability.

  • Build and maintain the platform for CPU, storage, GPU, and network lifecycle management to drive efficiency, accountability and dynamic optimization of our resources.

  • Implement fault-tolerant and resilient design patterns to minimize service disruptions.

  • Develop and maintain service level objectives (SLOs) and service level indicators (SLIs) to measure and ensure system reliability.

  • Partner with researchers, engineers, product managers, and designers to bring new features and research capabilities to the world.

  • Participate in an on-call rotation to respond to critical incidents and ensure 24/7 system availability.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a track record of accelerating engineering reliability by building world-class tooling and systems from 0→1.

  • Have a humble attitude, an eagerness to help your colleagues, and a desire to do whatever it takes to make the team succeed.

  • Own problems end-to-end, and are willing to pick up whatever knowledge you're missing to get the job done.

  • Enjoy seeking out and addressing bottlenecks and areas for performance improvement in our systems.

  • Utilize Infrastructure as Code (IaC) principles to automate infrastructure provisioning and configuration management.

  • Are experienced in collaborating with cross-functional teams to ensure that reliability and scalability are considered in the design and development of new features and services.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field (or equivalent work experience).

  • Proven experience as an SWE focused on reliability or a similar role in a fast-paced, rapidly scaling company.

  • Strong proficiency in cloud infrastructure.

  • Proficiency in programming languages.

  • Experience with containerization technologies and container orchestration platforms like Kubernetes.

  • Knowledge of IaC tools such as Terraform or CloudFormation.

  • Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting skills.

  • Strong communication and collaboration skills.

  • Experience with observability tools such as Datadog, Prometheus, Grafana and Splunk.

title: Software Engineer, Core Network Engineering
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Core Network Engineering team owns the end-to-end networking stack that connects OpenAI’s compute infrastructure — spanning global WAN/edge connectivity, data-center networking, and high-performance host/xPU networking used for large-scale training and inference workloads.

This team is responsible for ensuring networking is never the bottleneck to model training efficiency, cluster reliability, or fleet expansion. They design and operate the systems that provide predictable, high-throughput, low-latency connectivity across some of the world’s most advanced AI infrastructure.

About the Role

We’re looking for engineers to help build and operate the networking foundation behind OpenAI’s frontier AI systems.

Depending on your background and area of focus, you may work across host networking, datacenter fabrics, or global WAN infrastructure. The problems span low-level systems software, distributed infrastructure, protocol readiness, observability, performance engineering, automation, and large-scale network operations.

You’ll work on systems where microseconds of latency, tail performance, and network reliability directly impact model training efficiency and production serving performance.

This role is ideal for engineers who enjoy operating close to the hardware/software boundary and solving performance-critical infrastructure problems at massive scale.

In this role, you will:

  • Design, build, and operate networking systems that support large-scale AI training and inference infrastructure

  • Improve performance, reliability, and scalability across host networking, datacenter fabrics, and WAN systems

  • Develop automation for provisioning, configuration management, validation, upgrades, and lifecycle management of networking infrastructure

  • Build tooling and observability systems for network health, performance analysis, debugging, and automated remediation

  • Optimize network performance across technologies such as RDMA, RoCE, InfiniBand, Ethernet, and high-performance GPU interconnects

  • Define and operationalize networking protocols, readiness criteria, and continuous validation systems

  • Partner closely with compute, storage, hardware, and infrastructure teams to ensure networking scales predictably with fleet growth

  • Contribute to architecture decisions around topology design, capacity planning, failure domains, and network reliability

  • Diagnose complex distributed systems and networking issues across large heterogeneous compute environments

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have experience building or operating large-scale networking or distributed systems infrastructure

  • Are comfortable working close to the hardware/software boundary

  • Have experience with Linux networking, kernel systems, NICs, RDMA, or performance-sensitive infrastructure software

  • Have worked with high-performance networking technologies such as InfiniBand, RoCE, DPDK, or large-scale Ethernet fabrics

  • Have experience with datacenter networking, WAN systems, or host networking stacks

  • Enjoy debugging complex systems and performance bottlenecks across multiple layers of the stack

  • Are comfortable writing production software in languages such as C++, Python, or Go

  • Have strong systems fundamentals across networking, operating systems, distributed systems, or infrastructure engineering

descriptionHtml:

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team partners with healthcare organizations to deploy production AI systems across clinical, operational, and member-facing workflows. We work at the boundary of customer deployment and core platform development, using customer engagements to define repeatable architectures, evaluations, integrations, and operating standards for complex, regulated healthcare environments.

We are hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to own end-to-end deployments of our models within healthcare organizations, including payers, providers, health systems, and healthcare technology companies. You will measure success through production adoption, measurable workflow impact, and evaluation loops that establish customer-specific benchmarks, acceptance criteria, and launch readiness. You’ll collaborate directly with customer technical and operational teams, alongside internal Business, Research, Product, Engineering, and Security partners, to deliver solutions and translate deployment learnings into product improvements. This role is based New York City. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required.

  • Own the technical solution end to end, from customer discovery and workflow scoping through architecture, hands-on implementation, evaluation, production deployment, adoption, and handoff.

title: Manager, Applied AI Architect (India)
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Applied AI Architect team partners with organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact. We work with customers across industries to identify where AI can create value, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption. The team brings together technical strategy, customer partnership, and practical deployment expertise, working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and specialist delivery teams.

About the Role

As the Manager of Applied AI Architects, you will lead a team of senior technical leaders responsible for the technical strategy, customer journey, and path to production value for OpenAI's largest and most complex customers. Your team will act as the “CTO of the book of business,” partnering with customer executives and technical teams from pre-sales discovery and solution evaluation through deployment, adoption, and measurable business impact.

You will set the operating model for how Applied AI Architects own technical account plans across ChatGPT Enterprise, the OpenAI API, Codex, and other agentic AI solutions. In close partnership with Sales leadership and Account Directors, you will help prioritize customer portfolios, allocate technical resources, and ensure business priorities translate into focused use cases, credible architectures, actionable adoption roadmaps, and durable customer value and growth.

You will remain accountable for the team's technical outcomes while developing its people and bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, enablement, security, product, research, and partners. You will serve as an executive technical sponsor for critical engagements, a senior voice of the customer inside OpenAI, and a cross-functional leader who can move confidently between regional strategy, executive decision-making, architectural depth, and hands-on coaching.

This role is based in Bangalore.

In this role, you will:

  • Hire, coach, and develop a high-performing team of Applied AI Architects, creating an environment of technical excellence, sound judgment, continuous learning, accountability, and strong customer stewardship.

  • Define and continuously refine the strategy and operating model for Applied AI Architecture teams, aligning company priorities with the evolving needs of strategic customers and the regional go-to-market.

  • Partner with Sales leadership and Account Directors to prioritize accounts and opportunities, allocate technical resources effectively, and establish clear technical strategies for the region's most consequential engagements.

  • Ensure Applied AI Architects serve as the primary technical advisors for their portfolios, owning technical account plans, technical milestones, adoption priorities, account health, and expansion opportunities.

  • Lead complex, multi-threaded customer journeys that connect executive vision and business outcomes with use-case qualification, solution evaluation, enterprise governance, and a credible path to production.

  • Coach the team on Applied AI architectures spanning models, applications, data, integration, identity, security, privacy, governance, evaluation, reliability, and deployment.

title: Product Designer, Accessibility
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Design Systems team creates the foundations that help teams across OpenAI build coherent, high-quality experiences at scale.

Accessibility is fundamental to that work. We’re building the shared standards, components, tools, and practices that make inclusive experiences the default across OpenAI’s products and platforms.

About the Role

In this role, you’ll lead OpenAI’s company-wide accessibility program from within the Design Foundations team within Product Design. You’ll pair strategy and organizational influence with hands-on product design (visual and interaction design) —advocating for disabled people, removing barriers across complete customer journeys, and establishing durable ownership throughout the company.

This is an opportunity to define accessibility for a new generation of products spanning web, mobile, desktop, voice, AI, and hardware. You’ll help teams consider the many ways people perceive, understand, navigate, and interact with technology, going beyond minimum compliance to create experiences that are genuinely useful and inclusive.

Working across design, engineering, research, product, go-to-market, and legal, you’ll make accessibility an expected part of product quality—not a final review or the responsibility of a single expert.

This role is based in our San Francisco HQ. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role you will:

  • Design and ship product experiences while identifying systemic barriers across complete customer journeys.

  • Define OpenAI’s accessibility strategy, roadmap, governance, priorities, and measures of progress.

  • Build accessibility into our design system through inclusive components, tokens, interaction patterns, Figma libraries, documentation, and engineering guardrails.

  • Center disabled people through participatory research, usability studies, and assistive-technology testing rather than relying solely on assumptions, simulations, or automated tools.

  • Design for permanent, temporary, and situational disabilities, including multiple ways to perceive information, navigate interfaces, understand content, and complete important tasks.

  • Establish practical standards for screen readers, keyboard navigation, focus, reading order, contrast, typography, motion, captions, forms, errors, and multimodal interactions.

  • Lead accessibility audits, remediation priorities, launch readiness, and continuous validation across platforms.

  • Partner with go-to-market, legal, compliance, and product teams on enterprise readiness, accessibility documentation, procurement needs, and customer commitments.

  • Grow company-wide capability through training, critiques, engineering partnerships, and a network of accessibility champions.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Pair deep accessibility expertise with a very high bar for design craft: strong interaction design, visual design, systems thinking, and prototyping skills

  • Have led accessibility or inclusive-design work across multiple teams, products, or platforms.

  • Understand the relationship between accessibility, usability, and inclusive design—and know when to go beyond standards to meet real human needs.

  • Have deep practical knowledge of WCAG, assistive technologies, accessible interaction design, and platform-specific standards.

  • Have embedded accessibility into design systems, reusable components, and engineering workflows.

  • Have worked directly with disabled people and translated their experiences into meaningful product and organizational decisions.

title: Commissioning and Quality Program Manager
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital partners, is building the world’s most advanced AI infrastructure ecosystem. The Compute team sets core infrastructure strategy and executes at global scale—spanning site selection through full buildout, in close partnership with internal and external stakeholders.

About the Role

We’re hiring a Commissioning and Quality Program Manager to oversee quality assurance, quality control and commissioning across all phases of our global hyperscale data center program. You will oversee the delivery quality for a massive portfolio of projects across several campuses. You’ll ensure work meets or exceeds OpenAI’s design standards, performance requirements, and reliability expectations—from early construction through commissioning and turnover to operations.

You’ll own development and enforcement of QA/QC standards, inspection protocols, commissioning scope, and acceptance criteria, working closely with contractors, design teams, and commissioning partners to embed a quality-first culture.

Travel: Up to 50%

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain the portfolio-level QA/QC program for hyperscale data center construction (standards, checklists, acceptance protocols).

  • Review and approve developer QA/QC and commissioning plans for alignment with project specs and industry best practices.

  • Oversee site inspections across civil, structural, architectural, mechanical, and electrical scopes.

  • Validate installation quality against drawings, specifications, and manufacturer requirements.

  • Monitor and track punch list items, NCRs, and corrective actions with the developer and contractors, including critical Method of Procedure (MOP) work.

  • Partner with the developer’s commissioning teams to ensure QA/QC documentation supports readiness for both functional and integrated testing.

  • Validate functional and integrated systems testing completion in preparation for OAI acceptance.

  • Maintain real-time quality tracking and reporting dashboards for program leadership.

  • Train and guide site teams on quality expectations, inspections, and documentation standards.

  • Drive continuous improvement by capturing lessons learned and updating standards for future sites.

Qualifications

  • Have 10+ years managing quality and commissioning for mission-critical, hyperscale, or complex commercial developments.

  • Have deep technical knowledge of construction means/methods and quality standards across major trades.

  • Can interpret design documents, specs, and submittals to verify field compliance.

  • Have experience developing and implementing quality management systems at program or portfolio scale.

  • Communicate effectively with executives, contractors, and site teams—translating findings into actionable recommendations.

  • Proactively identify quality risks before they impact cost or schedule.

  • Thrive in fast-paced, complex environments and can drive accountability across stakeholders.

Preferred Skills

  • This role is central to ensuring every system is delivered to spec, on time, and built to last—supporting OpenAI’s reliability expectations across a global hyperscale build program

    Familiarity with industry commissioning standards and frameworks (e.g., ASHRAE, Uptime Institute, CSA, BICSI).

  • Ability to operate effectively in global environments, including managing cultural, regulatory, and contractor differences across regions.

The Database Systems team specializes in high-performance distributed databases. Our team built Rockset, the real-time search, analytics, and vector database that powers all vector search and retrieval augmented generation (RAG) at OpenAI. title: Mechanical Engineer, Dynamometer and Actuator Testing Infrastructure
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.

About the Role

We are seeking a Mechanical Engineer to design, build, and own the mechanical side of our robotic actuator dynamometer and test infrastructure. You will create the test stands, couplings, fixtures, load paths, guarding, and serviceable lab hardware that enable rigorous characterization of robotic actuators.

This role combines precision mechanical design with hands-on lab work. You will take robotic actuator test infrastructure from requirements and analysis through CAD, fabrication, assembly, commissioning, and iteration, partnering closely with electrical and software engineers to deliver safe, flexible, high-uptime test cells.

In this role, you will

  • Own the mechanical architecture of dynamometer and actuator test cells, including frames, bases, load paths, alignment, guarding, and serviceability.

  • Design dynamometer structures, robotic actuator fixtures, load-motor mounts, couplings, shafts, bearings, adapters, and torque-reaction hardware.

  • Translate robotic actuator test requirements into robust mechanical systems for torque, speed, thermal, durability, backdrive, efficiency, and failure testing.

  • Perform first-principles analysis and simulation for stiffness, strength, fatigue, vibration, thermal growth, critical speed, and safety factors.

  • Create precise, repeatable alignment strategies that protect test articles, load machines, sensors, and couplings.

  • Design modular fixturing that supports rapid changeover across actuator and motor variants without compromising measurement quality.

  • Work closely with electrical engineers on cable routing, enclosures, cooling, sensor packaging, and test-cell safety interfaces.

  • Work closely with software and controls engineers to define mechanical limits, safe operating envelopes, and automated-test constraints.

  • Build, assemble, debug, and improve test stands in the lab, using measurement and fabrication tools directly.

  • Develop guarding, containment, pinch-point mitigation, hard stops, and other mechanical safety systems for high-energy rotating equipment.

  • Manage fabrication partners and vendors for machined parts, weldments, bearings, couplings, sensors, and test-stand components.

  • Establish drawings, tolerance stacks, assembly procedures, inspection plans, and preventive-maintenance practices.

  • Use test observations and failure analysis to continuously improve durability, usability, uptime, and measurement fidelity.

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Have strong intuition for load paths, stiffness, alignment, rotating machinery, and the practical behavior of real hardware.

  • Enjoy designing fixtures and structures that are precise, robust, safe, and easy for others to use.

  • Are highly hands-on and comfortable assembling, aligning, instrumenting, and debugging test equipment.

  • Can move fluidly between first-principles analysis, CAD, vendor collaboration, and lab iteration.

  • Care about details such as tolerances, runout, resonance, thermal growth, guarding, and serviceability.

  • Are comfortable working in fast-moving environments with evolving test needs and aggressive technical goals.

  • Take ownership of the full test-stand lifecycle, from concept through reliable daily operation.

  • Communicate clearly across mechanical, electrical, controls, software, safety, and operations teams.

  • Are motivated by building infrastructure that reveals how advanced robotic actuators really perform.

  • Are excited to build mechanical test infrastructure that accelerates robotic actuator development.

Preferred qualifications

  • Preferred qualifications

  • Bachelor’s or graduate degree in Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, Mechatronics, or a related field.

  • Experience designing mechanical systems for robotic actuator dynamometers, robotics, automation, rotating machinery, aerospace, automotive, or similar high-performance hardware.

  • Strong understanding of structures, load paths, shafts, bearings, couplings, fasteners, tolerances, alignment, and vibration.

  • Experience designing fixtures, test stands, frames, guarding, and precision mechanical interfaces.

  • Proficiency with CAD and drawing release workflows; NX, SolidWorks, Creo, or equivalent experience is welcome.

  • Experience with structural, thermal, fatigue, or modal analysis and applying results to practical hardware decisions.

  • Hands-on experience with assembly, machining, metrology, alignment, and troubleshooting in a lab or prototype environment.

  • Familiarity with mechanical safety for rotating equipment, containment, interlocks, and safe operating envelopes.

title: Staff Backend Engineer, Financial Engineering
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Financial Engineering (FinEng) builds the financial systems behind ChatGPT, Codex, and OpenAI’s API platform. These products serve people, developers, and businesses around the world. We make them easy to buy, use, and pay for. Our systems support everything from individual subscriptions to usage-based billing and complex enterprise agreements.

We also build the foundations for how products are packaged, accessed, and used: product catalogs, SKUs and bundles, workspaces, entitlements, and usage metering. These systems connect what customers purchase to the capabilities they can access and the usage they can manage.

That reach creates challenging engineering problems. We build services and data pipelines that handle large volumes of usage and transactions, keep payments, product access, and financial records consistent across systems, and adapt as products and pricing change. The same foundations must support a simple checkout and the detailed spending controls a large business needs.

Your work will help teams launch new products faster and give customers confidence in what they are paying for. The work spans customer experiences, backend services, and data systems, with opportunities to influence technical design and see your work through to production.

We’re hiring Staff+ engineers with strong backend experience. Experience in payments, billing, or financial systems is a strong plus, but not required.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and build systems for purchasing, payments, subscriptions, and billing across OpenAI products and global markets.

  • Build product catalogs, SKUs, and bundles that let product teams launch new offerings and evolve how products are packaged.

  • Develop workspace and entitlement systems that connect purchases and subscriptions to product access for individuals and teams.

  • Keep charges and product access correct when requests are retried, updates arrive late, or another service fails.

  • Build metering systems, data pipelines, and APIs that turn large volumes of usage into accurate bills, timely spending information, and records that are easy to trace and verify.

title: Data Program Manager, Science
descriptionHtml:
About the Team
OpenAI’s Research Data team exists to accelerate the evaluation, safety and capabilities of our models and products. Made up of technical operators and software engineers, we design the methods through which we acquire and create data.

About the Role
As a Data Program Manager, Science, you will help researchers develop and execute scientific data programs, connecting OpenAI’s research priorities with relevant data, expertise and external partners.

You’ll work closely with researchers to understand their needs, assess the scientific and practical value of opportunities, and develop partnerships across the scientific ecosystem. The work could range from acquiring existing datasets to shaping research collaborations. You’ll carry opportunities from initial investigation through commercial discussions, agreements, delivery and research use, exercising sound judgement around sensitive data and relationships.

Our current work focuses particularly on biology and chemistry. We welcome different combinations of scientific, technical and partnership experience.

This role is based in our San Francisco HQ.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop data strategies with Research. Translate research goals, model limitations and evaluation gaps into evidence needs and success criteria. Compare acquisition with internal, public and commissioned alternatives.

  • Find distinctive sources for research. Build trusted local and international relationships across research and industry, including organisations at the scientific frontier.

  • Assess opportunities in scientific context. Inspect samples for provenance, context, quality and completeness. Assess usefulness, involving researchers and specialists as needed.

  • Shape partnerships with lasting scientific value. Understand partners’ ambitions and define pilots, deliverables and acceptance criteria, considering expertise, scientific contribution and continuing relationships alongside commercial terms.

  • Lead commercial and operational execution. Develop proposals, assess pricing and negotiate terms. Coordinate Legal, Privacy, Security, Procurement and engineering to clarify permissions, responsibilities and delivery.

  • Navigate sensitive collaborations. Understand institutional interests and confidentiality. Identify ethical, privacy, security and misuse concerns early, involving specialists to develop responsible arrangements.

  • Follow through into research use. Coordinate preparation, ingestion, access and documentation. Gather researcher feedback to inform whether to expand, change or stop.

  • Make thoughtful portfolio decisions. Recommend options based on research value, cost, timing and capacity. Identify shared needs and opportunities for useful collaboration across projects.

  • Make the work more repeatable. Use code, APIs, automation and AI tools to improve sourcing, assessment and delivery. Resolve recurring blockers with engineers and retain partner knowledge and research feedback.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have substantial grounding in biology, chemistry or related sciences through research, industry or equivalent experience, and engage critically with methods and evidence.

  • Have delivered complex scientific, data or partnership projects, with depth in one or more of scientific data and evaluation, commercial partnerships or research collaborations across organisations.

  • Exercise sound judgement: test claims, match evidence to research needs and make clear recommendations while acknowledging uncertainty.

  • Work directly with data: inspect unfamiliar files, investigate quality and use Python, SQL, APIs and AI-assisted coding to answer questions and reduce manual work.

  • Build trust through careful listening, precise questions and thoughtful negotiation. You bring relevant local and international relationships, or a demonstrated ability to develop them, and understand what partners value beyond the transaction.

  • Exercise discretion, recognising the limits of your expertise and authority and when scientific, ethical or safety questions need specialist input.

  • Thrive in a fast-moving environment, taking broad ownership across multiple projects and moving readily between scientific, technical and commercial questions. You prioritise thoughtfully as needs change, making clear decisions about where to focus and what can wait.

  • Enjoy getting your hands dirty, bringing energy and creative problem solving to unfamiliar or ambiguous opportunities. You turn them into practical plans and follow through on the details.

  • Learn exceptionally quickly, developing your understanding of AI training, evaluation and unfamiliar research areas to become a useful collaborator.

  • We welcome different combinations of scientific, technical and partnership experience. You do not need equal depth in every area.

title: Component and Product Quality Engineer, Interconnects
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

OpenAI's Hardware organization builds supercompute platforms from silicon and boards to full rack-scale systems to power advanced AI workloads. This role owns end-to-end quality for high-speed interconnect hardware across the product lifecycle: early design influence, supplier/contract manufacturer readiness, qualification, ramp, and fleet quality in lab and data center environments.

You will be the quality lead for advanced interconnect components and assemblies, including high-speed copper cables, cable cartridges, patch panels, backplane/cable-backplane solutions, high-speed connectors, and related electro-mechanical interfaces. You will partner closely with electrical, mechanical, SI/PI, systems, reliability, operations, and external vendors to prevent escapes and drive rapid, data-driven containment and corrective action.

In this role you will:

  • Own quality for advanced interconnect components and assemblies: high-speed connectors, high-speed copper cables, cable cartridges (e.g., cable cassette style assemblies), patch panels & optics, and backplane/cable-backplane interconnect solutions.

  • Drive quality-by-design: participate in design reviews, DFM/DFx, tolerance stacks, material and plating selections, connector mating strategy, strain relief, and assembly methods to reduce variation and field failures.

  • Define and track quality and reliability metrics (DPPM, yield, escapes, RMA/FRACAS trends, Cpk/Ppk where applicable) for interconnects across NPI and mass production.

  • Build and execute qualification strategies for cables/connectors/patch panels (mechanical, environmental, electrical, and reliability), including test coverage, sample plans, clear pass/fail criteria, defining installation criteria and processes, optics termination quality management and setting fiber standards criteria.

  • Partner with engineering and operations to drive smooth ramp: risk assessments, pilot build learnings, change control, and readiness reviews (EVT/DVT/PVT/MP or equivalent phases).

  • Own supplier and CM performance management: scorecards, audits (process and quality system), and follow-up to close findings with verified effectiveness

  • Work with suppliers to improve manufacturing throughput, stability, and yields for cable and connector assembly processes (e.g., wire prep, welding/crimping, overmolding/injection molding, plating, and assembly fixturing).

  • Lead rapid containment and root-cause investigations for failures found during bring-up, system integration tests, reliability testing, and fleet deployments.

  • Own the end-to-end corrective action process (8D, 5-Whys, Ishikawa, DOE as needed): define problem statements, isolate variables, validate root cause, implement fixes, and verify effectiveness.

  • Partner with SI/PI and test teams to correlate electrical performance issues (e.g., link margin, BER, eye closure, impedance discontinuities, PAM4, TDR and VNA) with manufacturing and mechanical drivers (connector wear, plating, contamination, misalignment, cable routing, assembly variation).

  • Support integration and deployment of OpenAI supercompute racks in lab and data center environments; identify quality risks tied to shipping, handling, installation, and service operations.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • 7+ years of experience in quality engineering, manufacturing quality, supplier quality, or reliability for interconnects or high-speed hardware used in servers, networking, storage, or high-performance compute systems.

  • Hands-on experience with high-speed copper interconnect products: connectors and/or cable assemblies; familiarity with patch panels or backplane/cable-backplane solutions is a plus

  • Strong command of problem-solving and quality tools: 8D, 5-Whys, Fishbone, PFMEA/control plans, SPC/MSA (gauge R&R), and change control.

  • Ability to read and interpret mechanical drawings, GD&T basics, and electrical/interface specifications; comfortable working across ME/EE/SI disciplines.

  • Experience driving supplier/CM improvements (audits, scorecards, CAPA) and managing nonconformance/MRB workflows.

  • Clear written and verbal communication skills; ability to drive alignment across internal teams and external partners.

  • Experience with cable manufacturing and assembly processes (wire treatment, resistance welding/laser welding, crimping, overmolding/injection molding, braiding/shielding, plating, and automated test).

  • Experience with optical interconnects (AOC/DAC, pluggable modules such as QSFP/OSFP), fiber termination quality, optical return loss, end-face inspection standards (IEC 61300), and contamination control practices.

  • Ability to travel internationally and work effectively across time zones with ODM/JDM and supplier partners.

title: Founding Software Engineer, Physical Engineering
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Physical Engineering team sits within OpenAI’s Enterprise Verticals organization. We’re exploring how frontier AI can help people design, simulate, and build better physical products—shortening development cycles, improving product performance, and expanding what engineering teams can accomplish.

Our initial focus is on mechanical and electrical engineering. We’re building experiences within ChatGPT and integrations with engineering software to help engineers move from early concepts through design, simulation, and preparation for production.

We operate as a small founding team within OpenAI, working directly with customers and closely with research, design, and forward deployed engineers. We learn by building, putting products in users’ hands, and using their feedback to guide our next steps.

About the Role

As a Founding Full Stack Software Engineer, you’ll help define and build the product and technical foundations of this new vertical. You’ll work across frontend experiences, backend services, and integrations to bring AI into complex engineering workflows.

You’ll combine strong software engineering fundamentals with product judgment and an eye for intuitive user experiences. Working directly with engineers and design partners, you’ll identify valuable problems, prototype solutions, and develop them into reliable products.

We’re particularly interested in engineers who have built CAD, CAE, simulation, or other engineering design software. You should be comfortable owning work independently, making decisions with incomplete information, and moving between product details and system architecture.

This is an opportunity to shape a new product area from its earliest stages, with significant influence over what we build, how it works, and the team we become.

In this role, you will:

  • Build and ship full-stack AI products that help mechanical and electrical engineers work through design and simulation tasks.

  • Own projects from customer discovery and prototyping through production deployment and iteration.

  • Create intuitive interfaces that help users understand, inspect, and refine complex engineering outputs.

  • Develop backend services, APIs, plugins, and integrations that connect OpenAI models with engineering software.

  • Work directly with customers to understand engineering constraints, identify valuable applications, and translate specific needs into broadly useful products.

  • Partner with research, design, platform, and forward deployed engineering teams to bring emerging AI capabilities into practical workflows.

  • Evaluate quality and reliability, using customer feedback and product evidence to understand whether we’re improving how engineers work.

  • Help establish the technical foundations and engineering practices of a growing team.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have independently built and shipped substantial software products, with ownership across frontend and backend systems.

  • Bring strong product instincts and UI judgment, especially for tools that make complex work easier to understand and perform.

  • Enjoy working directly with users and translating their needs into thoughtful product and technical decisions.

  • Can turn an ambiguous opportunity into a clear starting point and a working product.

  • Move quickly, make pragmatic tradeoffs, and stay accountable for quality after launch.

  • Learn unfamiliar tools and domains quickly and communicate clearly across disciplines.

  • Are excited about applying frontier AI to the design and development of physical products.

Particularly relevant experience

  • Building CAD, CAE, simulation, electrical design, or related professional software.

  • Developing interactive tools for visual, spatial, or technically complex workflows.

  • Connecting engineering tools through APIs, plugins, or extensions.

  • Building AI-powered applications and evaluating their usefulness and reliability.

  • Taking a product from concept to production as a founder or early engineer.

title: Senior Special Programs Security Manager (CSSO/CPSO)
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Industrial Security team enables OpenAI’s classified and national security work by building secure, compliant programs that support government customers and protect sensitive information. We partner across Security, Legal, People, Facilities, Engineering, IT, and program leadership to translate complex government requirements into practical operating models that allow important work to move forward responsibly. Our work spans personnel security, classified facilities, special programs, government customer engagement, and the safeguards required to operate in highly regulated environments.

About the Role

As a Senior Special Programs Security Manager, you will lead security operations for OpenAI’s Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) and Special Access Programs (SAP), serving in customer-designated roles such as Contractor Special Security Officer (CSSO) or Contractor Program Security Officer (CPSO). You will help shape how OpenAI operates across the Intelligence Community and other national security environments, building the relationships, processes, and security foundations required to support classified work at scale.

We’re looking for someone who brings deep special programs expertise, sound operational judgment, and the credibility to work directly with government customers and senior internal stakeholders. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone comfortable navigating ambiguity, helping build the function, mentoring future team members, and finding compliant paths forward when mission needs and security requirements intersect.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, or Washington, DC. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. Additional onsite presence and occasional travel may be required based on classified program, facility, and government customer needs.

This position requires active Top Secret eligibility, current SCI access, and a current counterintelligence (CI) polygraph at the time of application. Candidates must also be able to obtain and maintain additional customer-required accesses, including a full-scope polygraph if required.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead SCI and SAP security operations across the program lifecycle, including access administration, indoctrinations and debriefings, security plans, classification requirements, incident reporting, inspections, and program closeout.

  • Serve as the designated CSSO, CPSO, or equivalent program security official for assigned government customers and classified programs.

  • Build and maintain trusted relationships with Intelligence Community and Department of Defense customers, government security officers, program security officers, and other external security stakeholders.

  • Oversee the establishment, accreditation, operation, modification, and inspection readiness of Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities and Special Access Program Facilities.

  • Translate government regulations, contract requirements, DD Forms 254, security classification guides, and customer direction into practical policies, procedures, and operating decisions.

  • Coordinate closely with personnel security, information systems security, classified IT, Facilities, Legal, and program teams to establish clear ownership and integrated safeguards.

  • Lead self-inspections, security inquiries, corrective actions, customer assessments, and escalation of risks that could affect access, accreditation, or program execution.

  • Advise Industrial Security leadership, independently represent the security function, and provide operational continuity across critical programs and customer relationships.

  • Mentor and develop special programs security personnel while establishing the staffing, metrics, governance, and operating rhythms needed to support continued growth.

  • Enable classified work through risk-informed decisions while maintaining the judgment and authority to stop or escalate activity that would violate security requirements.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have substantial experience leading contractor security for SCI and SAP programs, including direct experience as a CSSO, CPSO, CSPSO, SSO, or comparable customer-designated security official.

  • Understand how Intelligence Community customers operate, including sponsor relationships, access processes, reciprocity, customer-specific requirements, and appropriate escalation channels.

  • Have strong working knowledge of the NISPOM, ICDs 703, 704, and 705, Intelligence Community technical specifications for SCIFs, DoDM 5205.07, applicable Security Executive Agent Directives, and related customer guidance.

  • Have established, accredited, operated, or modified SCIFs or SAPFs and can coordinate facility, physical security, information security, and technical accreditation requirements.

  • Have successfully managed government customer relationships and can communicate clearly with security officials, technical teams, program leaders, and senior executives.

  • Have led security inspections, customer reviews, incident response, corrective actions, and closure of complex compliance findings.

  • Exercise strong judgment under pressure and can distinguish between requirements that can be addressed creatively and boundaries that cannot be crossed.

  • Enjoy building teams, improving operating models, clarifying ownership, and creating durable processes in fast-moving environments, and are eager to use approved AI tools, agents, and automations to reduce administrative burden, improve visibility, and scale sound judgment without replacing sponsor approvals, security authority, or required human review.
