You will also help define how we serve enterprise customers at scale by developing effective coverage models, reusable implementation patterns, technical enablement, escalation mechanisms, and systems for turning field insights into high-quality product feedback.

As Industrial Compute continues to expand globally, Site Operations plays a critical role in ensuring each campus is prepared to support reliable AI infrastructure at scale.

About the Role

We are seeking a Site Operations Technician to support the daily operation of Industrial Compute campuses. This role acts as OpenAI's on-site technical representative, helping coordinate activities across hardware operations, facilities, construction, logistics, security, and external service providers.

You will perform routine site inspections, support asset tracking, coordinate vendor activities, assist with operational readiness, document site conditions, and help ensure infrastructure issues are identified and resolved quickly.

title: Counsel, AI Safety & Cyber Incident Response
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Legal team helps address the cutting-edge legal questions that arise from developing and deploying advanced AI. The Security and Public Sector Legal team helps protect OpenAI’s technology, systems, data, and people and supports the safe and responsible use of our tools. We work closely with technical and operational teams to provide practical advice on novel, consequential, and fast-moving issues.

About the Role

We are seeking a counsel to help lead legal responses to cybersecurity and AI safety incidents. This is an opportunity to bring deep incident response expertise to some of the hardest questions in AI, and help build the legal frameworks and practices for answering them.

You will advise on complex cybersecurity incidents, from discovery through to resolution, and also help develop our response to incidents involving the safety of our models and tools. AI safety incident response is a new and rapidly evolving legal practice area. Your work will help define how frontier AI companies investigate and respond to safety events such as unexpected model behavior, degradation of safeguards, harmful uses of our services, and potential harm to third parties—often where established legal standards do not yet exist. Working directly with Security, Safety, Product, Engineering, and colleagues across Legal, you will advise on consequential decisions where established approaches may offer little guidance.

We are looking for a practical, dynamic lawyer who can turn incomplete information into clear recommendations, exercise sound judgment on novel questions, and follow matters through to resolution. You will help establish the facts, assess risks, and guide investigations, communications, remediation, and reporting. You will also turn lessons from individual incidents into durable response processes, helping further develop a legal function that evolves alongside the technology.

This role is based in Washington, D.C. or San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will be:

  • Serving as legal lead on assigned cybersecurity and AI safety incidents, coordinating fact development, legal analysis and advising, cross-functional escalation, and follow-through with the response team.

  • Working with investigators to understand incident scope, attack paths, root cause, and affected systems and data, and potential third-party impacts, while helping teams distinguish established facts from gaps in the evidence.

  • Managing outside counsel and third party service provider engagements necessary to incident response.

  • Serving as key Legal point of contact for cross-functional teams.

  • Partnering with Privacy, Product, Regulatory, and other counsel to assess notification and reporting obligations, advise on timely customer and user communications, and coordinate third-party outreach and incident-related information sharing with industry peers and government partners.

  • Preparing concise incident updates and decision materials that distinguish established facts, uncertainties, options, and recommended next steps.

  • Developing severity-based escalation criteria, response playbooks, exercises, and clear decision and handoff processes for cybersecurity and AI safety incidents, adapting established practices to emerging model risks.

  • Supporting post-incident reviews, tracking agreed corrective actions, and turning lessons into practical improvements to safeguards and response processes.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • A JD and a license or qualification to practice law in your jurisdiction.

  • 5+ years of relevant experience.

  • Relevant legal experience managing cybersecurity or privacy incident responses or comparable complex technology investigations at a technology company, law firm, or government agency, including work with technical teams, other counsel, and communications partners.

  • The ability to translate technical findings into practical legal advice, with a working understanding of technical information.

  • Sound judgment under time pressure, clear communication of uncertainty, and an understanding of when to act, seek specialist advice, or escalate.

  • Clear, concise writing and the ability to keep cross-functional teams aligned through changing facts and competing priorities.

  • Ownership of details and follow-through, paired with collaborative work with colleagues who bring different expertise.

  • A strong interest in the novel challenges of AI safety and a willingness to help develop new approaches. Direct AI incident experience is helpful; strong transferable incident response skills are welcome.

  • Availability to participate in time-sensitive incident response, including occasional work outside normal business hours.

title: Incident Commander, Detection & Response - APAC
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Security is at the foundation of OpenAI’s mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

The Security team protects OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We are technical in what we build but are operational in how we do our work, and are committed to supporting all products and research at OpenAI. Our Security team tenets include: prioritizing for impact, enabling researchers, preparing for future transformative technologies, and engaging a robust security culture.

About the Role

As an Incident Commander on Detection & Response, you’ll lead the response to complex security incidents affecting OpenAI’s intellectual property, customer data, and infrastructure. You’ll establish response priorities, coordinate technical work streams, drive containment and recovery decisions within agreed authority, and keep stakeholders informed as facts evolve. You’ll work with security and infrastructure teams across endpoints, identity, cloud, and compute environments, maintaining clear ownership and effective handoffs across time zones. Detection engineering knowledge is a supporting requirement: you’ll use telemetry and detection logic to assess evidence, identify visibility gaps, and guide improvements that make incident response more effective.

In this role, you will:

  • Run incident command from initial assessment through containment, recovery, and closure, establishing severity, scope, response objectives, and escalation needs.

  • Assign work stream owners and coordinate investigation, containment, and recovery in parallel. Maintain a decision log and distinguish confirmed facts from assumptions.

  • Drive timely containment and recovery decisions with the appropriate owners, weighing security risk, evidence preservation, and operational impact within agreed decision rights.

  • Communicate incident status, impact, uncertainty, actions underway, and the next update to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

  • Manage cross-time-zone handoffs with explicit command ownership, current status, outstanding risks, pending decisions, and next actions.

  • Improve response readiness through exercises, playbooks, and post-incident reviews; track agreed corrective actions with their owners.

  • Partner with detection engineers to evaluate telemetry and detection quality, close incident-related visibility gaps, and prioritize practical response automation.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have personally led complex security incidents as incident commander or an equivalent response lead, with clear examples of decisions, delegation, escalation, and outcomes.

  • Make sound decisions with incomplete information and revise them as evidence changes, balancing containment urgency with operational impact.

  • Coordinate responders across teams and time zones, resolve conflicting priorities, and maintain clear ownership during handoffs.

  • Communicate calmly and precisely under pressure, including concise stakeholder updates and explicit statements of uncertainty.

  • Have the security and infrastructure fundamentals to challenge investigation findings and assess containment and recovery options.

  • Understand detection engineering, including telemetry coverage, detection logic, false positives and false negatives, and validation. Can query and interpret evidence to support response decisions.

title: Full-Stack Software Engineer, Intelligence & Investigations
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Intelligence & Investigations team helps OpenAI understand and respond to the risks that can accompany increasingly capable AI. Our work has two central responsibilities: investigating potential high-severity misuse or harm involving our models, and monitoring and characterizing risks to OpenAI, our users, and the broader world. We bring together analysts, investigators, engineers, and other subject matter experts to turn complex signals into a clearer picture of what matters and support informed action.

About the Role

As an engineer on Intelligence & Investigations Engineering, you will build the systems that support both sides of this mission: giving OpenAI’s leadership superhuman situational awareness of important risks and developments, and accelerating expert investigators and analysts as they assess potential high-severity misuse or harm.

You will design, prototype, ship, and maintain end-to-end products that use OpenAI’s models and infrastructure to make sense of large, complex information environments. These systems will surface meaningful signals, synthesize important developments, and help people make well-informed decisions when the stakes are high.

You will work directly with analysts, investigators, and other subject matter experts to understand their needs and build products that make their work faster, more effective, and more scalable. Your engineering work will be central to how the team investigates potential misuse, develops situational awareness, and informs decisions.

We’re looking for engineers who combine strong technical and analytical skills with product judgment and the ability to move between rapid prototyping and reliable production systems. You should be comfortable working with ambiguous problems, complex data, and evolving AI capabilities—and excited to build tools that expand what human experts can understand and accomplish.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • 7+ years of experience as a software engineer

  • Build intelligence systems that monitor and characterize emerging risks, synthesize internal and external signals, and give OpenAI leadership a timely, decision-ready view of what matters

  • Develop investigative tools that help analysts, investigators, and subject matter experts assess potential high-severity misuse or harm with greater speed, depth, and consistency

  • Own technical solutions end to end, from identifying user needs and prototyping new capabilities to deploying, maintaining, and improving production systems

  • Apply OpenAI’s models to research and investigative workflows, including lead generation, triage, synthesis, and analysis across large, complex datasets

  • Design effective interfaces and workflows that help expert users explore evidence, follow leads, and make well-informed decisions

  • Shape the team’s technical and product direction as model capabilities, risk landscapes, and investigative needs evolve

  • Collaborate closely with analysts and investigators, as well as partners across Applied, Safety Systems, Research, User Operations, and Strategy

You might thrive in this role if you have / are:

  • 4+ years of experience as a software engineer

  • Experience designing, building, and operating production software, ideally for intelligence, investigations, security, research, or other complex analytical workflows.

title: Manufacturing Engineer, Motors & Actuators
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.

About the Role

We are seeking Manufacturing Engineers to lead the development of processes, tooling, and prototype builds for custom motors and actuators. You will own a primary area as a Stator Process / Manufacturing Engineer, Tooling / Fixture Engineer, or Prototype Manufacturing Engineer, taking that work from early development through validation and repeatable execution in close partnership with mechanical, electromagnetic, electrical, test, quality, and supplier teams.

These roles focus on the development, integration, and validation of electromechanical manufacturing capabilities, including stator winding processes, assembly and inspection tooling, and actuator prototype builds. You will help translate engineering designs into reliable hardware while establishing scalable processes, equipment, and build practices for future robotic platforms.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 5 days a week.

In this role, you will

Each opening focuses on one of the three specialties below, with shared responsibility for reliable processes and hardware.

  • Stator Process / Manufacturing: develop and validate stacking, winding, termination, and potting processes. Establish process parameters, work instructions, and defect controls that produce consistent results across trained operators.

  • Tooling / Fixture: design and deliver winding tools, assembly fixtures, inspection gauges, and bench equipment, from CAD and drawings through fabrication, commissioning, and troubleshooting. Improve setup time, labor, and repeatability.

  • Prototype Manufacturing: plan and execute builds of existing actuator designs, from parts readiness and work instructions through inspection, approved rework, and delivery of complete actuator assemblies ready for robot integration. Resolve supplier and process issues, track failed parts, and use labor and yield data to improve subsequent builds.

  • Integrate and troubleshoot equipment within your specialty, working through operator workflow, material flow, and controls or test interfaces.

  • Resolve defects and bottlenecks through measurements and controlled trials. Demonstrate improvements in build time, repeatability, yield, and quality against defined acceptance criteria.

  • Release clear process and tooling documentation, maintain revisions, and train technicians and operators to reproduce successful results.

  • Work with mechanical designers to improve manufacturability while preserving approved magnetic, electrical, and safety requirements. Own the tooling designs and drawings needed to build and inspect the hardware, and coordinate product geometry, tolerance, and drawing changes with the product-design owner.

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Have personally developed, built, or improved manufacturing processes, tooling, or electromechanical assemblies, and can explain the engineering decisions and results you owned.

  • Move comfortably between hands-on troubleshooting, technical analysis, and working with technicians, operators, and suppliers.

  • Use measurements and experiments to distinguish part variation, tooling problems, process settings, and operator effects.

  • Choose equipment and automation with sound judgment about production rate, flexibility, cost, safety, and maintainability.

  • Set practical build or development priorities, communicate blockers early, and work across design, controls, test, quality, and operations to resolve them.

Preferred qualifications

Relevant experience depends on the specialty:

  • Stator Process / Manufacturing: stacking, winding, termination, potting or cure processes, and winding or handling tooling.

  • Tooling / Fixture: fixture design, CAD and manufacturing drawings, metrology, equipment commissioning, and repeatability studies.

  • Prototype Manufacturing: electromechanical assembly, build planning, parts readiness, inspection, rework, testing, and delivery of complete hardware builds.

  • Motor, stator, actuator, or comparable electromechanical manufacturing experience.

  • Automated assembly, inline inspection, end-of-line testing, or equipment fault recovery; familiarity with sensors, PLCs, I/O, or pneumatics.

  • Process capability, measurement-system studies, and structured experiments.

  • Interest in using AI to simplify repetitive engineering work, with sound review of its outputs.

title: Software Engineer, AI for Chip Design
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI develops models that can reason through complex problems and hardware designed for the demands of advanced AI. AI for Chips connects these efforts: applying increasingly capable AI systems to the work of semiconductor engineering.

Our goal is to help engineers develop better chips and shorten design cycles. This work brings research, model training, and hardware expertise together to build tools that engineers can use on real designs, with correctness and measurable performance at the center.

 

About the Role

We’re hiring a Software Engineer to build the research infrastructure and tooling that help OpenAI models design silicon. You’ll turn chip-design workflows into reliable environments for reinforcement learning and evaluation, and make it easier for researchers to run experiments and iterate on new ideas.

You’ll move between software engineering, tool integration, and open research problems. We value strong coding fundamentals, clear technical judgment, and independent execution. Prior chip-design experience is helpful, but you can learn the domain alongside the team’s hardware specialists.

 

In this role, you will:

  • Build and maintain infrastructure for reinforcement learning environments, evaluations, and long-running experiments.

  • Integrate electronic design automation (EDA) tools into workflows for RTL generation, verification, and physical design optimization.

  • Improve experiment reliability, reproducibility, observability, and performance; debug failures across tools, services, and infrastructure.

  • Develop tooling and model harnesses that let researchers test ideas quickly and measure correctness and power, performance, and area (PPA).

  • Collaborate with researchers and engineers to turn successful experiments into reusable systems and training workflows.

  • Own ambiguous projects end to end, communicate progress, and use results to guide the next iteration.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have strong software engineering fundamentals, with experience designing, implementing, and debugging reliable systems.

  • Can work across a stack, investigate unfamiliar failures, and make practical tradeoffs between speed, correctness, and maintainability.

  • Have independently delivered substantial software projects and can explain your technical decisions and their impact.

  • Are comfortable working with researchers on evolving requirements and turning open-ended problems into working software.

  • Are interested in learning how reinforcement learning and chip-design tools fit together.

  • Care about developing safe, beneficial AI.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with research infrastructure, distributed systems, experiment orchestration, or ML tooling.

  • Familiarity with reinforcement learning, model evaluations, or training workflows.

  • Experience with Python, containerized tools, and reproducible development environments.

  • Experience with RTL, Verilog/SystemVerilog, EDA tools, formal verification, or chip-design automation.

title: Applied AI Architect, Digital Natives (Strategics)
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The AI Architect team partners with organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact. We work with customers across industries and digital-native businesses to identify where AI can create value, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption. The team brings together technical strategy, customer partnership, and practical deployment expertise, working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and specialist delivery teams.

 

About the Role

As an AI Architect, you will be the senior technical owner for a named portfolio of customers and the primary technical counterpart to their leadership teams. You will act as the “CTO of your book of business”, shaping each customer's AI strategy and guiding their journey from pre-sales discovery and solution evaluation through deployment, adoption, and measurable business impact.

You will own the technical account plan across ChatGPT Enterprise, the OpenAI API, Codex, and other agentic AI solutions. In partnership with the Account Director, you will translate business priorities into a focused use-case portfolio, an actionable adoption roadmap, and a clear path to durable customer value and growth. The Account Director owns commercial strategy; you own the technical strategy, customer journey, and path to production value.

You will remain accountable for the technical outcome while bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, enablement, security, product, and partners to provide deeper expertise and execute work where needed. This role calls for strong industry fluency, sound architectural judgment, and the ability to move confidently between executive strategy and hands-on technical conversations.

 

In this role, you will:

  • Serve as the primary technical advisor and long-term technical relationship owner for a named portfolio of existing customers and pre-sales prospects.

  • Partner with Account Directors on account strategy while owning the technical account plan, technical milestones, adoption priorities, and expansion opportunities.

  • Lead discovery with executives and technical teams to identify, qualify, and prioritize use cases tied to meaningful business outcomes.

  • Develop clear Applied AI Architectures spanning models, applications, data, integration, security, privacy, governance, evaluation, and deployment.

  • Guide customers through technical evaluations, demonstrations, workshops, prototypes, and proofs of value, securing confidence in both the solution and its path to production.

  • Maintain a focused use-case portfolio with clear decision criteria, ownership, blockers, success measures, delivery needs, and adoption plans.

  • Develop trusted relationships and technical champions across CTOs, CIOs, CISOs, AI leaders, engineering teams, and other customer stakeholders.

  • Qualify and coordinate support from Deployment Engineering, implementation, training and enablement, product and domain specialists, partners, and other delivery teams.

  • Remain accountable for technical progress and customer outcomes while ensuring delivery teams own implementation execution once engaged.

  • Track adoption, usage, account health, production readiness, and measurable customer impact, intervening early when risks threaten value realization.

  • Apply industry or digital-native expertise to recognize repeatable patterns, sharpen customer priorities, and identify relevant expansion opportunities.

  • Share customer insights with Product, Engineering, and Research, translating field learnings into better products, architecture guidance, and reusable practices.

 

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have significant experience in customer-facing technical roles such as solutions architecture, solutions engineering, technical account leadership, AI deployment, or technical customer success.

  • Have guided enterprise organizations from technical evaluation through production adoption and measurable business impact.

  • Build credibility with senior technical and business leaders while communicating equally well with hands-on engineers.

  • Bring strong software and cloud architecture foundations, including APIs, distributed systems, data integration, identity, security, and privacy.

  • Understand modern AI systems, frontier LLM models, agentic applications, model evaluation, retrieval, or enterprise AI workflows.

  • Can prototype, explain technical tradeoffs, and work confidently with APIs, SDKs, and languages such as Python or JavaScript.

  • Exercise sound judgment about when to go deep personally, when to involve specialists, and how to define clear handoffs and ownership.

  • Have experience developing technical account plans, prioritizing complex customer portfolios, and connecting adoption to measurable outcomes.

  • Bring meaningful expertise in a relevant industry or strong fluency with the needs of digital-native businesses.

  • Communicate clearly and can turn ambiguity into a practical technical narrative, executive decision, or action plan.

title: US Congressional Lead
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We believe that achieving our goal requires effective engagement with public policy stakeholders and the broader community impacted by AI. Accordingly, our Global Affairs team builds authentic, collaborative relationships with public officials and the broader AI policymaking community to inform and support our shared work in these domains. We ensure that insights from policymakers inform our work and - in collaboration with our colleagues and external stakeholders - seek to further regulation, industry standards, and safe and beneficial development of AI tools.

About the Role

As a US Congressional Lead on the Global Affairs team, you will help develop strategies and advance OpenAI’s engagement with the U.S. Congress across a range of legislative and policy priorities. You will develop and manage relationships with House and Senate lawmakers and staff, with particular attention to committees shaping technology and emerging policy issues. You will support OpenAI’s U.S. Global Affairs team in meetings, briefings, hearings, and other engagements, and collaborate with civil society and industry partners in alignment with OpenAI’s mission.

OpenAI releases industry-leading research and tools. You will face new challenges as the impact of cutting edge generative AI technologies continues to be explored and as the needs of the organization evolve. Day-to-day work may encompass tracking emerging congressional policy issues, coordinating complex cross-functional engagement with legal, policy, and communications teams, developing briefing materials, preparing our leaders for congressional hearings and other government engagements, and representing OpenAI in private and public forums.

We are looking for a self-directed and creative individual with substantial Capitol Hill experience, strong congressional relationships, experience managing private sector and civil society relationships, and an understanding of AI-related legislative and regulatory issues and processes.

This role is based in Washington, DC and may require frequent travel to participate in meetings and events with key stakeholders.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Are well versed in the issues around emerging AI technologies, particularly as they relate to congressional policymaking.

  • Are an enthusiastic and effective coalition builder who thrives as a member of a high performing, peer-led global team.

  • Are highly organized, and are used to working as an accountable individual contributor as well as a team player.

  • Are passionate about the promise of technology and the future of artificial intelligence but thoughtful about its potential risks.

We're looking for a blend of:

  • Demonstrated experience (8+ years) and credibility working with the U.S. federal government, particularly the legislative branch.

  • Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of the U.S. government, its institutions and legislative processes, and the key policy issues and debates related to AI.

  • The ideal candidate will have substantial experience working with Congress, with a strong preference for experience working with the House or Senate Judiciary Committees, the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, or other relevant congressional committees. The candidate should bring strong bipartisan relationships, sound political judgment, and demonstrated experience navigating complex legislative and policy issues.

  • Track record of effectively working with cross-functional teams, especially communications, policy and legal teams, and aligning a diverse range of internal and external partners

  • Sound judgment and outstanding personal integrity

  • Ability to execute in fast and flexible environments through rapid cycles of analysis, decision, and action

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Product & Platform teams at OpenAI are responsible for delivering the company’s most impactful offerings—such as ChatGPT, our API platform, and new enterprise capabilities—to a global and diverse customer base. These systems must perform at scale and deliver exceptional experiences to developers, consumers, and businesses alike.

The ChatGPT infrastructure team is responsible for ensuring that our products can serve rapidly growing demand with the performance, reliability, and quality our users expect.

This work sits at the intersection of product demand, model deployment, inference, research, fleet, and capacity. The team translates changing product and model needs into clear capacity decisions and safe, scalable launches.

 

About the Role

We are seeking a Technical Program Manager to lead the operating system for Chat capacity and model deployment. You will connect demand forecasting and capacity allocation with model readiness, rollout planning, launch coordination, and post-deployment learning. You will also own mode deployment beyond capacity by working with cross functional teams across research, post-training, inference and product to own mainline model deployment.

You will bring structure to constrained-capacity decisions, improve the tooling and mechanisms teams use to prioritize demand, and help new models reach users safely and efficiently. Success requires technical depth, sound judgment under ambiguity, and crisp execution across product, research, infrastructure, and operations teams.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 

In this role, you will:

  • Own cross-functional programs for Chat capacity forecasting, allocation, headroom planning, and constrained-capacity operations.

  • Build durable intake, prioritization, and decision mechanisms that connect product demand and model requirements to available serving capacity.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

We’re looking for a product manufacturing & quality engineer, who will be responsible for driving technical initiatives related to the manufacturing, quality and reliability of our AI supercomputer hardware systems to ensure product success from concept to launch and through mass production. You’ll have the opportunity to coordinate with functional SMEs and work with a wide range of stakeholders, from design engineering and operations teams, TPMs, external industry vendors and partners to ensure that all products are developed and delivered on time and to the highest quality standards.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees

In this role, you will:

  • Own the integrated manufacturing and quality readiness for a product across L6, L10, and L11, with clear gates, milestones, deliverables, owners, and closure criteria.

  • Lead readiness of process flows, tooling, fixtures, assembly operations, test interfaces, and production controls. Review and contribute to work instructions.

  • Translate product requirements into qualification plans, process controls, test requirements and acceptance criteria with design engineering and Area SMEs

  • Coordinate and drive execution of product and process qualification, reliability testing, and validation with the relevant SMEs. Maintain traceable evidence that assigned products and processes meet agreed performance, reliability, and compliance requirements.

  • Own the supplier and line scorecard. Using yield, defect tracking, process capability, and reliability data to assess process health, identify trends and escapes, prioritize improvements, and verify their effectiveness.

  • Lead containment, failure analysis, root cause investigation, and corrective actions for issues affecting the program during development, production, and deployment. Drive actions to closure with evidence that fixes are effective and sustained.

  • Work on-site with Area SMEs at supplier and sub-supplier locations to assess line readiness and process execution, troubleshoot issues, and verify that agreed controls and corrective actions are implemented.

  • Lead JDM/CM manufacturing and quality audits and performance reviews for the program, and drive readiness, process, and control gaps to closure.

  • Assess the manufacturing and quality impact of design, process, source, and site changes. Coordinate validation and control updates with the responsible engineering and sourcing owners.

  • Provide evidence-based release recommendations using readiness gate status, qualification and control evidence, containment status, and remaining risks and actions. Make any unmet criteria clear to the responsible approval owners.

  • Manage multiple projects, track progress against milestones, communicate priorities and risks across functions, and coordinate risk mitigation to meet schedules and quality standards.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a track record of owning both manufacturing and quality outcomes for complex hardware from new product introduction through production ramp and sustaining operations.

  • Are hands-on, detail-oriented, and comfortable taking deep ownership of an assigned product, source, or site while coordinating specialists across disciplines.

  • Understand high-performance computing hardware and the manufacturing and quality risks that carry across component, system, and rack integration, including L6, L10, and L11.

  • Partner closely with design engineering and subject matter experts to assess changes, define validation needs, and integrate technical decisions while respecting design and commercial ownership.

  • Have experience building integrated readiness plans, managing qualification gates and dependencies, and using technical evidence to make clear release recommendations.

  • Have significant experience working with multinational JDM/CM partners on manufacturing readiness, process controls, yield improvement, quality, reliability, and issue closure.

  • Are familiar with mechanical and electrical Design for Quality (DFQ), Excellence (DFX), Manufacturability (DFM), Assembly (DFA), Test (DFT), and Reliability (DFR), and can apply them with the relevant specialists.

  • Have experience leading structured problem solving and root cause analysis using methods such as 8D, 5 Whys, and fishbone analysis, including validation of corrective-action effectiveness.

  • Use statistical methods and manufacturing and quality data to understand yield, defects, process capability, and reliability, and communicate findings through clear supplier and line scorecards.

  • Have experience qualifying processes or sources, evaluating technical equivalency, and managing risks across suppliers, sites, and product or process interfaces.

  • Are comfortable with ambiguity and changing conditions, and can make clear decisions, document risks, and escalate issues while maintaining ownership through closure.

title: Data Center Infrastructure Architect
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Industrial Compute team is building and productizing infrastructure capabilities that help organizations deploy and operate advanced AI systems at scale. The team works across AI hardware, systems engineering, physical infrastructure, and customer delivery to turn emerging technologies into reliable, repeatable infrastructure solutions.

Our work sits at the intersection of technical strategy, product development, engineering, and deployment. We partner closely with customers and internal engineering teams to solve complex infrastructure challenges spanning compute, power, cooling, controls, and facility efficiency.

About the Role

We are seeking a senior, hands-on Data Center Infrastructure Architect to develop and optimize the physical infrastructure required for large-scale AI deployments.

This is a broad technical role spanning data center architecture, electrical and mechanical systems, high-density compute, controls, telemetry, and digital modeling. You will use simulation, operational data, and digital-twin approaches to evaluate infrastructure designs, identify system-level constraints, and improve efficiency, reliability, cost, and speed of deployment.

The ideal candidate can move fluidly between first-principles analysis, facility and equipment design, computational modeling, engineering review, and real-world implementation. You should be comfortable working across disciplines rather than operating solely within electrical, mechanical, or software boundaries.

Key Responsibilities

  • Define system-level architectures for high-density AI data centers across power, cooling, IT equipment, controls, and facility infrastructure.

  • Develop digital twins and other computational models that represent the behavior of data center systems under changing workloads, environmental conditions, equipment configurations, and failure scenarios.

  • Use design and operational data to identify constraints, improve PUE and related efficiency metrics, and optimize capacity, reliability, water consumption, cost, and deployment schedules.

  • Evaluate tradeoffs across electrical topology, cooling architecture, rack density, redundancy, controls, maintainability, constructability, and operational complexity.

  • Translate evolving AI hardware requirements into practical facility, rack, power, and thermal architectures.

  • Establish reference architectures, modeling standards, design assumptions, performance requirements, and validation methodologies that can be reused across customer deployments.

  • Partner with software, data, controls, hardware, mechanical, electrical, construction, commissioning, and operations teams to connect digital models with real infrastructure behavior.

  • Integrate telemetry from systems such as BMS, EPMS, DCIM, SCADA, equipment controllers, and IT hardware into modeling and optimization workflows.

  • Lead technical reviews of customer and partner designs, identify material risks, and recommend changes grounded in quantitative analysis.

  • Work with customers and delivery teams to adapt reference solutions to site-specific constraints while preserving performance, reliability, and efficiency objectives.

  • Support pilots, commissioning, performance testing, and post-deployment analysis to validate models and continuously improve infrastructure designs.

  • Help shape the technical roadmap for Industrial Compute’s physical-infrastructure products and engineering services.

Qualifications

  • Significant experience designing or optimizing hyperscale data centers, large mission-critical facilities, or comparable infrastructure systems.

  • Broad knowledge of data center electrical and mechanical systems, including power distribution, backup power, thermal management, liquid cooling, heat rejection, controls, and monitoring.

  • Experience making system-level design decisions across multiple engineering disciplines.

  • Experience developing or applying simulation, optimization, digital-twin, or physics-based modeling techniques to physical infrastructure.

  • Strong understanding of data center efficiency and performance metrics, including PUE, WUE, utilization, capacity, reliability, and total cost of ownership.

  • Experience working with operational telemetry and translating real-world system behavior into design improvements.

  • Ability to evaluate complex tradeoffs involving performance, reliability, cost, schedule, scalability, sustainability, and maintainability.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead technical work in ambiguous, rapidly changing environments.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex engineering decisions to customers, executives, and cross-functional teams.

  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, systems engineering, applied physics, or a related technical discipline.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience with high-density GPU clusters and direct-to-chip liquid cooling.

  • Experience connecting facility models with workload, rack, server, or chip-level power and thermal behavior.

  • Familiarity with modeling or engineering tools such as Modelica, MATLAB/Simulink, Python, EnergyPlus, computational fluid dynamics tools, or equivalent platforms.

  • Experience with BMS, EPMS, DCIM, SCADA, PLCs, data historians, or industrial controls.

  • Experience developing reference designs or new infrastructure architectures within a hyperscaler, data center operator, advanced engineering organization, or major design consultancy.

  • Experience taking an infrastructure concept from modeling and prototype validation through deployment and operational feedback.

  • Advanced degree in an engineering or scientific discipline.

Success in the First Year

  • Establish a credible system-level model of power, cooling, compute, and facility behavior for priority Industrial Compute use cases.

  • Identify and validate meaningful opportunities to improve efficiency, capacity, reliability, or deployment cost.

  • Deliver reusable reference architectures and engineering methodologies for customer deployments.

  • Create a repeatable feedback loop connecting modeling, operational telemetry, commissioning results, and future design decisions.

  • Become a trusted technical partner to internal engineering teams, customers, and infrastructure delivery partners.

title: Product Growth
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Growth team drives user and revenue growth across ChatGPT’s consumer and business segments worldwide. We work across the full funnel, from acquisition and activation to retention and monetization, through product experiments, in-product improvements, performance marketing, creative development, and AI-powered workflows.

The International Growth team works with regional leaders in priority markets to identify the user needs and product gaps that matter most for adoption, usage, and monetization. We turn country priorities into product roadmaps and growth plans, then partner with engineering, research, design, data science, marketing, finance, policy, and partnerships to test and ship improvements.

We combine product strategy, product experimentation, with hands-on growth operations. We account for local behavior, competition, and product experience while building shared capabilities such as segmentation, lifecycle journeys, and experimentation systems. We measure what ships, adapt it to the market, and scale approaches that work across markets.

About the Role

We’re looking for a hands-on Product Growth generalist with an international focus to help people get lasting value from ChatGPT across markets, use cases and product experiences. You’ll partner with international and central teams to understand user needs, identify growth opportunities and turn them into measurable improvements across acquisition, activation, engagement, retention and monetization.

You’ll combine strong analytics and experimentation with product intuition, design judgment and a deep understanding of users and local markets. You’ll use AI-native automation and agentic tools to accelerate research, analysis, prototyping and execution. This role requires systems thinking and the ability to move across diverse experiences, improving both individual funnels and end-to-end workflows as products, user behavior and market needs evolve.

You’ll be responsible for:

  • Partner with product, eng, and design to turn insights into intuitive experiences and prototypes, improving how users discover value, complete tasks and return.

  • Diagnose and optimize funnel performance using user research, event-level behavior, cohort analysis, and competitive insight. Identify drop-offs and high-value segments, distinguish local needs from shared product friction, and prioritize interventions.

  • Build and use agentic workflows to automate research, analysis, prototyping and experiment operations, with clear quality checks and human judgment where needed.

  • Connect acquisition and marketing insights to product journeys; partner with regional marketers and channel specialists on tests that improve qualified acquisition and activation.

  • Own a rigorous experimentation program across onboarding, activation, repeat usage, re-engagement, paid conversion, and expansion. Partner with Engineering and Data Science on hypotheses, instrumentation, A/B tests and holdouts, readouts, and staged rollouts, with clear success metrics and guardrails.

  • Build and execute a focused international growth roadmap, including in-product upsell, cross-sell, targeting, onboarding, activation/adoption, expansion, and monetization related experiences. title: Researcher, Frontier Cybersecurity Risks
descriptionHtml:
About the team

Models are becoming increasingly capable—moving from tools that assist humans to agents that can plan, execute, and adapt in the real world. Mitigating the frontier risks resulting from these capabilities is paramount to OpenAI’s ability to continue deploying models safely.

The Preparedness team is dedicated to addressing these critical risks. Our work includes:

  1. Measurement. Monitoring and predicting the evolving capabilities of frontier AI systems.

  2. Mitigation. Keeping misuse and misalignment safeguards, alignment tools, and security measures on track to adequately address extreme threats that might arise in the future.

  3. Coordination. Setting mitigation targets by maintaining OpenAI’s preparedness framework, and partnering with other staff to achieve these targets.

This is urgent, fast-paced work that has far-reaching implications for the company and for society.

About the role

As we push toward AGI, cybersecurity becomes one of the most important and urgent frontiers: the same systems that can accelerate productivity can also accelerate exploitation.

As a Researcher for cybersecurity risks, you will help design and implement an end-to-end mitigation stack to reduce severe cyber misuse across OpenAI’s products. This role requires strong technical depth and close cross-functional collaboration to ensure safeguards are enforceable, scalable, and effective. You’ll contribute directly to building protections that remain robust as products, model capabilities, and attacker behaviors evolve.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and implement mitigation components for model-enabled cybersecurity misuse—spanning prevention, monitoring, detection, and enforcement—under the guidance of senior technical and risk leadership.

  • Integrate safeguards across product surfaces in partnership with product and engineering teams, helping ensure protections are consistent, low-latency, and scale with usage and new model capabilities.

  • Evaluate technical trade-offs within the cybersecurity risk domain (coverage, latency, model utility, and user privacy) and propose pragmatic, testable solutions.

  • Collaborate closely with risk and threat modeling partners to align mitigation design with anticipated attacker behaviors and high-impact misuse scenarios.

  • Execute rigorous testing and red-teaming workflows, helping stress-test the mitigation stack against evolving threats (e.g., novel exploits, tool-use chains, automated attack workflows) and across different product surfaces—then iterate based on findings.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a passion for AI safety and are motivated to make cutting-edge AI models safer for real-world use.

  • Bring demonstrated experience in deep learning and transformer models.

  • Are proficient with frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.

  • Possess a strong foundation in data structures, algorithms, and software engineering principles.

  • Are familiar with methods for training and fine-tuning large language models, including distillation, supervised fine-tuning, and policy optimization.

  • Excel at working collaboratively with cross-functional teams across research, security, policy, product, and engineering.

  • Have significant experience designing and deploying technical safeguards for abuse prevention, detection, and enforcement at scale.

title: ML Silicon Performance Lead
descriptionHtml:
About the Team:

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role:

We’re looking for an ML Silicon Performance Lead to drive hardware/software co-design for our silicon architecture. You will work across models, kernels, compilers, and silicon to shape how ML workloads map to hardware—and how the hardware should evolve to support them. Your work will connect model and workload requirements with compute, memory, and specialized acceleration capabilities to maximize performance, efficiency, and scalability across current and future generations of AI silicon.

You’ll partner closely with ML research, compiler, and silicon architecture teams to jointly develop software approaches and hardware capabilities. From kernel mapping and quantization to new data structures and specialized IP, you’ll evaluate hardware and software tradeoffs to improve performance, efficiency, and utilization across large-scale AI workloads. Through performance modeling, simulation, and hands-on optimization, you’ll guide architectural decisions and validate improvements on representative workloads.

In this role, you will:

  • Drive hardware/software co-design across ML research, compiler, and silicon teams, jointly shaping kernel implementations and hardware capabilities to meet workload performance and efficiency goals.

  • Partner with ML research to translate model and workload needs into kernel performance targets and compute, memory capacity, and bandwidth requirements, feeding hardware constraints and opportunities back into model and algorithm choices.

  • Map and optimize ML kernels for architecture, using insights from data movement, memory hierarchy, and execution efficiency to guide both software improvements and hardware design.

  • Co-design support for new data structures and quantization formats across kernels, compilers, and silicon, balancing model quality, numerical behavior, performance, power, and implementation cost.

  • Define and help develop specialized acceleration IP, working with compiler and silicon partners to determine the right division of functionality across software, instructions, and dedicated hardware.

  • Drive ML performance modeling and simulation with the compiler team to compare hardware/software design options, expose bottlenecks, and quantify end-to-end benefits on representative workloads.

  • Partner with the Silicon Architecture lead and silicon team to specify and validate new IP, using kernel and simulation results to refine requirements and prioritize architectural improvements.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have deep experience with ML accelerator architecture and how compute resources, memory systems, and data movement shape workload performance.

  • Can translate model-level behavior into concrete kernel requirements and hardware design decisions.

  • Have built or used accelerator performance models and simulators, and know how to validate their assumptions and interpret their limitations.

  • Have hands-on experience optimizing ML kernels, including identifying bottlenecks and improving utilization, locality, and execution efficiency.

  • Understand quantization and numerical formats, including their implications for model quality, memory bandwidth, compute efficiency, and hardware support.

  • Have experience with hardware/software co-design and can reason about whether a capability belongs in a kernel, compiler, instruction set, or dedicated hardware.

  • Work effectively across research, compiler, and silicon teams, bringing clarity to ambiguous requirements and building alignment through technical evidence.

title: Product Content Creator
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The B2B Content team helps business audiences understand what AI makes possible and how to put it to work. We develop narrative, editorial, demo, and adoption programs that connect OpenAI’s products to concrete business value.

We partner closely with Product Marketing, Demand Generation, Customer Education, Sales, and other teams to create content that is useful on its own and supports the broader customer journey.

We value people who are eager to learn, have a bias for action, and look beyond the immediate deliverable. We build the tools, systems, and shared practices that help the whole team produce better work over time.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Product Content Creator to help create the next generation of AI-native marketing content. You’ll develop videos, interactive tutorials, live demos, written guides, and other experiences that help business audiences understand what AI makes possible and how it applies to their work.

This is a hands-on creative role spanning demand generation and product adoption. You’ll explore product capabilities, build and test workflows, and produce content for campaigns that introduce people to useful ideas and help them put those ideas into practice. You’ll maintain evergreen campaign content and develop new adoption campaigns, using practical workflows, research, and thought leadership as source material.

You’ll use Codex and other AI tools to prototype ideas and create experiences that would previously have required a larger production team. We’re looking for the fluency of a coding-assistant power user; an engineering background isn’t required. Strong judgment about the idea, the audience, and the finished experience matters as much as the ability to build it.

You’ll partner with Product Marketing on positioning and product accuracy, Demand Generation on campaign goals and distribution needs, and Demo Studio on demonstrations and production. You’ll own the content from concept through delivery, choosing the format that best serves the idea and the audience. This is an individual-contributor role for someone who enjoys making, explaining, experimenting, and shipping.

The role is hybrid and will be based in San Francisco, Monday through Wednesday. Thursday and Friday are work-from-home days, with occasional in-office attendance as needed for live webinars.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop creative concepts and produce content for Demand Generation campaigns, grounded in audience needs, product workflows, research, and expert perspectives.

  • Personally create videos, interactive tutorials, live demos, and written guides, carrying work from the initial idea through a finished asset.

  • Use Codex and other AI tools to build and test workflows, prototype interactive experiences, and improve how content is produced.

  • Develop and test original content formats, learn from audience response, and turn the strongest ideas into recurring series or reusable campaign experiences. Choose formats for what they help the audience understand or do.

  • Develop webinar content with the webinar strategist, including the storyline, presentation, demonstration, and useful follow-up resources.

  • Work with Product Marketing, subject-matter experts, and Demo Studio to make content accurate, substantive, and engaging.

  • Work with customer-facing teams to learn how people actually use the products, where they get stuck, and which workflows are worth demonstrating. Use those insights to develop relevant stories and adoption content.

  • Adapt strong ideas across formats and audiences while giving each asset a clear purpose within the campaign.

  • Deliver usable campaign assets to Demand Generation, with clear audience framing, supporting copy, and a proposed next action.

  • Use audience feedback and campaign results with DG to improve the content, and keep reusable workflows, examples, and source material current.

  • Maintain evergreen campaign content, updating workflows, demonstrations, and supporting resources as products and audience needs change.

  • Create adoption campaign content that helps people try relevant workflows, overcome common difficulties, and continue using them in their work.

  • Review campaign results and audience feedback with partners to understand both what attracts interest and what helps people successfully use the product.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a portfolio of substantive content you personally created across several formats, such as video, interactive tutorials, live demos, and written guides. Work projects, side projects, and experiments driven by your own curiosity are all relevant—we want to understand what you made and the decisions behind it.

  • Are a confident user of Codex or comparable coding assistants and can show how you used them to build, test, and improve something useful. An engineering background isn’t required.

  • Bring strong creative and editorial judgment: you can recognize an interesting idea, explain why a format works, and improve an experience beyond the first version.

  • Can learn a product deeply enough to demonstrate real workflows and explain them clearly to business audiences with different levels of technical fluency.

  • Write clearly, communicate well on video or in live demonstrations, and can turn complex material into something people want to spend time with.

title: Data Center Controls Network Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI is building the infrastructure foundation for the next generation of AI. The Data Center Engineering team defines the strategy, reference architectures, technical requirements, and delivery standards for the large-scale data centers that support OpenAI research, products, and infrastructure partners.

As a Data Center Controls Network Engineer, you will design, validate, and scale the controls and OT network architectures that support high-density AI data centers. You will work across controls systems, OT infrastructure, telemetry, commissioning, deployment, and operations, partnering with mechanical, electrical, IT/networking, security, and external delivery teams.

About the Role

We are seeking a mid to senior OT Network Engineer with a strong controls systems background to lead the design and operation of resilient, secure, and scalable OT network architectures for high-density AI data centers. This role translates compute, power, cooling, and operational requirements into practical OT network designs, evaluates vendor solutions, and drives technical decisions across controls infrastructure, telemetry, commissioning, and operations.

The ideal candidate has strong hands-on experience in mission-critical OT environments, including industrial networking, virtualized infrastructure, and OT network operations, with expertise in routing, switching, segmentation, firewall policy, time synchronization, monitoring, and network lifecycle support.

Key Responsibilities

  • Define controls, automation, and OT network requirements for AI data center campuses.

  • Develop reference architectures, engineering standards, and reusable design templates.

  • Review and develop basis-of-design and functional design documents, including OT network diagrams, IP/VLAN schemes, telemetry architectures, data flow diagrams, and commissioning requirements.

  • Design OT and infrastructure network architectures, including physical topology, logical topology, IP addressing, subnetting, VLANs, routing, switching, redundancy, segmentation, firewall policy coordination, out-of-band management, monitoring, and remote access patterns.

  • Develop day-two network operations requirements, including change management, configuration backups, golden configurations, monitoring thresholds, firmware lifecycle, rollback plans, and post-change validation.

  • Partner with electrical, mechanical, IT/networking, security, and operations teams to ensure OT network systems align with GPU deployments, campus-wide telemetry, and failure-domain isolation requirements.

  • Define integration patterns and protocol requirements across BACnet/IP, BACnet MSTP, Modbus TCP/RTU, OPC UA, IEC-61850 MMS/GOOSE, MQTT, SNMP, syslog, NTP/PTP, IRIG-B, and vendor-specific interfaces.

  • Lead technical evaluation of controls integrators, network equipment suppliers, design consultants, contractors, and commissioning agents

  • Review network equipment submittals, configurations, firmware assumptions, certifications, test reports, and quality documentation.

  • Support factory witnessed testing (FWT), site acceptance testing, network readiness checks, failover testing, and integrated systems testing.

  • Troubleshoot complex controls network issues including packet loss, latency, duplicate IPs, routing errors, firewall drops, protocol incompatibilities, time synchronization drift, and intermittent device communication failures.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of relevant experience in controls engineering, industrial automation, OT networking, mission-critical facilities, or similar critical infrastructure environments.

  • Strong expertise in resilient OT network architecture, implementation, troubleshooting, and lifecycle support.

  • Experience with OT/IT boundary design, secure enterprise integration, firewall policy design, redundant topologies, out-of-band management, and monitoring.

  • Hands-on experience with Layer 3 OT network design, including IP addressing, subnetting, routing, VRFs, ACLs, inter-VLAN traffic control, and network segmentation.

  • Hands-on experience with Layer 2 security and switching controls, including MACsec, port security, loop prevention, and switch-level access control.

  • Hands-on experience in designing resilient OT network topologies using industrial redundancy protocols and architectures such as PRP, HSR, Cisco REP, RSTP/MSTP, and ring or star topologies.

  • Hands-on experience in designing resilient infrastructure network architectures using HSRP/VRRP, spine-leaf topologies, redundant uplinks, and failure-domain isolation.

  • Hands-on experience with industrial and infrastructure network equipment such as Cisco switches/routers, Juniper switches/routers, Palo Alto firewalls, Rockwell Automation Stratix switches, Siemens Ruggedcom or comparable industrial networking platforms.

  • Experience with network management and observability platforms such as Cisco Catalyst Center (DNA Center), Palo Alto Panorama, Juniper Mist, industrial NMS tools, packet brokers, and OT monitoring platforms.

  • Hands-on experience with industrial Ethernet, VPN tunneling, IPsec-based connectivity, and secure remote access.

  • Hands-on experience with virtualized OT or controls server environments such as VMware vSAN, Microsoft Azure Stack HCI / Hyper-V, or comparable infrastructure platforms.

  • Experience with industrial communication and OT infrastructure protocols, including BACnet/IP, BACnet MSTP, Modbus TCP/RTU, OPC UA, IEC-61850 MMS/GOOSE, MQTT, SNMP, syslog, NTP/PTP, IRIG-B, and vendor-specific interfaces, and strong understanding of their behavior across OT network architectures.

  • Experience reviewing and producing technical design documentation, commissioning plans, and acceptance test procedures.

  • Experience with factory witnessed testing, site acceptance testing, failover testing, telemetry validation, protocol compatibility testing, and root-cause analysis.

  • Ability to use logs, packet captures, and field observations to make sound technical decisions and communicate risk clearly.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Network Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related discipline.

Preferred Skills

  • Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Network Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related discipline.

  • Experience leading multi-campus OT network integration, commissioning, and operations across cross-functional teams, contractors, vendors, and delivery partners.

  • Relevant networking certifications such as Cisco CCNA/CCNP, Palo Alto PCNSA/PCNSE, Juniper JNCIA/JNCIS, or similar networking credentials.

  • Cybersecurity certifications such as CISSP, GICSP, ISA/IEC 62443, CompTIA Security+, or similar cybersecurity credentials are a plus.

  • Experience with network automation, Git-based configuration management, and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) using tools such as Ansible, Terraform, Python, or similar to support scalable OT network deployment and lifecycle management.

  • Experience with scripting, APIs, and automation workflows that improve OT network operations.

  • Experience using AI agents or MCP-connected tools to support telemetry analysis,and troubleshooting.

  • Experience with relational database systems such as PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MySQL, or similar platforms used for OT telemetry, historian integrations, troubleshooting, and reporting.

Work Environment and Travel

  • This role requires periodic travel to data center campuses, vendors, labs, construction sites, commissioning activities, and controls/network cutovers.

  • The engineer should be comfortable working across office, lab, construction, and live data center environments, including PPE, lockout/tagout, cyber hygiene, and change-control requirements.

  • Work may include time-sensitive support during commissioning, startup, vendor testing, cutovers, network changes, telemetry issues, automation failures, and operational events.

title: Software Engineer - Data Aquisition (systems)
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

This team builds and operates the systems that enable OpenAI researchers to run reliable, scalable, and efficient research workflows. The team sits close to research and works across infrastructure, systems, and automation to make sure researchers have the tools and environments they need to move quickly.

The work spans software engineering, infrastructure, systems administration, cluster operations, and reliability engineering. As OpenAI’s infrastructure evolves from bespoke bare-metal systems toward more standard, scalable platforms, the team needs engineers who can understand how systems work end-to-end and build the right abstractions without reinventing the wheel.

 

About the Role

As a Software Engineer on this team, you will build and operate the infrastructure that supports frontier research and critical research-facing systems. You will work on systems that sit close to the metal, but the role is not limited to classic operations or sysadmin work. We are looking for someone who can reason about networking, bootstrapping, Kubernetes, scalability, automation, and reliability - while also writing software to make these systems better over time.

This role is a strong fit for an independent, high-ownership engineer who enjoys reliability-heavy infrastructure work but still wants to build. You do not need to come in as a kernel expert or highly algorithmic optimization engineer, but you should be deeply curious about infrastructure, comfortable debugging complex systems, and excited to support researchers doing novel work.

 

We expect you to:

  • Build and operate reliable infrastructure for research workloads and research-facing services.

  • Support and improve systems across data infrastructure, processing, crawl and ingest, caching, search, observability, and clusterwide services.

  • Improve cluster bootstrapping, provisioning, automation, and deployment workflows.

  • Debug issues across networking, compute, storage, orchestration, and service reliability layers.

  • Build software and automation that reduce manual operational work and improve system reliability.

  • Partner closely with researchers, infrastructure engineers, and service owners to understand system needs and translate them into durable solutions.

  • Help evolve existing infrastructure toward more scalable, maintainable, and standard patterns.

  • Take ownership of critical systems and drive work independently from problem definition through execution.

 

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have strong systems fundamentals and understand how infrastructure scales in practice.

  • Are comfortable with Linux, networking, Kubernetes, provisioning, and distributed systems operations.

  • Can write software to automate, debug, and improve infrastructure systems.

  • Have a strong execution mindset and can independently drive ambiguous infrastructure work.

  • Enjoy supporting a wide surface area of systems, from research tooling to platform services.

  • Are pragmatic about when to build custom systems versus using existing, well-supported tools.

  • Care about building reliable systems that make researchers faster and reduce operational friction.

 

Nice to have:

  • Experience with PXE boot, cluster provisioning, bare-metal infrastructure, or large-scale fleet management.

  • Experience operating Kubernetes or similar orchestration systems at scale.

  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD, observability, or deployment automation.

title: Field Service Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI's infrastructure teams design, build, activate, and operate the critical systems that support large-scale AI compute. Field Service Engineering partners across design, construction, commissioning, site operations, hardware operations, and equipment providers to turn complex infrastructure into safe, reliable, and serviceable systems.

About the Role

We are seeking a senior, field service engineer to build the technical operating model responsible for critical electrical and mechanical infrastructure across our data center portfolio. This is a field-oriented electrical & mechanical engineering role, not a traditional facilities operations position. You will combine deep systems understanding in data center power and cooling systems to aid in SOO, design, maintenance & operability, troubleshooting and other engineering related responsibility around key equipment. The role will include leveraging training and experience to establish standards, develop people, coordinate vendors, and drive issues from design, first principles, first signals through verified resolution. The strongest candidates will have deep expertise in either electrical and mechanical systems and strong working fluency across the other discipline (e.g. controls, business acumen).

Remote - travel 50%

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead field support for startup, commissioning, troubleshooting, repair, and reliability improvement across critical data center infrastructure.

  • Serve as the senior technical owner for transformers, switchgear, UPS systems, generators, PDUs, protection and controls, chillers, cooling towers, pumps, CDUs, CRAH units, and associated control systems.

  • Diagnose complex failures across power, cooling, controls, and hardware interfaces; distinguish symptoms from root causes and drive corrective actions through validation.

  • Build the field service operating model, including staffing recommendations, coverage, escalation paths, response expectations, spare-parts strategy, documentation, and performance metrics.

  • Aid in hiring, development, and coaching other field service engineers and technicians while creating a culture of safety, technical rigor, accountability, and continuous learning.

  • Partner with design, construction, commissioning, site operations, and hardware teams to improve maintainability, readiness, and lifecycle reliability.

  • Manage OEM and service-provider relationships, technical escalations, repair plans, warranties, and sustained corrective action.

  • Establish and improve safe work practices, including lockout/tagout, switching and maintenance procedures, MOPs, SOPs, EOPs, and incident response.

  • Translate field learning into design feedback, preventive maintenance improvements, training, and reusable standards.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of hands-on experience supporting critical electrical, mechanical, or electromechanical infrastructure in data centers, industrial facilities, utilities, manufacturing, or similarly complex environments.

  • Deep technical expertise in at least one discipline, electrical or mechanical, with demonstrated ability to troubleshoot across electromechanical and controls boundaries.

  • Experience building, leading, or materially developing a field engineering, service, maintenance, or technician team.

  • Demonstrated success leading high-severity troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and reliability improvement.

  • Ability to read and use one-line diagrams, schematics, P&IDs, sequence-of-operations documents, control diagrams, equipment manuals, and commissioning records.

  • Strong safety judgment and experience working under formal energization, isolation, maintenance, and change-control procedures.

  • Clear written and verbal communication with engineers, technicians, vendors, construction teams, and senior stakeholders.

  • Ability to travel up to 50% and support planned or urgent field activity when required.

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience with hyperscale data centers, high-density compute infrastructure, or other mission-critical environments.

  • Experience bringing new sites from construction and commissioning into steady-state operations.

  • Working knowledge of BMS, EPMS, SCADA, PLC, or other infrastructure monitoring and controls platforms.

  • Experience establishing service programs, readiness criteria, technical training, or fleet-wide reliability standards.

  • Relevant electrical, mechanical, HVAC, controls, safety, or trade certifications.
