title: Software Engineer, Full-Stack - Core Experimentation
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Statsig team within OpenAI builds the experimentation, feature rollout, dynamic configuration, and analytics systems that help OpenAI ship products with speed, safety, and evidence. Our work sits on the critical path for how product, engineering, research, and go-to-market teams learn from real-world usage and make high-confidence decisions.

Statsig began as an independent company focused on helping builders move faster through trustworthy experimentation and feature management. After Statsig joined OpenAI, the team began the next chapter: bringing that deep product expertise, customer intuition, and mature platform infrastructure into OpenAI as the experimentation and rollout platform for every product we ship.

Today, we support teams across ChatGPT, Codex, model measurement, consumer experiences including ads, business subscriptions, developer products, and the shared infrastructure that connects them. These teams rely on Statsig to safely introduce new capabilities, compare product and model behavior, measure impact, and roll changes forward or back with confidence.

We are at a defining moment in the platform journey. OpenAI has the data, product surface area, and pace of innovation to learn faster than almost any organization in the world, but that potential only becomes real if teams can experiment responsibly, measure clearly, and roll out changes safely. Adoption of the platform is accelerating rapidly across the company, and recent SDK and server-side infrastructure work has already produced measurable wins in latency, reliability, memory usage, and compute efficiency for important services.

Based out of OpenAI’s Bellevue office, we are a close-knit team that values in-person collaboration, urgency, craft, and impact. We build for other builders, and the best version of this team is one where every OpenAI product team can move faster because the experimentation and rollout layer is dependable, fast, and easy to use.

About the Role

We are looking for a full-stack engineer to help build the systems that make experimentation and rollout a first-class capability across OpenAI. You will work across frontend, backend, SDK, data, and infrastructure surfaces, with a focus on making complex workflows feel simple for the teams shipping OpenAI’s most important products.

This role is not only about adding features to a platform. It is about shaping the operating system OpenAI uses to decide what to launch, how to learn from it, and how to protect users and products as we scale. OpenAI’s next phase depends on our ability to move quickly without losing rigor, and Statsig is one of the places where that balance becomes real.

You will collaborate closely with teams building ChatGPT, Codex, model measurement workflows, consumer monetization and ads, business subscription experiences, developer products, and shared infrastructure. You will translate their launch and measurement needs into platform capabilities that can support the full company, not just one-off use cases.

  • Build product experiences and platform capabilities for experimentation, feature flags, dynamic configuration, rollout safety, and analytics.

  • Partner with product teams to understand launch workflows, measurement needs, and decision points, then turn those insights into durable platform features.

  • Improve SDK and server-side systems so experimentation and configuration are fast, reliable, and safe for high-scale OpenAI services.

  • Help teams across ChatGPT, Codex, model measurement, ads, business subscriptions, developer products, and infrastructure use Statsig effectively.

  • Design workflows that make it easier to create experiments, interpret results, monitor rollouts, and act quickly when a launch needs adjustment.

  • Work from the Bellevue office with a team that values ownership, clear communication, and high-trust collaboration.

You Might Thrive In This Role If You

  • Have strong full-stack engineering judgment and enjoy building product surfaces that sit on top of serious platform and infrastructure constraints.

  • Care deeply about developer experience and can make powerful experimentation concepts feel intuitive to busy product teams.

  • Like working on systems where performance, reliability, and product quality all matter at the same time.

title: Product Designer, Engineering Acceleration
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Engineering Acceleration team builds products that multiply the effectiveness of OpenAI’s technical teams, helping engineers, researchers, and product teams understand complex systems, learn from what they ship, and operate reliably at scale.

As AI changes how software is built, we have an opportunity to rethink engineering workflows from first principles. We’re creating tools and shared systems that turn complex data, experimentation, and technical workflows into clear decisions and useful action.

About the Role

In this role, you’ll lead design across two connected product areas: a real-time data exploration and observability experience for investigating large-scale system and product behavior, and an experimentation platform for safely launching changes, measuring their impact, and deciding whether to ramp, iterate, or roll back.

This is more than a dashboard-design role. You’ll define the interaction models that take someone from a vague question or unexpected signal to a trustworthy answer and clear next step. You’ll work closely with engineers, researchers, data scientists, and product teams to understand the mechanics of their work and make dense technical systems coherent without flattening the details that matter.

You’ll also help establish greater consistency across OpenAI’s enterprise and internal tools, developing durable patterns that support AI-native workflows and enable other designers to build more effectively.

title: Applied Risk Standards Architect
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We believe that achieving our goal requires effective engagement with public policy stakeholders and the broader community impacted by AI. Accordingly, our Global Affairs team builds authentic, collaborative relationships with public officials and the broader AI policymaking community to inform and support our shared work in these domains. We ensure that insights from policymakers inform our work and – in collaboration with our colleagues and external stakeholders – seek to shape policy so that it aligns with and supports our mission.

About the role

OpenAI is looking for an Applied Risk Standards Architect to lead standards work for applied risk in applications, including mental health, youth safety, age assurance, functional efficacy, reliability, and privacy-related risks. You will help turn internal research, safety policies, and evaluation methods into technically sound, measurable, and adaptable standards that build public trust and support responsible deployment.

This role sits within our AI standards and global assurance function in Global Affairs. Working closely with Safety Systems, Research, Product, Model Policy, Legal, and third-party evaluators, you will author proposals, negotiate requirements, and represent OpenAI in priority standards bodies. You will take on the drafting and external engagement needed to advance this work, enabling technical experts to focus on the underlying methods and evidence. You will also bring emerging requirements back into internal planning before they become established expectations.

Alongside this primary portfolio, you will support the AI Standards and Global Assurance Lead on frontier AI assurance, contributing to risk-management standards, evaluation and benchmarking requirements, and approaches to independent assessment.

The role connects technical practice with external standards. It does not replace the teams responsible for evaluation methods, safety decisions, controls, internal compliance, or implementation. You will own standards drafting, review coordination, negotiation, and assessment-design contributions within an agreed mandate.

In this role, you will

  • Lead the development of applied AI risk standards. This includes working with technical and policy teams to define and advance standards for mental health, youth safety, age assurance, efficacy, reliability, and privacy-related risks, with a particular focus on evaluations and assessments.

  • Work with technical owners to turn research, internal policies, and evaluation methods into credible test methods, assessment criteria, and standards grounded in real system behavior.

  • Bring emerging requirements into internal planning and work with responsible teams to clarify their implications for evaluations, controls, and assurance for our products.

  • Work with technical and GRC partners on assessor competence, independence, conflicts of interest, evidence access, reporting, and the distinction between management-system audits and technical evaluations.

  • Contribute drafting, representation, and coordination on frontier risk-management and independent-assessment standards.

  • Lead assigned standards-body workstreams, negotiate proposals, and coordinate internal input, reducing the external engagement burden on technical experts. Contribute to relevant ISO/IEC, INCITS, NIST consortium, and cross-industry work.

  • Maintain clear approvals, negotiating positions, contribution records, and implementation handoffs so that external commitments remain connected to technical owners and available capacity.

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Have technical depth in evaluation science, AI evaluations and red teaming, AI safety, or trust and safety, combined with demonstrated ability to translate that expertise into credible standards or assessment methods.

  • Have authored or materially shaped standards, evaluation criteria, control frameworks, or normative technical contributions—not only coordinated participation.

  • Can translate a broad safety objective into a clear requirement and explain what evidence would demonstrate that it has been met.

  • Understand the differences among organizational risk-management processes, model and system evaluations, mitigation testing, and broader assurance claims.

  • Can evaluate sensitive, context-dependent outcomes, including uncertainty and variation across users and use cases, without overstating what a benchmark or assessment can establish. You do not need to be an expert in every risk domain.

  • Understand how assessor competence, independence, incentives, and access affect the credibility of an assessment.

  • Can build consensus without sacrificing technical rigor, and know when to compromise, challenge a proposal, or escalate a decision.

  • Earn trust with technical teams while communicating clearly with lawyers, executives, policymakers, and external standards participants.

title: Systems Generalist, GPT Infrastructure
descriptionHtml:
About OpenAI

OpenAI is dedicated to ensuring that artificial general intelligence (AGI) benefits all of humanity. Our mission requires building not only world-class AI models, but also the infrastructure that enables those models to be deployed reliably, efficiently, and at global scale. As demand for AI continues to grow, we are expanding the ways OpenAI can bring high-performance inference capacity online across a diverse hardware ecosystem.

About the Team

The GPT Infrastructure team builds software that turns advanced inference and optimization research into production products. One focus is enabling strategic infrastructure partners and accelerator vendors to qualify and onboard new compute without a bespoke porting and optimization effort for every hardware platform.

We build the control planes, APIs, secure partner-side execution environments, evaluation systems, artifact pipelines, and operational tooling that make these workflows repeatable and trustworthy. The work sits at the intersection of distributed systems, AI inference, compilers and runtimes, performance engineering, security, and external partnerships.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced systems generalist who can work comfortably across the stack to help build an automated inference optimization platform. Given a workload, target hardware profile, compiler and runtime context, and a trusted verifier, the system runs durable optimization campaigns that generate, compile, execute, grade, and improve candidate kernels, runtime configurations, and serving-stack changes.

You will design both the OpenAI-hosted control plane and the partner-side software that evaluates candidates on real accelerator hardware. The product must keep long-running workflows reliable, make performance results reproducible, and maintain clear trust boundaries around sensitive model and hardware information.

This is a deeply cross-stack role, combining strong software engineering fundamentals with systems thinking and performance intuition. You will work closely with research, inference engineering, infrastructure, security, product, and strategic partners to turn a powerful research workflow into a scalable product.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and operate durable APIs and control-plane services for multi-hour or multi-day optimization campaigns, including scheduling, retries, budgets, checkpoints, artifact lineage, and observability.

  • Build secure partner-side runner and grader software that can compile, execute, verify, and benchmark candidate artifacts on third-party accelerator hardware.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Consulting team is part of OpenAI’s Enterprise Verticals organization. Our goal is to help consulting teams do better work for their clients. We work side by side with design partners to understand how their teams operate, then use what we learn to build for consultants everywhere.

Today, we’re bringing OpenAI’s models and products together to accelerate the core work of consulting, from investigating a client’s question to delivering advice they can act on. We’re starting by removing the barriers that keep consultants from using AI in their day-to-day work. We’ll draw on the full range of OpenAI’s capabilities, from ChatGPT Work to newer tools such as Dots and Spaces.

Longer term, we want to help firms develop AI-native ways of working. A team could design an engagement around questions it can now afford to explore, test several strategies with its client, and change course as it learns what works. We’re moving quickly, working across OpenAI’s research, product, and engineering teams to turn what we learn with design partners into products consultants everywhere can use.

About the Role

We’re looking for a full-stack software engineer to build first-party OpenAI products for consulting. You’ll own features end to end, from the frontend interfaces consultants use to the backend services and integrations that power them.

You’ll work closely with our consulting design partners and with colleagues across product, design, research, and engineering at OpenAI. Together, you’ll turn what you learn from individual engagement teams into products we can distribute broadly. Success will ultimately be defined by adoption and the value generated for consulting firms.

In this role, you will:

title: Agent Standards Architect, Global Affairs
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We believe that achieving our goal requires effective engagement with public policy stakeholders and the broader community impacted by AI. Accordingly, our Global Affairs team builds authentic, collaborative relationships with public officials and the broader AI policymaking community to inform and support our shared work in these domains. We ensure that insights from policymakers inform our work and – in collaboration with our colleagues and external stakeholders – seek to shape policy so that it aligns with and supports our mission.

About the Role

As AI agents move from answering questions to taking action across the internet, the standards that govern identity, delegated authority, discovery, communications, agentic-commerce and payment interfaces, agent-facing web access, agent-specific provenance, and auditability will determine whether agents can operate safely, interoperably, and with clear accountability. OpenAI is looking for an Agent Standards Architect to lead execution of our external technical standards strategy for a defined set of agent standards workstreams.

This role will work closely with Agent Security, Applied and Platform teams, Product, Legal, GRC, Global Affairs, and GTM to turn OpenAI’s technical architecture and controls into credible specifications, protocol profiles, assurance criteria, and implementation guidance—and to bring emerging external requirements back into product and security roadmaps before they become blockers. The positions developed here are technical standards positions, not broad public-policy positions.

This is a builder’s role as much as an external-facing role. You will execute a prioritized standards plan, author and negotiate protocols, build coalitions, secure the right internal approvals, and represent OpenAI in assigned technical forums. You will also help create repeatable processes that let the company shape agent standards without depending on a single person or relying on technical teams to carry external standards work on top of their core jobs.

The Agent Standards Architect is an integrator, not the owner of every underlying technical system. Security, Product, Engineering, and other designated technical teams retain ownership of architecture, threat models, controls, product decisions, approvals, and implementation. This role owns workstream planning, standards translation, drafting, negotiation, external representation within approved mandates, commitment traceability, and implementation handoff.

In this role, you will:

  • Own a focused workstream plan for core agent identity, discovery, and delegated-authorization standards, with adjacent agentic-commerce, web-access, provenance, and auditability work assigned through portfolio prioritization.

  • Recommend where OpenAI should lead, shape, monitor, oppose, or decline to participate within the assigned workstream, based on technical maturity, governance quality, strategic leverage, implementation readiness, and company priorities.

  • Develop technical standards positions and normative contributions that preserve distinctions among the human or service principal, agent, workload or runtime, task, session, resource, and policy decision.

  • Shape requirements for scoped delegation, attenuation, step-up approval, revocation, credential custody, runtime binding, discovery, interoperability, agent-specific provenance, and auditable action trails.

  • Embed with Agent Security and Applied or Platform teams to translate internal architecture and controls into technically credible specifications, profiles, white papers, and assurance evidence without overstating maturity or deployment status.

  • Lead review and approval paths across Product, Security, Engineering, Legal, GRC, Global Affairs, and GTM; maintain clear mandates, red lines, owners, dependencies, and external commitments.

  • Represent OpenAI in priority venues and coalitions, such as IETF and OAuth-related work, FIDO, OIDF, W3C, AAIF, and relevant NIST or ISO efforts; build trust with peer companies, standards operators, and public-sector stakeholders.

  • Bring external standards intelligence back into product, security, compliance, and go-to-market decisions early enough to shape roadmaps and avoid retrofit, launch, procurement, or market-access friction.

  • Contribute reusable playbooks, decision records, contribution patterns, and handoffs that reduce key-person risk across the assigned workstream.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have strong experience in technical standards, internet protocols, identity and access, security architecture, applied cryptography, or closely related product or infrastructure work.

  • Have authored, edited, or materially shaped normative specifications, profiles, drafts, or conformance requirements in serious technical standards or open-source governance settings.

  • Can reason clearly about OAuth and OIDC, FIDO or WebAuth, workload identity, HTTP signatures, delegated authority, credential lifecycle, revocation, provenance, and auditability; you do not need to be expert in every layer.

  • Understand that agent trust is a composed stack rather than a single credential, and can separate principal, agent, runtime, task, session, resource, and policy claims.

  • Can distinguish adopted standards, stable extensions, active drafts, working-group proposals, and exploratory ideas—and know how that maturity should change OpenAI’s posture.

  • Earn trust with engineers and security leaders while also communicating crisply with lawyers, product leaders, executives, policymakers, and external standards participants.

  • Have strong judgment in ambiguous, high-stakes environments and know when to lead, compromise, oppose, escalate, or walk away.

  • Write clearly, negotiate constructively, and are comfortable representing OpenAI externally with discretion.

About the Team

About the Role

As a Data Scientist for Financial Engineering, you will drive the measurement, experimentation, and optimization work that powers OpenAI’s monetization infrastructure.

You will define how we measure and improve checkout, payments, subscriptions, and pricing systems globally—balancing conversion, risk, cost, reliability, and user experience. As a senior individual contributor, you will establish source-of-truth metrics, design rigorous experiments, develop analytical frameworks, and translate complex findings into decisions that directly affect revenue and international growth.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid model of three days per week in the office and offer relocation support.

In this role, you will

  • Define key metrics and guardrails across checkout, payments, subscriptions, and pricing.

  • Design experiments, staged rollouts, and offline incrementality studies.

  • Improve conversion, payment performance, retention, and involuntary churn.

  • Develop pricing, elasticity, FX, and localization frameworks.

  • Partner with Data Engineering to build trusted datasets and operational monitoring.

  • Turn complex analysis into recommendations that shape product and business decisions.

  • Provide technical leadership and mentor other data scientists.

You might thrive in this role if you have

descriptionHtml:

OpenAI’s mission is to build safe artificial general intelligence (AGI) which benefits all of humanity. This long-term undertaking brings the world’s best scientists, engineers, and business professionals into one lab together to accomplish this.

The team is made of Sales, Solutions, Support, Marketing, and Partnership professionals that work together to create valuable solutions that will help bring AI to as many users as possible.

OpenAI is seeking a highly motivated and experienced VC Partnerships Manager to join our Startups Go To Market team. You will play a critical role in managing relationships with top venture capital funds and startup accelerators, with the goal of providing exceptional support to the portfolio companies of these funds.

We believe that many of the most disruptive and category-defining AI applications will be created by startups. The Startup Go To Market team’s mission is to help startups harness the power of AI models to drive these advances. This role is a mixture of technical understanding, vision, partnership, and strategy. About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that AGI benefits all of humanity. Our Internal Communications team helps employees stay informed, connected, and engaged so they can focus on building and deploying safe and impactful AI. We partner across the company to explain what’s being built, why it matters, and how it connects to our strategy and mission.

About the Role

We’re looking for an internal communications professional to help employees understand the work happening across OpenAI’s research and product organizations. You’ll translate technical developments, product milestones, and team priorities into clear, useful communications that connect people to the work and to one another.

Reporting to the Internal Communications lead for Research and Product, you’ll be the second member of the team dedicated to this part of OpenAI. You’ll independently own specific communications programs and projects within the broader strategy, build trusted relationships with technical teams, and identify stories and information employees need to hear. You’ll also help build practical processes that allow a small team to support a broad and fast-moving organization.

This role requires strong writing and editing skills, technical curiosity, and sound judgment. You should enjoy asking questions, making sense of complex information, and moving work forward independently, with guidance from your manager on broader strategy and sensitive issues.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Own recurring communications programs that help employees understand research and product priorities, progress, and upcoming milestones.

  • Lead communications for defined projects and initiatives, developing plans, gathering input, drafting content, coordinating reviews, and managing delivery.

  • Translate complex technical and research concepts into accurate, accessible stories for employees with different levels of technical knowledge.

  • Build trusted relationships with researchers, product managers, engineers, and cross-functional partners to stay close to their work, identify important developments, and surface communication needs.

  • Partner with your manager on major announcements and organizational changes, owning defined workstreams and flagging sensitive issues, dependencies, and decisions that need leadership input.

You might thrive in this role if you:

title: Editor, Research Team
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

About the Role

As Editor, Research, you will help define the editorial voice of OpenAI’s research films. You will personally edit films that introduce new models, demonstrate emerging capabilities, and tell the stories behind our research. You will lead the editorial approach across assigned projects, guide collaborators, and set a high standard for cinematic storytelling and craft.

Your influence will begin well before footage reaches the edit. Working alongside researchers, filmmakers, and production, design, and product partners, you will shape concepts, develop narratives, test ideas through prototypes, and help plan shoots and demonstrations with the finished film in mind. You will bring clarity, humanity, and emotional depth to complex, evolving subjects, finding compelling ways to show the research while preserving its meaning and technical accuracy.

This is a hands-on leadership role for an exceptional editor who makes the work—and the people around them—better. You will take responsibility for editorial execution from concept through delivery, provide clear creative direction and actionable feedback, mentor editors, and lead external collaborators. You will also strengthen shared workflows and practices that help the studio deliver ambitious work across formats, platforms, markets, and timelines.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead editorial work from concept through final delivery, personally editing research launch films, cinematic demonstrations, and stories about the people behind the work while directing the contributions of other editors on assigned projects. Take responsibility for narrative quality and continuity across development, production support, editing, finishing, and delivery.

  • Set editorial direction across assigned projects, translating creative goals into a clear approach and helping internal editors and external partners deliver cohesive, distinctive work. Bring exceptional judgment to story, structure, pacing, performance, music, sound, and the relationship between picture and graphics.

  • Shape stories from the beginning, partnering with filmmakers and researchers on concepts, treatments, scripts, interview questions, and demonstration coverage. Use rough cuts, story assemblies, and rapid prototypes to find the strongest narrative and inform what needs to be captured.

  • Lead editorial reviews, presenting work and explaining creative choices clearly. Synthesize feedback from researchers and creative partners into focused revisions that strengthen the film while preserving the accuracy of demonstrations and technical explanations.

  • Lead editors and editorial collaborators on assigned projects, setting clear expectations, delegating work, supporting onboarding, and providing actionable creative feedback. Mentor editors and assistant editors to strengthen their storytelling, technical skills, and independent judgment.

  • Partner with production to scope and deliver editorial work, assessing resource needs, estimating effort, setting realistic schedules, and recommending the right talent for each assignment. Brief and creatively lead external editorial partners, surface risks early, and help resolve competing priorities.

  • Guide work through finishing, collaborating with motion designers, sound designers, composers, colorists, and VFX artists to preserve the creative intent through final delivery.

  • Strengthen editorial workflows and uphold shared standards, including project setup, technical specifications, media organization, version control, review processes, secure asset handling, handoffs, archival, and delivery quality. Identify improvements through project experience and share effective practices with the team.

  • Own the editorial approach to adaptations of assigned work, guiding cutdowns, platform variations, and localized versions. Review work for narrative clarity, cultural context, and consistency of meaning, tone, and emotional impact.

  • Evaluate new tools and approaches, including AI-enabled creative tools, that expand the studio’s ability to explore, edit, and deliver work. Share findings and partner with editorial leadership on testing and adoption.

  • Collaborate closely with researchers to translate complex capabilities into compelling stories, developing a working understanding of what a model can do and what a demonstration actually shows. Find inventive ways to make those capabilities clear on screen, and work with researchers to ensure edits preserve the context and meaning of the underlying work.

  • Partner with editorial and post-production leadership to build and maintain a world-class team, helping identify exceptional talent, mentor collaborators, and create a culture of creative excellence, collaboration, and shared craft.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 8+ years of relevant editing experience and a portfolio demonstrating exceptional cinematic storytelling, with work that shows your ability to make complex ideas compelling and accessible. Experience with research, science, technology, documentary, or demonstration-driven films is especially relevant.

  • Have experience leading editorial projects and guiding other editors or external partners, with clear examples of how your direction improved the work.

  • Combine strong narrative instincts with precise execution, and can build a compelling film from varied material, including interviews, demonstrations, live-action footage, and model-generated content.

  • Remain deeply engaged in the craft of editing while comfortably taking responsibility for the quality and progress of work beyond your own timeline.

  • Can articulate why an edit works, give specific and constructive feedback, and help others find solutions while encouraging their creative ownership.

  • Bring advanced proficiency in professional editing software and a strong understanding of post-production, including media workflows, motion graphics, sound, color, VFX, finishing, localization, versioning, archival, and delivery.

  • Have experience delegating work, onboarding collaborators, and coordinating editorial contributions across a project.

  • Build trust with researchers and creative partners, ask thoughtful questions to understand unfamiliar technical ideas, and translate feedback into clear editorial decisions under deadline pressure.

  • Know how to balance creative ambition with schedules and resources, and introduce enough structure to help teams do their best work.

  • Are curious about AI research and emerging creative technologies, and excited to explore how cinematic storytelling can reveal new capabilities and the people behind them.

title: Dedicated Support Engineer - Singapore
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s User Operations team shepherds our customers’ adoption of AI and ensures that our customers' product experience is nothing short of exceptional. We are building the very first post-AGI support team. We resolve complex issues, provide technical guidance, and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our products. We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others, to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. OpenAI's customers represent a range of diverse backgrounds and maturity, from early-stage startups to established global enterprises.

About the Role

The Support Engineering team works closely with Engineering, Product, Technical Success, Go-to-Market, and other teams to deliver an exceptional experience for our most strategic customers. We combine deep technical troubleshooting with durable customer context, proactive reliability work, and clear ownership during critical moments. We use automation, agents, and our own technology to help build the future of technical support.

We’re looking for experienced, deeply curious technical problem-solvers to serve as trusted support partners for our Premium Support customers. You’ll work directly with customers on novel, ambiguous, and high-impact technical issues, using logs, telemetry, reproduction, and systems-level investigation to isolate causes and drive issues toward resolution.

Beyond resolving individual issues, you’ll use your deep understanding of OpenAI’s infrastructure and products, together with each customer’s architecture and operating context, to anticipate risk and make their workloads more resilient over time. You’ll proactively monitor integrations, identify emerging failure patterns and architectural breakpoints, and work with customers and internal teams to address them before they become incidents. Success means that as a customer’s workloads mature and scale, the day-to-day effort required to support them decreases through better monitoring, runbooks, automation, and preventative improvements.

This role is based in Singapore. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. To succeed in this position you must be fully fluent in English (spoken and written). Please note that your resume must be submitted in English, and the interview process will be conducted in English.

In this role, you will:

  • Work directly with Premium Support customers to troubleshoot their most complex technical issues, including API failures, integration challenges, authentication errors, unexpected product behavior, performance degradation, and production incidents.

  • Provide end-to-end technical ownership by analyzing logs and system behavior, reproducing errors, testing hypotheses, and isolating the likely failure domain. Where possible, you’ll identify the root cause before escalating to Engineering; where that is not possible, you’ll provide a clear hypothesis and the evidence needed to accelerate Engineering’s investigation.

  • Become a trusted expert on OpenAI’s products and systems, serving as a critical escalation point and a technical backstop for our most strategic customers.

  • Own the customer-specific response to high-impact incidents. You’ll assess severity and business impact, initiate the appropriate response path, coordinate cross-functional responders, maintain clear ownership, and ensure issues move through mitigation, resolution, and post-incident follow-through.

  • Communicate clearly and proactively during periods of uncertainty, providing accurate updates to customer technical teams, business stakeholders, executives, and internal partners.

  • Develop a detailed understanding of each customer’s architecture, integrations, dependencies, critical workloads, and operational constraints. You’ll document this context and make it accessible to Support, Product, and Engineering teams.

  • Partner with Go-to-Market and Technical Success teams to understand the business importance of customer workloads and ensure that relevant commercial context informs severity, prioritization, and communication without bypassing established support processes.

  • Represent Support Engineering in relevant customer meetings, including QBRs, and partner closely with account teams to communicate technical health, surface risks and blockers early, coordinate follow-up, and provide customers and internal stakeholders with clear, proactive updates.

  • Monitor customer integrations and support trends to identify emerging risks, recurring failure patterns, and readiness gaps before they become major escalations.

  • Prepare for important launches, migrations, traffic increases, and business events by developing account-specific runbooks, validating escalation paths, coordinating support readiness, and providing heightened monitoring where needed.

  • Lead or contribute to incident reviews and postmortems, identify opportunities to prevent recurrence, and track corrective actions through closure.

  • Translate recurring customer pain into clear, evidence-backed feedback for Product and Engineering, with a particular focus on improving the reliability and performance of existing products, integrations, and deployments.

  • Turn what you learn from customer investigations into scalable improvements, including troubleshooting guides, monitoring, internal tooling, support workflows, and AI-powered automation.

  • Help shape the operating model, technical standards, and tooling for Premium Support as the function grows globally.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have significant experience in Support Engineering, Solutions Engineering, Solutions Architecture, or another role involving hands-on diagnosis of complex production issues.

  • Have expert-level troubleshooting skills and a strong track record of resolving ambiguous technical problems across APIs, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise integrations.

  • Are comfortable working with logs, metrics, traces, API requests, authentication flows, and customer-provided code or configurations to understand system behavior and test hypotheses.

  • Have experience leading or playing a central role in customer-impacting incidents, including severity assessment, technical coordination, stakeholder communication, root-cause analysis, and post-incident follow-through.

  • Can write code or scripts to reproduce issues, interrogate systems, automate repetitive work, and improve internal tools. Experience with Python, JavaScript, or similar languages is valuable.

  • Can communicate complex technical issues clearly to engineers, customer technical teams, business stakeholders, and senior leaders—especially when information is incomplete or evolving.

  • Build strong, high-trust relationships with customers and cross-functional partners while maintaining clear and scalable ownership boundaries.

  • Look beyond the immediate issue to identify patterns, improve the system, and prevent the same problem from recurring.

  • Thrive in ambiguity, update quickly as new information emerges, and are willing to learn whatever is needed to get the job done.

  • Bring a humble, team-first mindset, strong judgment, and a genuine eagerness to help both customers and colleagues succeed.

  • Are excited to use OpenAI’s products, agents, and emerging AI capabilities to transform how technical support operates at scale.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Across industries, OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering (AIE) team helps organizations turn frontier AI into safe, reliable production systems that deliver meaningful business outcomes. We turn lessons from these deployments into better OpenAI products and reusable patterns that help customers move faster.

As an Enterprise AIE, you will serve as a technical partner to leading organizations including universities and other educational institutions, helping them turn ambitious AI use cases into durable production systems and adoption at scale. You will combine deep technical judgment with hands-on engineering to provide technical leadership on complex customer deployments. You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions about model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by durable production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful business impact. Your deployment experience will also directly influence how OpenAI’s products evolve.

title: Host Systems Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About the Team
OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role
We’re looking for an experienced systems software engineer to help define and build the host software stack for our custom next-generation AI systems. You will work close to the hardware on performance-critical software, including Linux kernel drivers, high-throughput I/O paths, and system-scale networking and RDMA.

This role spans architecture, implementation, platform bring-up, debugging, and performance optimization. You will work across hardware and software boundaries to make new systems usable end to end, from low-level device interfaces through userspace tooling and production validation.

In this role you will:

  • Design, implement, and debug host-side systems software for AI infrastructure, including Linux kernel drivers and supporting userspace components.

  • Build and optimize software paths for high-throughput, low-latency communication, including RDMA and related networking functionality.

  • Develop software around PCIe, DMA, NICs, accelerators, memory movement, and device interaction.

  • Bring up new hardware platforms and diagnose complex issues across kernel, firmware, networking, and hardware boundaries.

  • Build tooling for integration, testing, diagnostics, observability, qualification, and performance characterization.

  • Collaborate with hardware, networking, and platform teams to define interfaces and integrate new capabilities.

  • Work with external vendors where needed to integrate technologies and drive issues to resolution.

  • Contribute across the systems software stack as the platform and team evolve.

  • Help shape the technical direction and engineering practices for a growing systems software stack.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Experience building low-level or performance-critical systems software.

  • Strong programming skills in C or C++, with proficiency using Python and Linux tooling for automation and debugging.

  • Strong Linux systems fundamentals and the ability to debug across hardware and software boundaries.

  • Hands-on experience in at least one relevant area, such as Linux kernel drivers, kernel networking, RDMA, PCIe, DMA, NIC software, accelerator software, or high-performance I/O.

  • Experience owning complex software projects from design through implementation, bring-up, and validation.

  • Ability to thrive in ambiguity, work across subsystem boundaries, and build systems from scratch.

  • Strong cross-functional communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience developing Linux kernel drivers or other OS-level performance-critical components.

  • Familiarity with RDMA or RoCE, ibverbs, kernel networking, or congestion-control concepts such as ECN and DCQCN.

  • Experience with PCIe, DMA, peer-to-peer communication, SR-IOV, IOMMU, dma-buf, or related accelerator and I/O subsystems.

  • Experience bringing up accelerators, NICs, SoCs, or custom hardware platforms.

  • Experience profiling and optimizing high-throughput, low-latency systems.

title: Mechanical Engineer, PCBA Test Infrastructure, Robotics
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.


About the Role

We are seeking a Mechanical Engineer for a senior individual-contributor role leading printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) test fixtures and infrastructure for advanced robotic systems. You will independently turn evolving requirements into working fixtures, make technical tradeoffs, and own delivery from concept and detailed design through fabrication, validation, deployment, and reliable operation.

This role combines development-lab work with deployment at contract manufacturers. You will build precision mechanical systems for board programming, functional test, and characterization, including board nests, probe plates, connector interfaces, alignment features, clamps, enclosures, and thermal interfaces. You will partner with electrical, firmware, software, manufacturing, and reliability teams to make fixtures repeatable, protective of delicate assemblies, and maintainable as board designs evolve.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 4 days a week. Travel to contract-manufacturer sites is part of the role, with timing based on build and deployment needs.


In this role, you will:

  • Own the mechanical architecture of PCBA test stations, including frames, board nests, datum schemes, access, guarding, ergonomics, and serviceability.

  • Design probe and bed-of-nails fixtures, connector-mating mechanisms, board supports, clamps, and interchangeable tooling for programming, functional test, and characterization.

  • Use first-principles analysis and simulation to assess stiffness, probe and insertion forces, board deflection, tolerance stacks, thermal growth, and fixture life; validate key predictions on hardware.

  • Develop locating and compliance features that accommodate board and assembly variation, protect components and solder joints, and preserve contact repeatability across loading cycles and board revisions.

  • Partner with electrical engineers on test-point access, probe selection, connector engagement, ESD provisions, cable routing, cooling, and interlocks; define motion and sequencing constraints with software and controls partners.

  • Build, assemble, instrument, and debug fixtures in the lab. Establish acceptance checks for alignment, force, board strain where needed, contact repeatability, and cycle life; separate fixture problems from board failures.

  • Design safe loading, pinch-point protection, hard stops, and operator access for manual or actuated fixtures. Make wear components easy to inspect, clean, and replace.

  • Manage fabrication partners and component vendors. Release CAD, drawings, bills of materials, tolerance analyses, assembly instructions, inspection plans, and maintenance procedures.

  • Own fixture deployment and acceptance at contract manufacturers, including assembly and alignment checks, correlation with lab fixtures, operator training, and troubleshooting. Support replication, board-revision changes, and maintenance through released documentation.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have strong mechanical intuition for precision interfaces, load paths, compliance, tolerances, and the behavior of delicate electronic assemblies.

  • Move readily between analysis, CAD, vendor collaboration, and hands-on assembly and debugging.

  • Care about repeatable contact, controlled forces, operator usability, and equipment that others can maintain.

  • Take ownership from concept through reliable daily operation, adapting fixtures to evolving boards and communicating clearly across electrical, software, manufacturing, and operations teams.

Required qualifications

  • Demonstrated ability to independently deliver significant precision-fixture or equipment projects from ambiguous requirements through detailed design, fabrication, validation, and sustained use.

  • Strong 3D CAD and released-drawing capability, including complete fabrication and assembly packages, bills of materials, and revision control.

  • Strong fundamentals in GD&T, tolerance analysis, locating schemes, stiffness, compliance, contact forces, and load paths.

  • Hands-on ability to work with fabrication partners, assemble and measure fixtures, diagnose failures, and iterate hardware in a lab or manufacturing environment.

  • Ability to communicate interfaces and tradeoffs across electrical, software, manufacturing, and operations teams and support deployment and troubleshooting at contract manufacturers.

Preferred qualifications

  • Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Prior PCBA test-fixture experience with board nests, probe or bed-of-nails fixtures, connector mating, and protection of delicate electronic assemblies.

  • Experience with ESD-aware tooling, thermal interfaces, actuated fixtures, interlocks, or structural and thermal simulation.

  • Experience with NX, SolidWorks, Creo, or equivalent tools; robotics hardware; or fixture replication and new-product builds at contract manufacturers.

What success looks like

  • Deliver a reusable PCBA fixture that meets agreed alignment, contact, board-support, and loading requirements, with demonstrated repeatability and protection of the assembly under test.

title: Commissioning Project Lead, Data Center Delivery
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Industrial Compute organization is building the infrastructure required to support the next generation of frontier AI systems. Through a combination of strategic partnerships and self-built data center campuses, we are scaling the power, cooling, electrical, mechanical, and controls infrastructure needed to deliver compute at unprecedented scale.

The Commissioning organization is responsible for ensuring this infrastructure is safely tested, validated, integrated, and transitioned into reliable operations. For our self-build campuses, the team operates through a hybrid delivery model: OpenAI provides commissioning leadership, discipline ownership, governance, and project integration, while commissioning partners provide field and test engineering capacity to support inspections, startup, testing, and turnover.

About the Role

We are seeking a Commissioning Project Lead to own the commissioning strategy and execution for a large-scale, self-build data center project.

You will lead the overall commissioning program from early construction planning through startup, functional testing, integrated systems testing, and final turnover. You will establish the commissioning execution plan, integrate commissioning activities into the master project schedule, coordinate multidisciplinary readiness, and lead the vendor commissioning partners providing field and test engineering capacity.

This role serves as the primary commissioning interface to project leadership, construction management, contractors, equipment vendors, operations, and commissioning partners. You will be responsible for creating clarity across organizations, identifying readiness and schedule risks early, and ensuring the facility progresses through testing and turnover against clearly defined acceptance criteria.

The role will initially support planning and coordination in a hybrid capacity and transition to full-time onsite presence as construction, inspections, startup, testing, and turnover become active.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the project commissioning strategy and execution plan, including scope, governance, acceptance criteria, responsibilities, sequencing, and escalation paths.

  • Lead the hybrid OpenAI and commissioning-partner delivery model, establishing clear RACI ownership, staffing requirements, performance expectations, and issue-management processes.

  • Integrate commissioning into the master project schedule, including construction readiness, energization, equipment startup, functional testing, integrated systems testing, and turnover milestones.

  • Lead commissioning coordination across construction management, contractors, design teams, equipment vendors, operations stakeholders, and field/test engineering teams.

  • Drive multidisciplinary commissioning readiness across electrical, mechanical, controls, and supporting infrastructure, identifying dependencies and resolving blockers before they affect testing.

  • Own visibility into commissioning risks, including schedule constraints, readiness gaps, design and submittal issues, safety constraints, resource bottlenecks, deficiencies, and documentation quality.

  • Coordinate QA/QC inspections and test execution with discipline commissioning leads, contractors, equipment vendors, and commissioning partners.

  • Strong working knowledge of electrical and mechanical commissioning workflows, with the ability to coordinate dependencies across power, cooling, controls, and supporting systems.

  • Experience integrating commissioning activities into construction schedules, lookaheads, energization plans, equipment startup sequences, and turnover milestones.

  • Strong owner, contractor, equipment vendor, and commissioning-agent management skills, including the ability to drive accountability across organizations without direct authority.

  • Experience managing commissioning documentation, test procedures, deficiency resolution, issue tracking, acceptance criteria, and quality governance.

  • Ability to identify commissioning and operational-readiness risks early and translate technical issues into actionable schedule and project decisions.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience communicating technical readiness, risk, and recovery plans to senior project leadership.

  • Owner-side commissioning experience and experience establishing or scaling hybrid owner/vendor commissioning delivery models are strongly preferred.

  • Professional credentials such as a PE license, QCxP, CxA, BCxP, CCP, PMP, or other relevant commissioning, engineering, construction, or project management certification are preferred.

Location

This role will support one of OpenAI’s self-build data center campuses in the Savannah, Georgia metro area or Abilene, Texas area. title: Deal Operations, EMEA
descriptionHtml:
About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a senior individual contributor to support revenue growth across EMEA by helping sales teams structure and close commercially sound deals. You will balance speed and responsiveness with pricing discipline, consistent processes, and appropriate financial and commercial controls.

In this role, you will be the day-to-day Deal Operations partner for EMEA account teams, reviewing pricing, discounts, and commercial terms across new business, renewals, and expansions. You will guide sellers through deal requirements, evaluate non-standard requests, and coordinate the approvals needed to move opportunities through contracting and closure.

You will also develop scalable workflows, guidance, and tools that improve deal turnaround times, documentation quality, and consistency across the region.

This role partners closely with Sales, Finance, Legal, Pricing, and Revenue Operations, with Product and other teams engaged as needed, to resolve deal issues and support accurate execution from quote through contract and booking.

In this role, you will:

  • Serve as the primary Deal Operations contact for EMEA account teams, managing deal intake, prioritizing requests, and guiding sellers through pricing, review, and approval processes.

  • Review quotes and proposed commercial terms, including discounts, payment schedules, contract duration, and customer commitments, for accuracy and alignment with pricing guidelines and commercial policies.

  • Build financial analyses and deal models to assess revenue, margin, discount impact, and profitability, and explain the tradeoffs of proposed deal structures to decision-makers.

  • Partner with Sales to structure deals that meet customer needs and OpenAI’s commercial objectives, recommending alternatives when proposed terms fall outside established guidelines.

  • Coordinate deal reviews and required approvals across Finance, Legal, Pricing, and Revenue Operations. Prepare clear recommendations, document decisions, and escalate exceptions to the appropriate stakeholders.

  • Identify risks in non-standard terms and work with Legal and Finance to resolve contractual, billing, and revenue recognition considerations before execution.

  • Maintain complete deal records and approval documentation in CRM, CPQ, and contract management systems, and partner with Revenue Operations to align approved terms, executed agreements, and booking information.

  • Help develop and maintain deal approval policies, escalation paths, pricing guidance, and standardized templates. Improve workflows to reduce bottlenecks while maintaining appropriate controls.

  • Equip sellers with practical guidance and training on deal requirements and approval processes. Apply AI and automation to improve deal intake, knowledge retrieval, and self-service support.

  • Track Deal Desk metrics such as turnaround time, approval bottlenecks, exception trends, and quote accuracy. Use recurring deal patterns to recommend improvements to commercial policies, processes, and tools.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 8+ years of experience in Deal Desk, commercial finance, pricing, sales operations, or a related function, preferably in a high-growth technology environment.

  • Hands-on experience reviewing and structuring complex enterprise deals and supporting quoting, commercial approvals, and contracting processes.

  • Strong financial modeling and analytical skills, including experience assessing pricing, discounts, revenue, margins, and deal profitability.

  • Knowledge of enterprise software commercial terms and subscription or consumption-based business models, with the judgment to identify issues that require Legal or Finance review.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to explain commercial tradeoffs, make clear recommendations, and coordinate timely decisions across teams.

  • Experience with CRM systems, configure-price-quote (CPQ) tools, and contract management platforms, along with strong spreadsheet skills.

  • Attention to detail and a track record of improving approval workflows, documentation, and operational processes as a business scales.

  • Sound commercial judgment and the ability to manage competing priorities and tight deadlines while maintaining accuracy and appropriate controls.

  • A collaborative, hands-on approach to supporting sales teams and familiarity with using AI and automation to improve deal workflows and productivity.

title: Senior Counsel, Competition
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI's Legal team plays a crucial role in furthering OpenAI's mission by tackling innovative, fundamental legal issues in AI. If you're passionate about doing significant and unique work as a technology lawyer, this team is for you. The team comprises professionals from diverse fields, including technology, AI, privacy, IP, corporate, employment, tax law, regulatory, and litigation.

We’re seeking a senior lawyer to join OpenAI’s small but growing competition legal team and play a leadership role on a wide range of important legal and regulatory matters. This role will involve engaging with competition regulators globally, supporting OpenAI’s active M&A program, providing strategic and actionable legal advice on competition law issues related to our business activities, and driving antitrust enablement and training initiatives.

title: Cyber Operations Strategist, Critical Harm Operations
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Critical Harm Operations sits within User Safety & Risk Operations and builds enforcement systems for Frontier Risk and Material Harm that are accurate, fast, defensible, and built to scale. The Cyber vertical turns policy into reviewer standards, calibrated judgment, quality systems, escalation paths, and automation guardrails.

 

About the Role

We are looking for a senior cybersecurity practitioner and operations strategist to raise the quality, scalability, and technical rigor of our Cyber Operations. You will combine hands-on cyber judgment with systems-level operating design: resolve the hardest dual-use questions, evolve SOPs, uplift reviewers and vendors, and build practical tools and automations.

This is a senior IC role. Success is not primarily cases closed; it is durable improvement in the operating model and the reviewers who run it.

This Toronto-based role is currently remote and is expected to transition to an in-office arrangement by end of year.

 

In this role, you will:

  • Drive the Cyber Operations operating model across domain priorities, SOPs, escalation paths, quality health, vendor capability, roadmap inputs and help inform trusted access strategies.

  • Serve as the senior cyber expert for complex or high-risk decisions across ChatGPT, API, Codex, agents, and emerging product surfaces.

  • Translate policy ambiguity, quality misses, appeals, and reviewer disagreement into clear decision rules, calibration examples, training, and tooling requirements.

  • Build durable operating systems and quality loops: golden sets, holdouts, double-labeling, adjudication, error taxonomies, reviewer calibration, and automation evaluations.

  • Raise FTE and BPO capability through onboarding, certification, coaching, recurring calibration, and vendor-performance partnership.

  • Use quality, appeals, SLA, backlog, and disagreement signals to diagnose root causes and prioritize high-leverage fixes.

  • Build hands-on solutions—SQL analyses, scripts, dashboards, LLM eval workflows, evidence enrichment, routing logic, and lightweight automations—that improve decision quality and reduce manual effort.

  • Partner with Policy, Integrity, Safety Systems, Security, Legal, Product, Engineering, and Investigations to operationalize changes and drive launch readiness.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Have 8+ years of hands-on cybersecurity experience in offensive security, threat intelligence, incident response, security research, red teaming, application security, DFIR, malware analysis, or a related field.

  • Can reason deeply about attacker tradecraft, vulnerability exploitation, credential abuse, malware, persistence, evasion, exfiltration, cloud or identity abuse, and ambiguous dual-use activity.

  • Have built or improved high-stakes operations, reviewer programs, QA systems, escalation workflows, or vendor/BPO programs.

  • Can turn complex cyber and policy judgment into reviewer-usable SOPs, decision trees, training, and concise written recommendations.

  • Are comfortable using SQL, Python, Python, C/C++, JavaScript, PowerShell, and Bash, APIs, LLM tooling, or automation to solve operational problems.

  • Understand human-in-the-loop automation, evaluations, monitoring, holdouts, and fallback paths for sensitive workflows.

  • Operate independently in ambiguity, communicate clearly across technical and non-technical audiences, and bring sound judgment and discretion when handling sensitive material.

  • Experience with trust and safety, platform abuse, cyber misuse of AI systems, or LLM safety.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with golden sets, classifier or prompt evaluations, and reviewer-quality programs.

  • Experience enabling global vendor reviewer operations.

title: Applied Data Science & Insights Leader - GTM Intelligence Solutions and Technical Success
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The GTM Data Science team partners with Go-to-Market, Technical Success, Product, Engineering, RevOps, and Strategic Finance to build the shared intelligence layer for OpenAI's B2B business. The team turns product usage, customer behavior, revenue, field activity, and customer feedback into rigorous insight products that help leaders and field teams understand where customers are succeeding, where adoption is blocked, and what actions will accelerate durable growth.

We are building systems that make customer intelligence proactive: surfacing risk, expansion potential, product gaps, and repeatable playbooks before they show up as escalations or missed opportunities.

About the Role

As the Applied Data Science & Insights Lead for GTM Intelligence Solutions and Technical Success, you will be a hands-on technical leader responsible for shaping how OpenAI measures, understands, and improves customer adoption across our B2B products. You will build AI/ML-powered intelligence products that connect account health, product usage, customer lifecycle, support tier, qualitative sentiment, commercial context, and field actions into a practical operating system for GTM and Technical Success.

This role will build the data science foundation for Technical Success: defining the metrics, models, operating insights, and decision systems that help the team scale customer adoption and expansion with rigor.

You will also be expected to build and lead a small mighty team over time: setting direction, hiring and developing talent, creating operating cadences, and holding a high bar for technical rigor and business impact.

You will lead the development of models, metrics, and decision systems that recommend what GTM and Technical Success teams should do next, explain why, and measure whether those interventions worked. Your work will help customers move from pilots to production, deepen usage across products, identify high-value use cases, reduce churn risk, and create a faster feedback loop from the field back to Product and Research.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.


The Vision

  • Build a unified GTM intelligence layer that connects product telemetry, customer health, revenue, support tier, lifecycle stage, field activity, and qualitative feedback.

  • Turn adoption breadth, usage depth, sentiment, and customer maturity signals into next-best-action systems for Technical Success and field teams.

  • Create a measurement foundation for Technical Success playbooks, including whether recommended actions were taken and whether they improved customer outcomes.

  • Help OpenAI understand customer happy paths: the use cases, product behaviors, and interventions that lead to durable adoption, expansion, and retention.

  • Productize insights into workflows used by Technical Success, Sales, RevOps, Finance, Product, and executive leadership.

In This Role, You Will:

  • Define and lead the roadmap for GTM Intelligence and Technical Success insight products in partnership with cross-functional leaders.

  • Build the data science foundation for Technical Success, including core metrics, customer health definitions, intervention measurement, and reusable playbook analytics.

  • Develop propensity score models for model and product feature adoption, helping Technical Success and GTM identify which customers are most likely to adopt, which interventions can move adoption, and where support should focus.

  • Build, mentor, and lead a small team of data scientists and cross-functional analytics partners as the GTM Intelligence function scales.

  • Set technical standards for modeling, metrics, experimentation, documentation, and production readiness across the team's work.

  • Create team operating rhythms that balance urgent field needs with durable roadmap execution, quality review, and stakeholder alignment.

  • Build predictive and causal models for customer health, expansion propensity, churn risk, adoption depth, use-case fit, and intervention effectiveness.

  • Design next-best-action systems that identify account opportunities and risks, recommend playbooks, and explain the evidence behind each recommendation.

  • Partner with Technical Success leaders to enumerate playbooks and actions, instrument action tracking, and measure outcomes over time.

  • Develop customer segmentation and benchmarking frameworks across products, industries, personas, support tiers, and lifecycle stages.

  • Create scalable insight products that are embedded into field workflows rather than living only as one-off analyses or static dashboards.

  • Translate field feedback and account-level patterns into clear product and GTM recommendations for senior leadership.

  • Collaborate with Data Engineering and RevOps to improve the data foundations connecting product telemetry, Salesforce, support signals, revenue, and qualitative feedback.

  • Maintain a high bar for analytical rigor, including causal evaluation, validation, data quality, and clear caveats.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have:

  • 10+ years of experience in applied data science, analytics, machine learning, quantitative strategy, or a closely related field.

  • Deep technical skill in SQL and Python, with the ability to move from raw tables to production-quality models, metrics, and decision systems.

  • Strong applied experience with statistical modeling, causal inference, machine learning, customer segmentation, churn or health modeling, or recommendation systems.

  • Experience with propensity score modeling, uplift modeling, or related causal methods for adoption, activation, retention, or product feature usage.

  • Experience building production or workflow-embedded data products for GTM, sales, customer success, technical success, growth, or enterprise SaaS teams.

  • Product intuition and business judgment for turning ambiguous questions into repeatable models, tools, metrics, and operating cadences.

  • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to distill complex analysis into clear recommendations for technical partners, field teams, and executives.

  • Comfort partnering across technical and non-technical teams, including Product, Engineering, Technical Success, Sales, RevOps, Finance, and Data Engineering.

  • A track record of operating autonomously in fast-moving environments and raising the quality of how teams use data to make decisions.

  • Experience leading teams or serving as a technical lead for multi-person data science initiatives, including mentoring, roadmap-setting, and quality review.

  • Ability to hire, develop, and retain strong data science talent while creating a collaborative, high-accountability team culture.

About the Role

We are seeking an Electrical Engineer to design and integrate on-site power-generation systems for large AI data center campuses. You will work across generation, substations, medium-voltage distribution, protection, auxiliary systems, grid interfaces, and data center loads. This role will establish technical requirements, evaluate technology and vendor solutions, and carry electrical designs from concept through commissioning and validated operation.

Travel: 50%

Responsibilities

  • Develop electrical architectures, one-lines, design criteria, specifications, and studies for generation plants and campus interconnections.

  • Design and review generator or alternator interfaces, transformers, MV and HV switchgear, protection, synchronization, grounding, station service, DC systems, and black-start capability.

  • Perform or review load flow, short circuit, arc flash, protection coordination, transient, motor-starting, grounding, and reliability studies.

  • Coordinate generation controls, microgrid or islanding behavior, utility interconnection, data center load characteristics, and operating modes.

  • Evaluate OEM and EPC proposals, equipment ratings, test plans, failure modes, maintenance strategies, and lifecycle tradeoffs.

  • Support procurement, factory acceptance testing, construction, energization, commissioning, performance testing, and root-cause investigations.

  • Resolve cross-discipline interfaces with mechanical, controls, CSA, fuel, utility, and data center electrical teams.

  • Create repeatable electrical reference designs and standards for future generation deployments.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of electrical engineering experience on power generation, utility, industrial, microgrid, or mission-critical projects.

  • Deep knowledge of generators, transformers, switchgear, protection and controls, grounding, auxiliary power, and electrical system studies.

  • Experience with grid-connected and islanded generation, synchronization, load sharing, and black-start or restoration concepts.

  • Ability to interpret OEM data, operating scenarios, failure modes, and data center load requirements.

  • Experience carrying designs through construction, commissioning, and operational validation.

  • Knowledge of applicable NEC, NFPA, IEEE, NERC, and utility requirements.

  • Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering or a related field.

Preferred Skills

  • Professional Engineer license.

  • Experience with gas turbines, reciprocating engines, battery systems, microgrids, or hybrid generation plants.

  • Proficiency with ETAP, PSCAD, PSS/E, SKM, EasyPower, or equivalent analysis tools.

  • Experience supporting high-density data center loads and fast-changing AI compute demand.

The AI Architect team partners with organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact.
