title: Protection Scientist Engineer, Integrity
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Integrity team is responsible for the scaled systems that help identify and respond to bad actors and harm on OpenAI’s platforms. We protect users and the wider world by developing responses to complex harms and building the harm protections needed for new product and model launches. Integrity’s work spans not only across frontier harms like biological weapons and cybersecurity, but also high severity abuses such as child safety, nation-state misuse, and violence.

About the Role

Protection Scientists within Integrity design, orchestrate, and mature systems of defence against usage harms enabled by OpenAI's products. We are systems thinkers that combine deep harm domain expertise with breadth across investigation, data science, machine learning, policy and operations. Our distinctive strength is understanding how these disciplines fit together and translating between them to design and build effective systems of defence.

Your core hands-on technical responsibility is harm detection. You will design, build, evaluate and maintain production detection systems, drawing on investigative expertise, data and shared engineering platforms. You will develop signals, classifiers and detection systems, and improve their ability to identify harmful activity accurately as products and behaviour evolve.

You will also own the strategy and cross-functional delivery of protection work for a harm area or product launch. Working closely with investigators and other domain experts, you will ground the design in a deep understanding of how the harm occurs and translate that understanding into a system of defence. You will connect detection with policy, review, interventions, enforcement and measurement, continually calibrating the system against real cases and expert judgement as it scales.

You will identify what needs to be built or changed and make it happen. Success requires setting clear priorities, aligning partners, resolving dependencies and communicating evidence, decisions and trade-offs crisply. It also requires a willingness to jump in and work directly on whatever is blocking system effectiveness, using your breadth of skills.

This role is based in our SF, NYC, or London offices and includes participation in an on-call rotation that may involve resolving urgent escalations outside normal working hours. Some investigations may involve sensitive content, including sexual, violent or otherwise disturbing material.

In this role, you will:

  • Define and drive protection strategy for a harm area or launch. Translate ambiguous risks into goals, priorities and roadmaps, and make trade-offs based on evidence, risk and available capacity.

  • Directly build and maintain harm detection. Develop production signals, classifiers and pipelines using SQL, Python, machine learning and language models, integrating with shared engineering platforms.

  • Lead cross-functional execution. Translate between specialist roles, establish shared understanding and ownership, resolve technical and organisational dependencies, and communicate recommendations and specific asks clearly.

  • Investigate emerging harms and abuse patterns. Work with world class domain experts to distinguish harmful activity from legitimate use, develop detection criteria, and inform policies and review protocols with Policy and Operations partners.

  • Evaluate and improve the complete system of defence. Measure remaining harm, detection quality and intervention effectiveness and collaborate with Data Science on more sophisticated metrics. Use expert feedback and operational outcomes to guide improvements.

  • Protect product and model launches. Define data, detection and review requirements; establish monitoring; investigate gaps and critical escalations; and drive improvements informed by post-launch findings.

  • Scale effective approaches with language models, agents and reusable tools. Choose where automation and human judgement are needed, and build documentation and processes that improve reliability and help others extend the work.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Think in systems. You have enough breadth across technical, analytical, investigative and operational disciplines to understand how they fit together, recognise gaps and translate between specialist perspectives.

  • Bring deep expertise in at least one relevant harm domain, developed through integrity, trust and safety, security, investigations or related work. You approach unfamiliar problems with curiosity and respect for expert knowledge and you are driven by reducing harm.

  • Are proficient in SQL and Python and have experience writing reliable and efficient production code for detection and data processing. Additional ML or SWE experience is a plus.

  • Can apply quantitative analysis and machine-learning methods to measure risks and evaluate system effectiveness. You understand the limitations of your data and can reason about missed harms, false positives and appropriate interventions. Additional DS/measurement background is a plus.

  • Have experience setting strategy and delivering complex, cross-functional technical projects. You can turn an ambiguous problem into a plan, align people with different priorities and drive work through to completion.

  • Communicate clearly and concisely in writing and conversation. You can explain technical findings, make actionable recommendations and surface uncertainty and trade-offs to different audiences.

  • Can use language models and other automation to scale analytical, investigative or operational work, with evaluation and human oversight appropriate to the problem.

title: Software Engineer, Identity Infrastructure
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Identity Infrastructure Engineering team builds the identity and access systems that OpenAI’s researchers, engineers, and internal teams rely on to protect critical systems and data.

We partner with Research, Applied Engineering, Infrastructure, IT, and Security to make secure access practical across cloud and internal environments.

About the Role

We’re looking for a hands-on software engineer to design and build high-scale, high-throughput secure access proxies and the distributed systems behind them. These are tier-zero services: researchers, engineers, and agents depend on them to reach critical infrastructure safely and reliably.

You’ll work at the intersection of networking, distributed systems, and infrastructure security, building the serving paths and control-plane integrations that connect identities to resources. Teleport is a core part of the current platform; the role also includes credential brokers, policy enforcement, and developer-facing integrations.

You’ll own the services you build from design and implementation through production. That means understanding human, agent, and workload traffic, improving throughput and tail latency, making authorization decisions auditable, and designing for safe multi-region rollout and recovery. We’re looking for someone who can turn a demanding security requirement into software that works well at scale and is straightforward for other engineers to use.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and implement secure access proxies, gateways, and credential brokers that provide narrowly scoped, auditable access to infrastructure and internal services while reducing standing privileges..

  • Integrate identity and access policy across clients, proxies, and target systems so approved permissions take effect promptly and access expires or is revoked when required. Ensure correct behavior when policy is stale or sessions remain active.

  • Build observability that explains the end-to-end access path: latency, errors, saturation, authorization decisions, and identity attribution, without leaking credentials.

  • Engineer safe multi-region rollouts, canaries, rollback, failover, and recovery. Validate changes with realistic test environments, load tests, and failure testing.

  • Keep core access services reliable, performant, and maintainable. Own production support, maintenance, upgrades, and incident recovery; ship durable fixes that reduce recurring failures, alert noise, and manual work.

  • Make secure access easy to adopt through reusable APIs, client tooling, diagnostics, and self-service workflows. Lead migrations that preserve critical workflows, with tested rollback and recovery paths and clear ownership across Infrastructure, Security, and SRE.

You might thrive in this role if you: 

  • Have built and operated production backend, proxy, networking, or infrastructure services with demanding scale or availability requirements.

  • Have practical networking depth and can reason about HTTP, TCP, TLS, DNS, routing, and load balancing across real request paths.

  • Can explain how you handled performance bottlenecks, partial failures, multi-region deployment, or a difficult production change in a system you personally built.

  • Understand authentication, authorization, least privilege, trust boundaries, credential handling, and the consequences of an access-control failure.

  • Have strong software engineering fundamentals and experience with Go, Rust, Python, or similar languages.

  • Use tests, profiling, telemetry, and reproducible experiments to debug across system boundaries and verify correctness, performance, and recovery.

  • Make practical scope decisions, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and follow through from code to production. Teleport or comparable access-platform experience is helpful; strong engineering and production ownership matter more than knowing every tool.

title: Controls Engineer, Power Generation and Microgird
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital and delivery partners, is building the infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems. The Data Center Engineering team defines repeatable technical standards and carries them through design, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness. The team works across data center facilities, power generation, compute infrastructure, construction, procurement, and operations to deliver reliable capacity at unprecedented scale and speed.

About the Role

We are seeking a Controls Engineer to design, program, integrate and commission on-site power generation and microgrid control systems serving large AI data center campuses. You will own control architecture and functional requirements across generation packages, balance-of-plant systems, electrical protection, microgrid controls, and data center monitoring. You will work from concept through factory testing, site commissioning, performance validation, and operational improvement.

This role requires hands-on experience with industrial control systems, including PLC and DCS programming, plant-level control sequences, equipment integration, simulation, testing and commissioning. The engineers will work with equipment vendors, system integrators and the broader data center team to make sure the complete power system operates safely and reliably across normal and failure conditions.

Travel: 50%

Key Responsibilities

  • Power Generation and Microgrid Controls

    • Design, program and commission plant power controllers (PPCs) and microgrid control systems for gas turbine and reciprocating engine power plants.

    • Develop control sequences for grid-connected, islanded and transition modes, including startup, shutdown, synchronization, load sharing, import/export control, load shedding, black start, restoration and resynchronization.

    • Coordinate active power, reactive power, voltage and frequency controls across generators, energy storage, MV UPS and other distributed energy resources.

    • Define how the plant responds to generator trips, loss of utility power, large load changes, equipment failures and loss of communication.

    • Work with OEMs to define the boundaries between turbine or engine controls, generator controls, the PPC, protection systems and data center controls.

  • Electrical systems and utility interconnection

    • Review utility and transmission-provider interconnection requirements and translate them into plant control, protection, metering, communications and testing requirements.

    • Work with utility and equipment vendors to define controls and interfaces at the point of interconnection, including power limits, voltage and frequency response, reactive, power factor, telemetry and dispatch.

    • Review interconnection studies, operating procedures and test requirements, and track the actions needed to demonstrate compliance.

    • Work with Engineer-Of-Record (EOR) to review load-flow, short-circuit, stability, step-load and electromagnetic transient (EMT) studies. Use the results to develop control settings, sequences and test cases.

  • Control Architecture:

    • Develop and review functional design specifications (FDS), sequences of operation, network architecture diagrams, I/O lists and alarm philosophies.

    • Review P&IDs and instrumentation for generation-plant systems, including fuel gas, cooling, lubrication and other balance-of-plant equipment.

    • Define equipment interfaces, control modes, permissives, interlocks and failure responses between OEM packages and the plant control system.

  • Real-Time Simulation and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing:

    • Develop and execute real-time simulation and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) tests for generation and microgrid control systems using RTDS and RSCAD.

    • Work with internal engineering teams and equipment vendors to build and validate representative models of the electrical system, from the generation plant and utility interconnection through the data center distribution system to representative GPU rack loads.

    • Develop and execute test cases for normal operation, mode changes, load steps, trips, faults, and system failures.

    • Compare simulation and HIL results with equipment data, factory test results and field performance. Document model assumptions and limitations.

  • Testing, commissioning and delivery

    • Develop and review FAT, SAT and integrated systems test plans for plant and microgrid controls.

    • Participate in factory testing, site testing, energization support, tuning and commissioning of generation and data center power systems.

    • Troubleshoot controls and system-integration issues using controller data, alarms, event records, trends and test results.

    • Work with OEMs, EPCs, utilities and system integrators to resolve interface gaps and track issues through closure.

    • Coordinate the handover of final project deliverables, including software, configurations, backups, test records, operating instructions and training, to the data center operations team.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of hands-on experience designing, programming, integrating and commissioning industrial controls for power generation, industrial plants, utilities, or mission-critical infrastructure.

  • Strong hands-on experience with PLC, DCS, SCADA, historian, industrial-networking, and control-system integration.

  • Experience with plant power control, generator controls, synchronization, load sharing, islanding and load-shedding schemes.

  • Experience integrating controls with power generation equipment, protective relays, SCADA/EPMS and other plant systems.

  • Experience developing functional specifications, sequences, I/O, alarms, graphics, and factory or site test procedures.

  • Ability to troubleshoot across software, instrumentation, electrical, mechanical, communications, and operating-process boundaries.

  • Understanding of industrial cybersecurity, redundancy, failover, and change-control practices.

  • Bachelor's degree in controls, electrical, mechanical, chemical engineering, computer engineering, or a related field.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience with major turbine or reciprocating-engine control platforms and microgrid controllers.

  • Experience with data center power systems and rapidly changing AI or GPU loads.

  • Experience integrating gas generation with BESS, MV UPS and grid-forming or grid-following inverters.

  • Experience with EMT studies and model validation for weak-grid or islanded power systems.

  • Experience developing automated simulation tests and regression test libraries.

  • Experience with network redundancy, industrial protocols, OT cybersecurity and remote support for critical facilities.

  • Experience transitioning from temporary generation to permanent power systems.

  • Experience with IEC 61850 (MMS, GOOSE, SV), Modbus, OPC UA, DNP3, EtherNet/IP, or comparable industrial protocols.

  • Professional Engineer license, functional-safety training, or industrial-cybersecurity certification.

title: Applied AI Architect, Large Enterprise
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Applied AI Architect team partners with organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact. We work with customers across industries and digital-native businesses to identify where AI can create value, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption. The team brings together technical strategy, customer partnership, and practical deployment expertise, working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and specialist delivery teams.

About the Role

As an Applied AI Architect, you will be the senior technical owner for a named portfolio of customers and the primary technical counterpart to their leadership teams. You will act as the “CTO of your book of business”, shaping each customer's AI strategy and guiding their journey from pre-sales discovery and solution evaluation through deployment, adoption, and measurable business impact.

You will own the technical account plan across ChatGPT Enterprise, the OpenAI API, Codex, and other agentic AI solutions. In partnership with the Account Director, you will translate business priorities into a focused use-case portfolio, an actionable adoption roadmap, and a clear path to durable customer value and growth. The Account Director owns commercial strategy; you own the technical strategy, customer journey, and path to production value.

You will remain accountable for the technical outcome while bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, enablement, security, product, and partners to provide deeper expertise and execute work where needed. This role calls for strong industry fluency, sound architectural judgment, and the ability to move confidently between executive strategy and hands-on technical conversations.

This role is based in our London office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Serve as the primary technical advisor and long-term technical relationship owner for a named portfolio of existing customers and pre-sales prospects.

  • Partner with Account Directors on account strategy while owning the technical account plan, technical milestones, adoption priorities, and expansion opportunities.

  • Lead discovery with executives and technical teams to identify, qualify, and prioritize use cases tied to meaningful business outcomes.

  • Develop clear Applied AI Architectures spanning models, applications, data, integration, security, privacy, governance, evaluation, and deployment.

  • Guide customers through technical evaluations, demonstrations, workshops, prototypes, and proofs of value, securing confidence in both the solution and its path to production.

  • Maintain a focused use-case portfolio with clear decision criteria, ownership, blockers, success measures, delivery needs, and adoption plans.

  • Develop trusted relationships and technical champions across CTOs, CIOs, CISOs, AI leaders, engineering teams, and other customer stakeholders.

  • Qualify and coordinate support from Deployment Engineering, implementation, training and enablement, product and domain specialists, partners, and other delivery teams.

  • Remain accountable for technical progress and customer outcomes while ensuring delivery teams own implementation execution once engaged.

  • Track adoption, usage, account health, production readiness, and measurable customer impact, intervening early when risks threaten value realization.

  • Apply industry or digital-native expertise to recognize repeatable patterns, sharpen customer priorities, and identify relevant expansion opportunities.

  • Share customer insights with Product, Engineering, and Research, translating field learnings into better products, architecture guidance, and reusable practices.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have significant experience in customer-facing technical roles such as solutions architecture, solutions engineering, technical account leadership, AI deployment, or technical customer success.

  • Have guided enterprise organizations from technical evaluation through production adoption and measurable business impact.

  • Build credibility with senior technical and business leaders while communicating equally well with hands-on engineers.

title: Applied AI Engineer, Codex
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. For software engineering organizations, this means helping customers adopt Codex and other OpenAI capabilities across the software development lifecycle—transforming how teams plan, build, test, review, and deliver software.

We work directly with engineering leaders and hands-on developers to identify high-value opportunities, design and implement AI-powered development workflows, and scale what works across engineering organizations. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products, reusable architectures, and technical patterns that help developers everywhere get more value from Codex.

About the Role

As an Applied AI Engineer focused on Codex, you will partner directly with leading engineering organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that transform how software is developed. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from workflow and use-case selection through prototyping, evaluation, production rollout, and scaled adoption.

You will work alongside engineering teams to build advanced AI coding workflows, integrations, automations, and evaluation systems—often using Codex itself as part of your development process. You will help customers make technical decisions involving model behavior, agentic workflows, developer environments, security, reliability, evaluation, and operational readiness, while ensuring deployments translate into measurable improvements in engineering productivity and software delivery.

You will work closely with OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, Sales, and the broader Codex organization, translating real-world deployment experience into high-signal product and model feedback. Success is measured by production systems, sustained developer adoption, and meaningful improvements to how engineering organizations build software—not simply successful demonstrations or enablement activity.

title: Applied AI Engineer, Codex Core Agent
descriptionHtml:
About the Team
The Codex Core Agent team builds the kernel of Codex. We own making the agent better, accelerating research, and making those improvements real in production for our users.

That means working across the systems that make Codex actually function as an agent in the real world: the production performance envelope around tokens, latency, reliability, cost, and capacity; the core execution loop and interfaces that turn models into useful behavior; the shared infrastructure that enables other teams to build on Codex; and the feedback loops that turn real-world usage into better models and better agent behavior over time.

About the Role
We’re looking for applied AI engineers to help bring Codex agents from impressive demos to dependable tools. This role is about improving agent performance on real software engineering tasks and closing the gap between research capability and real-world usefulness.

You’ll work closely with research, infrastructure, and product to ensure agents are not just powerful, but useful, steerable, and reliable in practice. The job is not only to improve model behavior in isolation, but to turn those improvements into measurable gains in solve rate, usefulness, and economic value for users.

What You’ll Do

  • Design and iterate on agent behaviors across real-world coding tasks and long-horizon workflows.

  • Work closely with research to develop and run evals to measure agent performance, regressions, failure modes, and edge cases.

  • Improve performance through prompting, tool-use strategies, context construction, and model-facing experimentation.

  • Analyze failures in production and systematically improve robustness and reliability.

  • Build feedback loops and data systems that get better real-task data into evaluation and research.

  • Work with product teams to shape user-facing agent experiences and the interfaces the agent depends on.

  • Help define what “good” looks like for agents completing complex tasks end-to-end.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

  • Have experience building or shipping machine learning or LLM-powered products.

  • Are strong in Python and comfortable with modern ML tooling.

  • Have worked on model evaluation, fine-tuning, or prompt design.

  • Think in terms of systems and user outcomes, not just model metrics.

  • Enjoy debugging messy, real-world failures and turning them into improvements.

  • Want to work in the layer that turns research and model potential into systems that actually work for users.

title: Software Engineer, Ads Integrity
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Integrity team builds the systems that protect OpenAI’s products, users, and ecosystem from abuse. We work across product engineering, infrastructure, safety, and operations to detect and prevent harmful, fraudulent, deceptive, and adversarial activity at global scale.

As OpenAI builds new ads experiences, we are establishing the integrity foundation that will keep the ads ecosystem safe and trustworthy from the start. This includes protecting advertiser onboarding, detecting unsafe or policy-violating ad content, preventing fraudulent and abusive advertiser behavior, and defending the ads ecosystem against spam, manipulation, and other forms of abuse.

Ads Integrity is a new and highly cross-functional area. The team partners closely with Ads, Product, Safety, Policy, ML, Privacy, Security, and operations teams to build protections directly into the ads platform rather than layering them on after the fact. This is an opportunity to define how integrity works for a new ads ecosystem from first principles.

About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced Software Engineer to build the backend systems and infrastructure that keep OpenAI’s ads products safe, trustworthy, and resilient to abuse.

In this foundational role, you will design systems that detect, prevent, and respond to harmful, deceptive, fraudulent, or policy-violating activity across the ads lifecycle. The problems span advertiser onboarding and verification, account and behavioral risk, content safety, spam and fraudulent interactions, detection and enforcement infrastructure, and the systems that connect integrity signals and models to real-time product decisions.

This is not an ML-specialist role, but familiarity with ML for Ads integrity is always welcome. You’ll work closely with ML engineers and researchers and build systems that consume and operationalize ML-based signals, but your primary focus will be designing and operating robust backend and distributed systems. You’ll help determine how signals, rules, models, and human review come together into reliable integrity protections for advertisements that can operate at OpenAI scale.

This role is particularly well suited to an engineer who has built large-scale systems in integrity, trust and safety, anti-abuse, fraud, risk, security, or a related adversarial domain.

You will have significant ownership over what we build and how we build it, partnering across Integrity and Ads to establish the architecture and technical foundations that will protect OpenAI’s ads ecosystem as it grows.

This role is based in San Francisco. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and build large-scale backend systems that detect and prevent harmful, deceptive, fraudulent, or policy-violating activity across the ads ecosystem.

  • Build low-latency integrity infrastructure capable of evaluating risk signals and making decisions in or near real time.

  • Develop scalable risk-signal pipelines, decision systems, rules and enforcement infrastructure across the advertiser and ads lifecycle.

  • Build advertiser onboarding, business verification, account-risk, fraud-detection, and abuse-prevention capabilities that make it harder for malicious actors to enter or exploit the ecosystem.

  • Develop systems that support ads-specific content safety and enable the detection and enforcement of unsafe, misleading, deceptive, or policy-violating ads.

  • Build protections against spam, fraudulent interactions, manipulation, and other adversarial behaviors that threaten the health of the ads ecosystem.

  • Partner with ML teams to integrate classifiers and model-based signals into production integrity systems, including both lightweight real-time protections and more sophisticated asynchronous detection.

  • Build feedback loops, review systems, and integrity metrics that improve detection quality while carefully managing false positives and impact on legitimate advertisers and users.

  • Create tooling and infrastructure that enable operations and policy teams to investigate abuse and make fast, consistent, and explainable decisions.

  • Engineer systems that adapt as adversaries change their tactics and support effective experimentation, monitoring, and incident response.

  • Partner closely with Ads Engineering to integrate integrity protections throughout the ads platform without compromising reliability, latency, or product quality.

  • Help define the technical strategy and architecture for Ads Integrity as both the product and underlying threat landscape evolve.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have significant experience building and operating large-scale backend or distributed systems.

  • Have worked on integrity, trust and safety, anti-abuse, fraud, risk, security, business verification, or another domain where systems must operate against sophisticated or evolving adversaries.

  • Have built detection, decisioning, enforcement, verification, investigation, or risk infrastructure in production.

  • Understand how rules, heuristics, risk signals, ML-based signals, and human review can work together within a dependable production system.

  • Are comfortable building ML-adjacent infrastructure and partnering closely with ML teams without needing to be an ML domain expert.

  • Have built low-latency, high-throughput services or data pipelines with demanding reliability, correctness, privacy, and security requirements.

  • Can reason about false positives, adversarial behavior, explainability, auditability, and the operational impact of automated enforcement.

  • Think holistically about threat models, system architecture, data quality, observability, user impact, and ecosystem health.

  • Can define technical direction in an ambiguous 0→1 environment and independently drive complex work across teams.

  • Communicate clearly and work effectively across engineering, product, policy, safety, security, operations, and machine-learning teams.

  • Have experience with ads, ads integrity, advertiser systems, or ads fraud. This is a plus, but not a requirement.

  • Are excited to build the integrity foundation for a new product area rather than inherit a mature system.

About the Role - Platform Operations Program Manager

As a Platform Operations Program Manager, you'll partner across Product, Engineering, Policy, Legal, Security, and Developer Experience to design the systems and operating models that enable ecosystem growth while maintaining quality, trust, and an exceptional developer experience.

This role requires strong operational judgment, a deep understanding of developer platforms and APIs, empathy for the developer experience, and the ability to translate evolving product, platform, and policy requirements into scalable operational systems.

Location: San Francisco, CA (Hybrid - 3 days in office)

What You'll Do

  • Own the operational processes that help developers bring apps, plugins, and integrations to market, from submission and review through launch, appeals, and ongoing monitoring.

  • Manage external review partners and policy operations workflows, helping teams apply standards consistently while identifying areas where guidance, process, or quality expectations need to improve.

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Policy, Legal, Security, Developer Experience, and Go-to-Market teams to turn platform goals and requirements into clear, effective operating processes.

  • Lead high-priority partner reviews and escalations, balancing speed to launch with user trust, and consistent standards.

  • Create feedback loops across product, policy, tooling, and developer experience teams to reduce friction for developers and improve the quality of integrations over time.

  • Lead automation and AI-driven initiatives, such as agentic workflows, to improve the speed, consistency, and scale review and support processes.

  • Serve as a senior cross-functional partner, using operational expertise and platform insights to help shape product strategy and improve how the ecosystem works.

You Might Thrive If You

title: Software Engineer, Frontier Systems - Power Management
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Frontier Systems team at OpenAI builds, launches, and supports the largest supercomputers in the world that OpenAI uses for its most cutting edge model training.

We take data center designs, turn them into real, working systems and build any software needed for running large-scale frontier model trainings.

Our mission is to bring up, stabilize and keep these hyperscale supercomputers reliable and efficient during the training of the frontier models.

About the Role

As a Software Engineer on the Frontier Systems team focused on power management, you will work on critical infrastructure to support cutting-edge research. With large-scale supercomputers consuming substantial amounts of power, managing this efficiently is key to maximizing computational capacity.  This role is critical to ensuring that our cutting-edge research supercomputing infrastructure runs smoothly, while maintaining reliability and grid-level power stability.

Our team empowers strong engineers with a high degree of autonomy and ownership, as well as ability to effect change. This role will require a keen focus on system-level comprehensive investigations and the development of automated solutions. We want people who go deep on problems, investigate as thoroughly as possible, and build automation for detection and remediation at scale. 

In this role, you will:

  • Develop and implement system-level and software-level solutions to optimize power usage in large-scale supercomputers, ensuring efficient and reliable operations.

  • Build automation to monitor power consumption patterns during training workloads and design algorithms to stabilize these fluctuations, preventing issues with grid reliability.

  • Work with researchers and engineers to design tools for real-time monitoring, detection, and remediation of power-related hardware and system faults.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally to translate complex electrical system requirements into code, while driving continuous improvements in power management solutions.

  • Drive the development of power throttling mechanisms at the IT system level to dynamically adjust power usage based on workload demands and infrastructure limitations.

  • Collaborate with hardware design teams to integrate system-level power control requirements into IT hardware design, ensuring seamless coordination between software-driven power management and hardware capabilities.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 7+ years of software engineering experience with a focus on solving large-scale, system-level challenges.

  • Strong proficiency in Python and familiarity with automation and scripting tools (e.g., shell scripting).

  • Experience with distributed systems to efficiently aggregate and analyze streaming data.

  • Knowledge of electrical engineering concepts including digital signal processing, power systems, Fast Fourier Transforms, or related areas.

  • Experience in system-level investigations and development of automated solutions to address power management, fault detection, and remediation.

  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to dig into noisy data (experience with SQL, PromQL, Pandas, etc.).

  • Comfort working with both hardware and software teams to solve multidisciplinary problems.

Bonus points if you have:

  • Deep expertise with the power characteristics of synchronous workloads (as seen in supercomputing or model training environments).

  • Knowledge of power control requirements in IT hardware design, with the ability to drive cross-functional collaboration to integrate power management features into hardware systems effectively.

  • Working knowledge of control system fundamentals and how physical systems respond to control strategies.

descriptionHtml:
About the team

Customer Education helps people and organizations build the skills and confidence to use AI effectively. We create courses, live learning, community programs and product education that help people apply OpenAI’s products to their work.

About the role

We’re looking for a User Education Lead who is excited about what AI can make possible for people at work and wants to bring more people along on that journey.

You’ll lead education for enterprise users who are getting started with AI or need help turning early experimentation into everyday use. You’ll help people discover what’s possible, build confidence through practice and develop the judgment to use AI well.

title: Head of Sourcing Enablement & Delivery
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Strategic Sourcing & Procurement helps OpenAI secure the products, services, and partnerships that support our research, build our products, and grow our business. We work with teams across the company to make sound commercial decisions and move important work forward.

As OpenAI grows, we are rethinking how sourcing works: bringing expertise into decisions earlier, simplifying contracting, and using AI to give Procurement more time for judgment and strategic work. What we learn internally—and through our supplier and enterprise-buyer relationships—can also inform better products, partnerships, and industry adoption.

About the Role

We’re looking for a senior leader to head Sourcing Enablement & Delivery, leading sourcing operational delivery, contracting enablement, and AI transformation—and building Procurement’s contribution to OpenAI’s commercial growth. You will build the teams, systems, service model, and cross-functional partnerships that enable sourcing and contracting at scale, helping teams move quickly without losing commercial discipline or accountability.

You will partner with GTM, Sales, and Partnerships to develop Procurement’s contribution to OpenAI adoption and commercial growth. Bring procurement-industry knowledge, buyer insights, and lessons from internal AI use into customer engagement, product feedback, and opportunities across the procurement ecosystem.

Reporting to the Head of Strategic Sourcing, you will manage the Sourcing Delivery and Contract Management leaders and shape this new function’s priorities, team, and measures of success.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

Priorities and what success looks like

  • A focused roadmap: clear choices about what to build first, what to defer, and how progress will be measured.

  • Stronger delivery: capable leaders and teams, faster execution, less rework, and fewer unresolved ownership gaps.

  • AI adoption: sustained use of AI-enabled capabilities, with measurable gains in quality, capacity, and user experience.

  • Commercial results: increased OpenAI adoption across the procurement industry and a measurable contribution to commercial growth, consistent with independent supplier selection and purchasing decisions.

In this role, you will:

  • Build and lead the organization. Hire and develop managers, coach performance, and build succession and leadership depth. Decide how employees, contractors, delivery partners, and AI share the work. Hold leaders accountable for results, capacity, and team health.

  • Own sourcing enablement and delivery operations. Set service commitments and quality standards with the Delivery and Contract Management leaders. Match support to deal complexity and risk, and use internal customer feedback to improve the service. Category and Sourcing leads retain ownership of their strategies and deals, including supplier selection, negotiations, and purchasing.

  • Lead the sourcing operating rhythm. Bring demand, priorities, and capacity into one forward plan, informed by workload and performance data. Work with category leaders to make tradeoffs, resolve dependencies, and follow through on commitments. Provide inputs to Procurement-wide planning and functional business reviews.

  • Strengthen contracting. Partner with Legal and Procurement Operations/COE on contract lifecycle management, approved templates, and negotiation playbooks that improve quality and free category teams to focus on strategic deals.

  • Lead RACI development. Define responsibilities, decision rights, handoffs, and escalation paths within Procurement and across partner teams. Define how the team prioritizes work, allocates resources, and resolves delivery issues.

  • Create mechanisms to bring sourcing into decisions earlier: connect business demand, supplier activity, and renewals—including work outside formal intake—with Sourcing teams, so options can be shaped before commitments and Finance and cross-functional teams can have better visibility.

  • Build and prove AI-enabled ways of working. Own use-case priorities, adoption, and business outcomes for sourcing and contracting experiences that begin in ChatGPT and connect to trusted enterprise systems. Partner with Finance Enterprise Technology on technical delivery and with Legal, Security, and Operations on controls and support, including preserving access restrictions and contractual commitments. Turn what works into reusable capabilities, demonstrations, and product feedback.

  • Define Procurement’s commercial-enablement approach with GTM, Partnerships, Legal, and Compliance including program scope, decision rights, purchasing independence, and information-sharing boundaries. Lead Procurement’s analysis, coordination, and follow-through for approved programs; GTM owns customer sales. Maintain independent purchasing decision-making and identify and escalate any proposed linkage between OpenAI’s purchasing commitments and customer sales.

  • Help define goals and measures of success for Procurement’s contribution to OpenAI adoption and commercial growth with Sourcing leadership and cross-functional partners.

  • Bring procurement-buyer expertise into GTM. Own this team’s buyer insights and use cases. Work with Marketing, Sales, Product, Customer Success, and Partnerships to shape demonstrations, industry content, and customer conversations, using examples approved for external use.

  • Drive OpenAI adoption across the procurement industry. Work with Sourcing leadership, partners and GTM to explore how Procurement third-parties and partners can adopt and distribute OpenAI capabilities. Contribute industry expertise and evidence from internal use; GTM and Partnerships own commercialization.

  • Partner with Legal and Compliance to embed business-integrity and confidentiality safeguards; implement required disclosures, recusals, and independent-decision making arrangements.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 12+ years of experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, vendor management, or commercial leadership, with strong judgment about supplier choices, negotiations, contracts, and risk.

  • Have built or transformed a procurement capability through rapid growth or change, with clear evidence of better execution, commercial outcomes, or user experience.

  • Have managed managers and developed strong teams through hiring, coaching, performance management, succession planning, and thoughtful use of internal and external capacity.

  • Have worked in or closely with marketing, sales, or commercial teams, ideally serving procurement buyers. You can turn customer needs into use cases and business cases, and deliver commercial results with partner teams.

  • Know the procurement industry—its buyers, technology providers, service firms, and buying priorities. You understand how to sell to Procurement, including how buyers assess risk, negotiate, and secure internal support.

  • Use industry analysts, market research, buyer conversations, and professional networks to form a point of view on emerging trends and inform roadmaps, partnerships, and GTM priorities.

  • Have turned AI, automation, or enterprise technology into capabilities people use. You can work with technical partners, drive adoption, measure improvements, and recognize where human judgment remains essential.

  • Can set direction when the path is not defined. You prioritize work and resources, explain tradeoffs plainly, and earn support from teams you do not manage. You are curious about AI and willing to test, learn, and change course.

title: Lead Counsel, Commercial (Energy - Infrastructure)
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Legal team plays a crucial role in advancing our mission by tackling innovative and fundamental legal issues in AI. The team includes professionals from diverse legal fields—technology, AI, infrastructure, privacy, IP, corporate, employment, tax, regulatory, and litigation—who collaborate closely with colleagues across the company.

If you are passionate about being an energy and infrastructure lawyer working on cutting-edge challenges, you’ll thrive here.

About the Role

We’re seeking an experienced energy lawyer to support the business on legal matters relating to the energy and power infrastructure supporting OpenAI’s fast-growing data center portfolio. This is a cross-functional role that will partner closely with energy, infrastructure development, engineering, procurement, and finance teams to advise on complex legal and regulatory issues and help structure, negotiate, and manage the transactions that secure reliable, cost-effective power for OpenAI’s long-term infrastructure ambitions.

We’re looking for an experienced energy and infrastructure lawyer who thrives in ambiguity and wants to help define the commercial playbook for power procurement and energy project development in the AI era. This role reports to the Associate General Counsel for Infrastructure.

The role’s scope and level will reflect the successful candidate’s experience and expertise.

In this role, you will:

  • Own legal strategy and risk management for OpenAI’s global energy procurement and power infrastructure transactions, from initial structuring through execution and ongoing implementation.

  • Draft, negotiate, and advise on complex power purchase agreements, energy supply and hedging arrangements, and utility service and special contracts, including related regulatory requirements and approvals.

  • Structure and negotiate interconnection, transmission, and utility infrastructure arrangements that align power availability with data center development and operating schedules.

  • Advise leadership and business leaders on legal and regulatory considerations as they develop and implement our energy and data center strategy

  • Support strategic partnerships involving renewable and other carbon-free generation, energy storage, and on-site or behind-the-meter power solutions for AI infrastructure.

  • Develop legal and regulatory frameworks for energy procurement, project development, and collaboration with utilities, independent power producers, and energy developers.

  • Partner with finance and operations teams to align contract terms with business and compliance requirements, including pricing, delivery and curtailment risk, credit support, and project milestones.

  • Collaborate with policy and regulatory colleagues on issues impacting energy transactions, utility tariffs, grid access, market participation, retail service requirements, and renewable energy attributes.

  • Build scalable, efficient contracting processes that support OpenAI’s energy and infrastructure development at speed while managing legal and regulatory risk.

  • Guide outside counsel and coordinate with real estate, construction, tax, and regulatory counsel on energy transactions and project development.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • 10+ years of legal experience, with substantial focus on complex commercial energy transactions.

  • Have a JD and license or qualification to practice in CA.

  • Relevant experience in-house, at a law firm, or a combination of both, advising energy companies, utilities, developers, major power customers, or infrastructure investors.

  • Demonstrated experience independently leading complex energy transactions, including power purchase, utility service, or interconnection agreements.

  • Familiarity with U.S. electricity markets, utility tariffs, and the regulatory frameworks affecting energy supply, interconnection, and transmission, including FERC, state utility commissions, and regional grid operators.

  • Strong commercial judgment and financial fluency in energy pricing, volume commitments, credit support, and allocation of development and operating risk.

  • Demonstrated ability to operate with autonomy and sound judgment in highly technical and fast-moving environments.

  • Exceptional communication skills, with an ability to distill complexity into actionable, business-aligned guidance and advise senior business leaders on strategic decisions.

  • Experience advising on cross-border energy deals and international energy regulatory frameworks is a plus.

  • Prior experience with data center power procurement, generation or storage development, energy project finance, joint ventures, or on-site and behind-the-meter energy projects is a strong plus.

title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Health
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Health team, within OpenAI’s broader Post Training organization, has a mission to ensure AGI improves health for all humanity.

Improving human health will be one of the defining impacts of AGI. Hundreds of millions of people already turn to ChatGPT for questions about their health and millions of clinicians use it weekly to support care delivery. Increasingly capable models create an opportunity to make high-quality medical intelligence more accessible across patients and clinicians—raising the floor of human health—and accelerate the new capabilities and scientific advances that raise the ceiling of human health.

Our job is to make those benefits real. We work across the full model stack—pretraining, midtraining, reinforcement learning, post-training, evaluations, harnessing, and deployment—and connect that research to the patients, clinicians, and real-world outcomes we aim to improve.

About the Role

We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher who wants to build frontier health capabilities and turn them into impact at scale. This is a role for someone who can take an important, underdefined problem from 0→1: identify the right bet, build what’s needed to test it, and drive it all the way to a measurable improvement in the models and products we actually ship.

We’re especially excited about two kinds of people: researchers with the technical depth to move the frontier in pretraining, reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, or evals; and researchers with real depth in developing frontier biomedical AI capabilities. Prior experience in healthcare is helpful but not required. Research excellence, velocity, ownership, and alignment with the mission are most important to us.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Own a high-leverage research direction end to end—from deciding which problem matters and how to measure it, to designing and running experiments, to integrating successful work into frontier models.

  • Develop scalable methods across pretraining, midtraining, reinforcement learning, and post-training to improve health reasoning, knowledge, reliability, calibration, and behavior.

  • Build and study RL environments grounded in real health problems; understand which data and training setups produce robust, generalizable improvements rather than just higher benchmark scores.

  • Create meaningful, trustworthy, and unsaturated evaluations that tell us whether our models are actually getting better at what matters for patients and clinicians.

  • Advance new 0→1 capabilities in health that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute.

  • Develop models and agents that can work over longitudinal, multimodal health data to produce useful predictions, surface new scientific insights, and support better individual- and population-level decisions.

  • Work closely with researchers, engineers, clinicians, and product teams to bring health capabilities into the models and products used by hundreds of millions of people.

  • Help establish that AI improves real health outcomes, not just that it can produce impressive answers or demos.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Care deeply about using increasingly capable AI to improve human health, and take seriously the responsibility of deploying it safely.

  • Have an unusually strong track record in machine learning or AI research, with the depth to push at least one important area forward: pretraining, reinforcement learning / post-training, evals (not necessarily specific to health); or substantial depth in a relevant frontier health / biomedical AI problem.

  • Are a hands-on builder: you can design experiments, write and debug code, work directly with data and training infrastructure, and move quickly from an idea to evidence.

  • Have strong research taste and can distinguish an important problem or a promising approach from an interesting one.

  • Own ambiguous problems end to end, and are willing to learn whatever is missing to get the job done.

  • Stay goal-oriented rather than method-oriented, and don’t shy away from unglamorous work if it is the highest-leverage path to impact.

  • Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype.

  • Enjoy working with low-ego, ambitious people across research, engineering, medicine, and product.

  • Bonus: Experience with health AI, longitudinal health data, or clinical research.

 

If you want your work to help make medical intelligence widely accessible—and to work on some of the most important frontier problems at the intersection of AI, science, and human health—we’d love to hear from you.

title: Technical Program Manager, Actuators
descriptionHtml:
About Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and advancing toward AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world environments. Working across the full model and systems stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the physical constraints of real-world systems to improve people’s lives.

About the Role

We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to own actuator development and integration from system goals through production readiness. The actuator program spans mechanical, electrical, firmware, harnessing, controls, test, reliability, manufacturing, and supply chain, and needs a TPM who can turn cross-functional decisions into clear scope, executable milestones, and timely decisions.

In this role, you will help the team converge on the right technical plan, surface risks early, and deliver reliable actuator systems on schedule.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA and requires in-person presence 4 days a week.

In this role you will:

  • Drive actuator programs end-to-end, aligning scope, milestones, interfaces, dependencies, and exit criteria across engineering teams.

  • Drive scope lock and technical convergence for sprints, MVPs, and stretch goals while connecting component decisions to system performance.

  • Coordinate actuator development across motors, gears, sensing, electronics, and firmware, and align the electrical and mechanical interfaces that connect actuators to the broader robot.

  • Lead validation planning from early prototypes through engineering validation, reliability testing, and production readiness.

  • Drive tradeoff decisions across cost, quality, performance, schedule, and lead time by collaborating cross-functionally and quantifying impact to meet program deliverables.

  • Establish effective mechanisms for technical reviews, change control, design releases, decision tracking, and manufacturing readiness.

  • Surface risks early and drive decisions, owners, and actions to closure.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have led complex electromechanical hardware programs from development through manufacturing.

  • Are equally comfortable reasoning about an actuator’s internal architecture and how it integrates into the larger system through PCBAs, connectors, cables,etc.

  • Can work effectively across ME, EE, firmware, interconnecting harnesses, controls, test, reliability, manufacturing, and supply chain.

  • Understand hardware development realities including prototype cycles, long-lead parts, suppliers, testing, design changes, and production ramp.

What success looks like:

  • Cross-functional scope, milestones, interfaces, dependencies, and exit criteria are aligned across engineering, supply chain and manufacturing teams.

  • Sprints, MVPs, and stretch goals converge on decisions connected to system performance.

  • Validation is planned from early prototypes through engineering validation, reliability testing, and production readiness.

  • Risks, tradeoffs, owners, and actions are surfaced early and driven to closure to meet program deliverables.

  • Mitigation strategies are well communicated and aligned upon, acceleration of hardware development from design to trials on the floor is quantifiable.

  • Tools and workflows built are well embedded in the daily routine of all the team members, thus do not seem an added overhead to get things done.

descriptionHtml:
About the Role

We are hiring a Data Scientist to help build OpenAI's B2B ecosystem and go-to-market data science capability. You will turn ambiguous commercial questions into evidence, recommendations, and operating decisions that help OpenAI understand where to focus as our B2B business expands.

OpenAI's B2B motion is growing quickly across products, customer segments, markets, and field teams. This role will partner with leaders across GTM, Revenue, Product, Finance, RevOps, Strategy, and Data Science to answer questions tied to international strategy, monetization, product penetration, field deployment, customer opportunity, and organizational design.

This is a founding-style opportunity within the broader GTM Data Science organization. The team and stakeholder model are still evolving, so you should be energized by building structure in ambiguity, helping define how the team works, and helping shape the bench around a high-priority commercial area.

In this role, you will bring data science craft, consulting-style problem solving, practical AI fluency, and strong business judgment to help senior leaders make better B2B decisions.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead strategic deep dives across international expansion, monetization, product penetration, customer segmentation, field deployment, ecosystem dynamics, and organizational design.

  • Help define the operating model for an emerging B2B data science capability, including how the team frames problems, engages stakeholders, evaluates opportunities, and turns insights into GTM action.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Senior-level experience in a quantitative role such as Data Science, Product Analytics, Decision Science, Growth Analytics, Strategy Analytics, or a related field.

title: Software Engineer, Compute Foundations Systems
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Frontier Systems Foundations, part of Compute Foundations at OpenAI, builds the systems software foundation that turns new compute infrastructure into reliable, usable capacity for frontier model training.

Our mission is to make some of the world's largest GPU clusters work reliably for frontier training. We bring new platforms and clusters online, safely maintain installed fleets, and partner with hardware, infrastructure, and research teams to resolve the system-level issues that keep jobs from running.

That means building and maintaining the software closest to the machine: Linux and Ubuntu operating-system images, kernels and modules, drivers, packages and repositories, disks and boot configuration, firmware integration, provisioning, and system-level validation. We make these components reproducible, compatible, and safe to operate across heterogeneous fleets.

About the Role

We are looking for systems software engineers with deep Linux and host-systems experience to build, qualify, and maintain the operating-system foundation for OpenAI's frontier compute fleet. Relevant backgrounds include kernel and module development, Linux distribution or image engineering, package management, firmware and driver integration, disks and boot, and bare-metal provisioning.

You'll work closely with hardware engineers, vendors, and infrastructure teams to bring up new platforms, integrate system components, and debug failures across firmware, disks, boot, operating systems, kernels, drivers, and workload interactions. Your work will directly influence how quickly new capacity becomes usable and how reliably large GPU fleets operate.

You should be comfortable writing and maintaining production-quality systems software and automation, but we do not expect expertise across every layer. This is an opportunity to go deep on challenging systems problems while building the image, package, qualification, and recovery paths that power the next generation of frontier models.

In this role, you will:

  • Build and maintain the Linux host software stack for large GPU clusters, including Ubuntu and OS images, kernel configuration and modules, drivers, packages, disks and storage configuration, and machine configuration.

  • Design reproducible OS-image builds, package and repository workflows, and system configuration for heterogeneous bare-metal and cloud compute fleets.

  • Integrate, test, and qualify kernels, modules, drivers, packages, and firmware across new and existing hardware platforms; build safe canary, rollback, and recovery paths for system changes.

  • Bring up new hardware platforms and compute SKUs, working with hardware engineers and vendors to resolve firmware, driver, operating-system, and compatibility issues.

  • Debug complex system failures across boot and provisioning, firmware, disks, kernels and drivers, and workload interactions; turn recurring failure modes into durable fixes, tests, and automation.

  • Improve provisioning, repave, maintenance, and recovery correctness by eliminating manual host-by-host intervention and making system behavior predictable at fleet scale.

  • Build focused systems tooling and diagnostics that make the host software stack easier to validate, troubleshoot, and operate across the installed fleet.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have significant experience building, integrating, or operating production Linux systems, particularly Ubuntu, Debian, or another major Linux distribution.

  • Have deep experience in one or more of: Linux kernels, modules, or device drivers; Linux distribution, package, repository, or OS-image engineering; boot, provisioning, disks, or machine configuration; firmware and driver integration, qualification, or rollout.

  • Can write, debug, and maintain production-quality systems software and automation using appropriate systems languages, scripting, and Linux tooling.

  • Understand how to build, test, package, qualify, and safely deliver system-level changes, including compatibility testing, staged rollout, rollback, and recovery.

  • Can systematically debug failures that cross hardware, firmware, boot, operating-system, kernel, and driver boundaries, and collaborate effectively with hardware and software partners.

  • Enjoy investigating difficult system behavior, identifying underlying failure modes, and building pragmatic fixes that make production systems more reliable.

Bonus points if you:

  • Have built bare-metal provisioning, machine-bootstrap, OS-reprovisioning, or system-lifecycle tooling.

  • Have worked with GPU systems, AI infrastructure, HPC clusters, accelerators, or other heterogeneous and performance-sensitive compute environments.

  • Have experience bringing up new server platforms or working directly with hardware and software vendors on firmware, driver, or operating-system compatibility issues.

  • Have contributed to Linux, kernel subsystems or modules, distributions, package ecosystems, drivers, firmware tooling, or other open-source systems software.

  • Have delivered or supported system-software changes across large production compute fleets.

title: Audio Engineer, Live Video
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity.

The Global Events Studio Team creates exceptional live and recorded video for Press, Marketing, Developer Experience, and Communications.

About the Role

The Audio Engineer will be the senior audio authority for high-profile livestreams, broadcast-style productions, studio recordings, public venue events, and critical on-location shoots. This person will design resilient audio systems, serve as A1 when failures are immediately visible, and deliver exceptional spoken-word audio across live, recorded, remote, and AI-enabled production workflows.

In this role, you will:

  • Own audio design and A1 execution for complex broadcasts, live stage events, podcasts, and critical film/on-location shoots

  • Build and operate redundant program, stream, multitrack, camera, backup-recorder, and archival audio paths with real-time monitoring and recovery procedures.

  • Mix full-duplex speech-to-speech audio between humans and AI models 

  • Design, commission, standardize, document, and improve audio signal flow for studios, control rooms, event spaces, and portable production systems.

  • Rapidly assess unfamiliar venues and design reliable systems around acoustic, power, network, access, RF, and footprint constraints.

  • Lead rigorous preproduction: technical designs, input lists, patch plans, frequency plans, rehearsals, testing, monitoring, redundancy, and fallback capture.

  • Diagnose and repair signal-chain, DSP, synchronization, routing, RF, networking, and hardware faults during live production.

  • Lead audio crews and freelancers, challenge flawed technical plans, and communicate decisive options under pressure.

  • Own multitrack recording, editorial handoff, backup, delivery, and archival workflows across professional formats and specifications.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 8+ years engineering complex live, broadcast, and studio production, including high-profile livestreams, public venue events, design, configuration, and programming of physical audio infrastructure, and critical on-location filming or streaming.

  • Proven experience serving as A1 when failures are immediately visible and time for sophisticated workarounds is measured in seconds.

  • Expert command of gain structure, routing, EQ, dynamics, automixing, feedback control, real time noise suppression, mix-minus, IFB, intercom, playback, comms, and latency management.

  • Deep experience designing and troubleshooting redundant program, stream, multitrack, camera, backup-recorder, and archival audio paths.

  • Advanced proficiency with networked audio and DSP systems such as Dante, AVB, SMPTE ST 2110, Q-SYS, Yamaha, and Shure.

  • Strong IP-networking knowledge, including clocking, multicast, VLANs, QoS, and diagnosing failures across audio, control, and enterprise IT environments.

  • Expert wireless-microphone and RF coordination skills across crowded, high-consequence production environments, including frequency planning, antenna distribution, and intermodulation.

  • Ability to capture exceptional spoken-word audio for keynote presenters, executive livestream hosts, stage panels, podcasts, voiceover, remote guests, and acoustically difficult spaces.

  • Advanced microphone selection and placement skills, including lavalier concealment, boom technique, room treatment, noise control, and feedback prevention.

  • Ability to mix full-duplex speech-to-speech audio between humans and AI models for a variety of different event formats

  • Fluency with broadcast encoders, embedded audio, streaming protocols, conferencing platforms, and external distribution endpoints.

  • Expert-level understanding of room acoustics and a fundamental understanding of acoustic science.

  • Demonstrated success diagnosing and repairing signal-chain, DSP, synchronization, routing, RF, networking, and hardware faults during live production.

  • Strong multitrack recording, timecode, sync, metadata, editing, mixing, delivery, backup, and archival judgment across professional formats and loudness specifications.

  • Functional audio post-production skills, including dialogue cleanup, noise reduction, EQ, dynamics, mix revisions, and delivery preparation.

  • Ability to lead audio crews, support technical freelancers, challenge flawed technical plans, and communicate decisive options under pressure.

  • Willingness to work onsite, travel globally as needed, and support rehearsals or productions outside standard hours when critical productions require it.

Workplace & Location

This is an onsite role and will require 5 days a week in our San Francisco office, with global travel and support outside standard hours when critical productions require it.

title: Lead Safety Engineer, Robotics
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.

About the Role

We are seeking a Lead Robotics Safety Engineer to define and lead the product safety strategy for our robotics program. You will work closely with leadership, engineering, research, legal, and policy teams to ensure safety is integrated into our products from the earliest stages of development through deployment.

This role combines product safety, regulatory strategy, systems engineering, and risk management. You will help shape how we think about safety across robotic platforms, influence product architecture and development decisions, and ensure our systems are designed to meet both current and emerging regulatory expectations.

You will serve as a subject matter expert on robotics safety standards, regulatory frameworks, and safety engineering practices while helping establish the long-term safety strategy for our products and organization.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. This role will be expected to be in office 4 days per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will

  • Define and lead the product safety strategy for robotic systems across the development lifecycle.

  • Monitor and influence emerging regulatory frameworks, industry standards, and policy developments relevant to robotics and autonomous systems.

  • Partner with engineering teams to translate safety requirements into product architecture, design decisions, and engineering requirements.

  • Develop and maintain system-level hazard analyses, risk assessments, and safety cases for robotic products.

  • Establish safety requirements, verification strategies, and evidence-generation plans to support product development and future certification activities.

  • Collaborate with legal, policy, and leadership teams to assess regulatory risks and inform long-term product strategy.

  • Partner with hardware, software, controls, and research teams to identify hazards and develop mitigations throughout the development process.

  • Lead system-level hazard analyses, HARA activities, FMEAs, and other structured risk assessment processes to identify hazards, evaluate risks, and drive mitigation strategies throughout product development.

  • Represent the company in discussions with standards bodies, industry groups, regulators, and external safety experts when appropriate.

  • Help build and scale the safety engineering function as the robotics organization grows.

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Enjoy applying first-principles thinking to complex safety and risk management challenges.

  • Are comfortable navigating ambiguity where regulations, standards, and technology are evolving simultaneously.

  • Can balance technical, regulatory, operational, and business considerations when making recommendations.

  • Enjoy working across disciplines and influencing engineering decisions without direct authority.

  • Are passionate about building products that are both innovative and demonstrably safe.

Preferred qualifications

  • Deep expertise in product safety, functional safety, systems safety, robotics safety, or related disciplines.

  • Experience working with safety and regulatory frameworks such as ISO 10218, ISO 13849, IEC 61508, ISO 12100, ANSI/RIA standards, or comparable safety standards.

  • Experience developing hazard analyses, risk assessments, safety cases, or certification strategies for complex electromechanical systems.

  • Familiarity with robotics, autonomous systems, industrial equipment, consumer products, medical devices, automotive systems, aerospace systems, or other safety-critical technologies.

  • Experience working with regulators, standards organizations, certification bodies, or industry working groups.
