title: Software Engineer, Infrastructure - Core Experimentation
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Statsig team within OpenAI owns the experimentation, rollout, dynamic configuration, and analytics infrastructure that sits on the launch path for OpenAI products. Our systems help teams ship safely, evaluate product and model changes in production, and make high-confidence decisions from real-world usage.

Statsig began as an independent company built around experimentation, feature management, and product analytics at scale. After Statsig joined OpenAI, the team began the next chapter: bringing that platform expertise and infrastructure into OpenAI as the experimentation and rollout foundation for every product we ship.

This is infrastructure with a very direct product consequence. Teams working on ChatGPT, Codex, model measurement, consumer experiences including ads, business subscriptions, developer products, and shared platform systems depend on Statsig to evaluate configurations, move traffic safely, ingest experiment data, serve analytics, and roll changes forward or back when production reality demands it.

We are at a critical point in the platform journey. Adoption is accelerating quickly across OpenAI, and the systems that were already important are becoming load-bearing for how the company launches. The infrastructure needs to stay fast under sharply increasing evaluation volume, reliable when more services depend on it, observable enough to debug quickly, and efficient enough to support OpenAI-wide scale.

Recent SDK and server-side infrastructure work has already produced measurable wins in latency, reliability, memory usage, and compute efficiency across important services. The next phase is to make those gains systematic: a platform that can absorb rapidly growing product velocity while preserving low latency, data quality, operational safety, and developer trust.

Based out of OpenAI's Bellevue office, we are a close-knit team that values in-person collaboration, technical depth, operational ownership, and building infrastructure that lets other builders move faster without taking on hidden reliability risk.

About the Role

As an Infrastructure Engineer on the Statsig team, you will build and scale the foundational systems behind OpenAI's experimentation and rollout platform. You will work on the distributed control plane, SDK and server evaluation paths, ingestion pipelines, analytics foundations, and operational tooling that make launches safe and measurable at OpenAI scale.

This role is deeply technical and centered on performance, scalability, reliability, and correctness. You will design systems that serve low-latency configuration decisions, handle high-throughput event ingestion, preserve data availability for experimentation and analytics workflows, and keep critical launch infrastructure dependable as usage grows.

The work matters because OpenAI's next phase depends on learning quickly without compromising safety or reliability. Every major product surface needs a trusted way to evaluate changes, progressively roll them out, understand impact, and recover cleanly. Statsig is one of the core infrastructure layers that makes that possible.

In This Role, You Will

  • Design and operate low-latency configuration delivery systems powering feature flags, dynamic configs, and progressive rollouts across OpenAI product suites.

  • Scale SDK, server-side evaluation, and control-plane systems so high-volume services can depend on Statsig without adding user-visible latency or operational fragility.

  • Build high-throughput data ingestion and analytics infrastructure for experimentation, product analytics, feature performance monitoring, and model or product measurement workflows.

  • Improve performance, efficiency, reliability, and observability of core Statsig infrastructure as OpenAI products scale globally.

  • Optimize query performance, data freshness, and data availability for teams making launch decisions from experimentation and analytics workflows.

  • Strengthen operational excellence through better SLOs, alerting, debugging tools, incident response, capacity planning, and failure-mode design.

  • Partner with teams across ChatGPT, Codex, model measurement, consumer ads, business subscriptions, developer products, and infrastructure to turn recurring launch and measurement needs into durable platform capabilities.

  • Lead large technical initiatives and shape the architecture of experimentation and rollout infrastructure used across the company.

You Might Thrive In This Role If You

  • Have experience building large-scale distributed systems with strict performance, availability, and correctness requirements.

  • Enjoy low-latency systems work, including real-time configuration delivery, SDK/runtime performance, caching, concurrency, and high-throughput service design.

  • Have built or operated large-scale data platforms, event pipelines, analytics systems, or query infrastructure where freshness and correctness matter.

  • Care deeply about reliability, observability, incident response, capacity planning, and the practical craft of keeping critical production systems boring in the best way.

  • Are excited by the post-acquisition chapter of a high-performing infrastructure team: preserving Statsig's strengths while integrating deeply into OpenAI's product and platform stack.

  • Want to work on infrastructure that directly affects how ChatGPT, Codex, model measurement, ads, business subscriptions, developer products, and future OpenAI surfaces ship.

  • Take ownership of complex technical problems end to end and enjoy building infrastructure that lets other teams move faster with more confidence.

Working alongside leading cloud providers, engineering firms, construction partners, utilities, and equipment manufacturers, we are delivering hyperscale AI campuses that enable the next generation of frontier AI models.

The Strategic Sourcing team develops and executes the commercial strategies that ensure our infrastructure programs have reliable access to the equipment, materials, and strategic partners needed to deliver at unprecedented scale. We partner closely with Infrastructure Delivery, Capacity Planning, Design Engineering, Hardware Operations, Finance, Legal, and our external suppliers to build a resilient global supply network capable of supporting Industrial Compute's long-term growth.

As we continue expanding globally, strategic sourcing becomes a critical competitive advantage, ensuring our infrastructure programs remain cost-effective, resilient, and capable of executing against aggressive deployment timelines.

You will own accounting and close activities across assigned balance sheet and P&L areas, manage intercompany activity for assigned entities, and build efficient, well-controlled processes.

title: Data Scientist, Cybersecurity
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Agentic Data Science team helps shape how AI agents are built, deployed, and improved across our products. We partner with product, engineering, research, and security teams to define meaningful measures of success, understand how our systems behave in the real world, and translate evidence into better decisions.
As AI agents become more capable, they can write and execute code, access sensitive systems, and complete increasingly complex tasks with greater autonomy. These capabilities create powerful opportunities to improve cybersecurity, but they also introduce risks that traditional security tools and processes were not designed to address. Meeting this moment requires new ways to measure security, evaluate defenses, and distinguish genuine risk reduction from friction that slows users down.


About the Role

We are looking for a senior data scientist to help define what effective cybersecurity looks like in the age of AI agents.
You will work across OpenAI’s Security organization and cybersecurity product teams to measure emerging risks, improve internal security controls, and shape AI-powered security products. The problems are foundational: How do we know whether an agent’s security controls are effective? Which safeguards meaningfully reduce risk, and which create unnecessary friction? When an AI system identifies a potential vulnerability, how do we determine whether the finding is accurate, actionable, and ultimately resolved? How do we detect anomalous behavior or risky access when the systems themselves are changing rapidly?
You will report into Data Science while partnering closely with Security, Cyber Product, Engineering, and Research. This is a high-ownership role for someone who can establish a new analytical discipline, operate across organizational boundaries, and turn ambiguous security challenges into measurable improvements.


In This Role You Will

  • Define how we measure AI-agent security. Establish metrics and evaluation frameworks for security-control coverage, agent behavior, sensitive actions, access patterns, detection quality, and emerging risks.

  • Improve security controls without introducing unnecessary friction. Quantify the effectiveness and operational costs of safeguards, including false positives, blocked actions, escalations, approval delays, and recovery paths. Help teams make controls safer, more precise, and easier to use.

  • Build the data foundations for security decisions. Partner with engineering and data teams to improve instrumentation, connect fragmented telemetry, establish trusted datasets, and surface important coverage and data-quality gaps.

  • Strengthen detection and response. Identify meaningful signals of anomalous behavior, risky access, sensitive-data exposure, and other security-relevant activity. Evaluate whether interventions improve detection quality, response times, and real-world security outcomes.

  • Shape AI-powered cybersecurity products. Partner with product, engineering, and research teams to assess how effectively AI systems identify security issues, support developer and enterprise workflows, and create measurable customer value.

  • Develop evaluation systems for security findings. Define quality measures for findings, including accuracy, severity, actionability, duplication, resolution, and downstream impact. Connect model behavior and product changes to outcomes such as triage, remediation, and vulnerability reduction.

  • Understand the complete security workflow. Measure how users discover, investigate, validate, prioritize, and resolve security issues. Identify opportunities to improve activation, adoption, retention, and enterprise value across customer-facing cybersecurity products.

  • Design rigorous measurement and experimentation strategies. Evaluate new models, security controls, product features, and workflows through controlled experiments, staged rollouts, observational analyses, and other methods appropriate for high-stakes environments.

  • Translate analysis into security and product strategy. Identify the highest-value decisions, clarify tradeoffs, recommend where teams should invest, and communicate findings clearly to technical partners and senior leadership.

  • Help establish a new security data science capability. Build a focused roadmap, create durable operating rhythms across Data Science and Security, and help shape how this discipline grows over time.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have

  • 5+ years of experience in data science, applied research, analytics, or a related quantitative field, with a track record of owning ambiguous, high-impact problems.

  • Experience in cybersecurity, trust and safety, fraud or abuse prevention, privacy, platform integrity, or another domain involving adversarial behavior and difficult-to-measure risks.

  • Strong proficiency in SQL and Python, including experience investigating complex datasets, working through incomplete instrumentation, and building reproducible analytical workflows.

  • Experience defining meaningful metrics and evaluation frameworks when ground truth is limited, outcomes are delayed, or important risks cannot be observed directly.

  • Strong judgment in experimentation, causal inference, observational analysis, and the practical limitations of different measurement approaches.

  • The ability to partner effectively with security engineers, product managers, software engineers, researchers, data engineers, and senior leaders.

  • A demonstrated ability to translate technical analysis into concrete improvements in products, systems, controls, or organizational priorities.

  • Comfort operating independently, defining a roadmap, and bringing structure to a domain without established processes or industry standards.

You Could Be an Especially Great Fit If You Have

  • Experience with detection engineering, threat research, security operations, insider risk, identity and access management, or privacy-preserving security analytics.

  • Familiarity with AI agents, large language models, model evaluations, automated code review, or AI-powered cybersecurity products.

  • Experience evaluating security findings, vulnerability detection, remediation workflows, or developer-facing security tools.

  • Experience balancing security effectiveness against user experience, including false positives, approval flows, operational burden, and recovery behavior.

  • Experience building automated monitoring, anomaly detection, production-oriented data assets, or systems that connect model outputs to real-world outcomes.

Role Summary

We are seeking a Partnerships Operations Lead to build and run the operating foundation for OpenAI for Government’s Partnerships team.

This person will serve as the operational connective tissue across the partner team, working closely with Account Directors, Solutions Architects, Revenue Operations, Deal Desk, and other cross-functional stakeholders to move opportunities from initial engagement through agreement and execution.

They will help ensure a smooth handoff to Technical Success across accounts by establishing clear readiness criteria, capturing the right commercial and customer context, and aligning teams on partner roles, commitments, dependencies, and success outcomes.

title: Applied AI Architect, Partner
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The AI Architect team partners with organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact. We work with customers across industries and digital-native businesses to identify where AI can create value, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption. The team brings together technical strategy, customer partnership, and practical deployment expertise, working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and specialist delivery teams.

Within the team, Partner Applied AI Architects work with strategic partners—including global and regional system integrators, consulting and advisory firms, and technology partners—to extend OpenAI’s technical reach and help partners deliver high-quality AI solutions for our joint customers. We bring together technical strategy, partner enablement, architecture expertise, and practical deployment experience, working closely with Partnerships, Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, Security, and specialist delivery teams.

About the Role

As a Partner Applied AI Architect, you will be a senior technical advisor to a portfolio of strategic partners and the primary technical counterpart to their leadership and delivery organizations. You will shape how partners build practices around OpenAI, develop solutions using our products, and take joint customers from AI opportunity and technical evaluation through production adoption and measurable business impact.

You will own the technical strategy and architecture across partner engagements involving ChatGPT Enterprise, the OpenAI API, Codex, and other agentic AI solutions. In close partnership with the Revenue Partnerships team, you will translate joint business priorities into technical strategies, solution patterns, enablement plans, and a focused portfolio of high-value customer opportunities.

You will work directly with partners on strategic customer engagements—leading discovery, shaping architectures, navigating complex technical decisions, and helping secure technical wins—while building the partner capabilities required to deliver successfully and independently at scale.

You will remain accountable for the technical quality and outcomes of the partnership while bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, security, product, enablement, and other teams when deeper expertise is needed. The role calls for strong architectural judgment, executive presence, partner leadership, and the ability to move confidently between business strategy and hands-on technical conversations.

In this role, you will:

  • Serve as the primary technical advisor and long-term technical relationship owner for a portfolio of strategic partners, building trusted relationships with their executives, AI leaders, architects, engineering teams, and delivery organizations.

  • Develop the technical strategy and plan for each partner, identifying priority solutions, use cases, technical capabilities, enablement needs, delivery risks, and opportunities to drive customer adoption.

  • Assess prospective and existing partners’ technical capabilities and delivery readiness, identifying strengths, gaps, and the investments required to successfully deliver OpenAI-powered solutions.

  • Lead technical discovery with partners and joint customers to identify, qualify, and prioritize AI use cases tied to meaningful business outcomes.

  • Develop clear Applied AI architectures spanning models, applications, enterprise data, integrations, identity, security, privacy, governance, evaluation, reliability, and deployment.

  • Collaborate with partner sales and technical teams on strategic opportunities, providing technical guidance through discovery, demonstrations, workshops, prototypes, architectural recommendations, and proofs of value.

  • Guide partners through their initial and most strategic OpenAI deployments, helping them navigate technical tradeoffs and production dependencies while ensuring solutions meet a high bar for quality, security, reliability, and responsible deployment.

  • Build partner capability and technical self-sufficiency through tailored enablement, architectural guidance, reusable solution patterns, technical workshops, and mentorship.

  • Establish clear standards and mechanisms for partner-delivered solution quality, identifying risks early and intervening when architecture, implementation, security, evaluation, or adoption issues threaten customer outcomes.

  • Orchestrate the right OpenAI specialists across Deployment Engineering, Product, Security, implementation, enablement, and domain teams while maintaining clear ownership and handoffs between OpenAI and partner delivery teams.

  • Track partner capability, joint pipeline technical progress, production adoption, usage, solution quality, and measurable customer impact to identify where additional investment or intervention is needed.

  • Identify repeatable patterns across partner engagements and turn them into architectures, playbooks, reference solutions, and best practices that allow successful approaches to scale across partners and customers.

  • Bring insights from partners and joint customers back to Product, Engineering, Research, and Partnerships, helping shape product strategy, technical guidance, and the broader OpenAI partner ecosystem.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have significant experience in senior customer- or partner-facing technical roles such as solutions architecture, partner engineering, field architecture, technical account leadership, AI deployment, or technical consulting.

  • Have worked successfully with global or regional system integrators, consulting firms, or other technology partners, and understand how partner organizations sell, architect, and deliver complex enterprise technology.

  • Have guided complex enterprise organizations from technical discovery and evaluation through production deployment, adoption, and measurable business impact.

  • Can build credibility with CTOs, CIOs, CISOs, partner executives, and AI leaders while communicating equally effectively with architects and hands-on engineers.

  • Bring strong software and cloud architecture foundations, including APIs, distributed systems, enterprise data, integrations, identity, security, privacy, and governance.

  • Understand modern AI systems, frontier LLMs, agentic applications, model evaluation, retrieval, and enterprise AI workflows.

  • Can prototype when useful, explain technical tradeoffs clearly, and work confidently with APIs, SDKs, and languages such as Python or JavaScript.

  • Have experience enabling technical organizations at scale, turning your own expertise into repeatable architectures, training, patterns, and practices that others can successfully apply.

  • Understand enterprise security and compliance requirements and can guide partners and customers through the technical considerations required to move AI systems safely into production.

  • Are comfortable balancing the needs of OpenAI, the partner, and the end customer, and can exercise sound judgment when those priorities do not perfectly align.

  • Know when to go deep personally, when to coach a partner toward the answer, and when to engage specialist resources.

  • Can prioritize across a portfolio of partners and customer opportunities, focusing technical resources on the work most likely to create durable customer value and adoption.

  • Communicate clearly and can turn ambiguity into a practical architecture, executive decision, enablement plan, or path to production.

title: Researcher, Alignment
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Alignment team at OpenAI is dedicated to ensuring that our AI systems are safe, trustworthy, and consistently aligned with human values, even as they scale in complexity and capability. Our work is at the cutting edge of AI research, focusing on developing methodologies that enable AI to robustly follow human intent across a wide range of scenarios, including those that are adversarial or high-stakes. We concentrate on the most pressing challenges, ensuring our work addresses areas where AI could have the most significant consequences. By focusing on risks that we can quantify and where our efforts can make a tangible difference, we aim to ensure that our models are ready for the complex, real-world environments in which they will be deployed.

The two pillars of our approach are: (1) harnessing improved capabilities into alignment, making sure that our alignment techniques improve, rather than break, as capabilities grow, and (2) centering humans by developing mechanisms and interfaces that enable humans to both express their intent and to effectively supervise and control AIs, even in highly complex situations.

About the Role

As a Research Engineer / Research Scientist on the Alignment team, you will be at the forefront of ensuring that our AI systems consistently follow human intent, even in complex and unpredictable scenarios. Your role will involve designing and implementing scalable solutions that ensure the alignment of AI as their capabilities grow and that integrate human oversight into AI decision-making.

This role is especially well suited for someone who can move from an ambiguous model-behavior question to a concrete experimental setup: formulate the hypothesis, build the evaluation or intervention, run the experiment, analyze the result, and decide what the evidence supports. This role may be based in San Francisco or London, subject to team needs and location approval.

In this role, you will:

We are seeking research engineers and research scientists to help design and implement experiments for alignment research. Responsibilities may include:

  • Develop and evaluate alignment capabilities that are subjective, context-dependent, and hard to measure.

  • Design evaluations to reliably measure risks and alignment with human intent and values.

  • Build tools and evaluations to study and test model robustness in different situations.

  • Design experiments to understand laws for how alignment scales as a function of compute, data, lengths of context and action, as well as resources of adversaries.

  • Design and evaluate new Human-AI-interaction paradigms and scalable oversight methods that redefine how humans interact with, understand, and supervise our models.

  • Train model to be calibrated on correctness and risk.

  • Designing novel approaches for using AI in alignment research

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Are a team player – willing to do a variety of tasks that move the team forward.

  • Have a PhD or equivalent experience in research in computer science, computational science, data science, cognitive science, or similar fields.

  • Have strong engineering skills, particularly in designing and optimizing large-scale machine learning systems(e.g., PyTorch).

  • Have a deep understanding of the science behind alignment algorithms and techniques.

  • Can develop data visualization or data collection interfaces (e.g., TypeScript, Python).

  • Enjoy fast-paced, collaborative, and cutting-edge research environments.

  • Want to focus on developing AI models that are trustworthy, safe, and reliable, especially in high-stakes scenarios.

Strategic Finance Data Science helps OpenAI make consequential financial and operating decisions as the business grows. We connect customer behavior, product economics and business performance to the choices leaders make about goals, customer acquisition and investment.

We work with customer executives, product and engineeriIng teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale. You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations. This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve.

This role is based in our SF or NYC office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.


In this role, you will:

descriptionHtml:

Our Federal Civilian and State & Local Government business supports public institutions across a broad range of missions. We help these customers apply frontier AI to public services, knowledge work, research, and mission operations through hands-on delivery, tailored enablement, and collaboration with their teams.

About the Role

The Strategic Delivery Lead (SDL), Federal Civilian & State and Local Government, will shape and deliver high-impact AI engagements across federal civilian agencies and state and local governments. You will turn customer priorities into practical deployments and sustained use, helping government leaders and mission teams apply OpenAI technology to public services, knowledge discovery, and operational workflows.

This individual contributor role reports to the leader of Federal Civilian and State & Local Government. You will work alongside Account Directors and Applied AI Architects across assigned engagements, coordinating Research, Product, Engineering, Policy, Security, and Enablement resources. title: Researcher, Safety Training
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Safety Research at OpenAI is responsible for ensuring our most capable models can be safely deployed in the real world. The Safety Training team develops the research and engineering methods that shape model behavior through post-training, reinforcement learning, evaluation, and deployment feedback.

Our work focuses on making models helpful, reliable, and aligned with safety policies across model types, modalities, and product surfaces. We work across both longer-term safety research and the core post-training work needed to improve production models.

About the Role


We are seeking researchers to advance safety training for OpenAI’s models. You will develop methods that improve model behavior after pretraining, including RLHF, RLAIF, DPO, PPO, preference optimization, adversarial training, synthetic data generation, safety evaluations, and model behavior analysis.

This role is highly cross-functional. You will work with core training teams, product teams, policy, legal, trust and safety, and domain experts to identify risks, design interventions, train models, evaluate outcomes, and launch safety improvements in OpenAI products.

In this role, you will:

  • Conduct research on safety post-training methods, including RLHF, RLAIF, DPO, PPO, reward modeling, adversarial training, synthetic data, and scalable oversight

  • Develop and implement model training interventions that make models safer, more reliable, and more aligned with user intent

  • Build evaluations and measurement infrastructure for safety harms, high-stakes reliability failures, policy adherence, jailbreak robustness, multimodal risks, agent behavior, and domain-specific risks

  • Translate ambiguous safety problems into concrete research plans, datasets, training runs, evals, and product-facing improvements

  • Analyze model failures such as hallucination, unsafe tool use, prompt injection, privacy leakage, over-refusal, under-refusal, sycophancy, and deceptive or misleading behavior

  • Partner with domain experts to design safety training approaches for areas like cyber, privacy, youth safety, wellbeing, and other frontier-risk domains

  • Collaborate with research and deployment teams to ensure safety improvements are incorporated into OpenAI’s core model training and product launches

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have hands-on experience training, fine-tuning, or post-training language models, multimodal models, or agentic systems

  • Have experience with RL, RLHF, RLAIF, DPO, PPO, reward modeling, preference optimization, instruction tuning, or related post-training methods

  • Care deeply about shaping model behavior in real-world systems, not only publishing research

  • Are excited by open-ended safety problems where the right method, dataset, eval, or training objective may not be obvious at the start

  • Bring strong research judgment and strong engineering ability, including comfort running experiments, analyzing model behavior, and working with large-scale ML systems

  • Have experience in one or more relevant domains: agents, tool use, multimodal models, cyber/security, reliability, uncertainty calibration, factuality, evals, privacy, youth safety, wellbeing, or applied alignment

  • Enjoy collaborating across research, engineering, product, policy, legal, and trust and safety teams

  • Hold a PhD in machine learning, computer science, or a related field, or have equivalent practical research or engineering experience

Nice to have:

  • Experience improving production model behavior through post-training or deployment feedback

  • Experience building safety evals, automated graders, red-teaming systems, or monitoring pipelines

  • Experience working with human feedback, expert feedback, synthetic data, or policy-grounded training data

  • Experience in safety-critical or abuse-sensitive domains where models must balance helpfulness, refusal, uncertainty, and user intent

The Statsig team at OpenAI builds and operates the experimentation platform that powers product development, measurement, and decision-making across the company. title: Engineering Technician, Actuators
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.

About the Role

We are seeking Engineering Technicians to support the assembly, testing, and prototyping of custom electromechanical actuators for advanced robotic systems. You will build and test hardware from engineering drawings and procedures through inspection, troubleshooting, and rework, partnering closely with mechanical, electrical, manufacturing, and test engineers.

These roles focus on hands-on work with precision electromechanical hardware, including stator prototypes, motor and actuator assemblies, and mechanical and electrical testing. You will help turn engineering designs into validated hardware while improving build records, work instructions, and repeatable assembly and test practices for future robotic platforms.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 5 days a week.

In this role, you will:

Each opening focuses on actuator builds, testing, or stator prototyping, with responsibilities aligned to the selected specialty.

  • Actuator builds: assemble subassemblies and complete actuators from drawings, bills of materials, and work instructions, checking fit, orientation, torque, routing, and workmanship.

  • Testing: set up and run established mechanical and electrical tests, confirm the setup against the procedure, record measurements, and identify unexpected results.

  • Stator prototyping: support winding, insulation, termination, bonding, inspection, and rework using the selected build process and documented instructions.

  • Troubleshoot build and test issues with engineers. Isolate problems through inspection and measurement, escalate deviations, and verify the result after approved rework.

  • Maintain accurate build and test records, part and revision traceability, inspection results, and rework history.

  • Use bench observations to improve work instructions, fixtures, tooling, and parts organization as prototypes evolve.

  • Follow safety, ESD, cleanliness, and quality practices, and communicate material shortages, unclear instructions, and other blockers as priorities change.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have hands-on experience building or testing mechanical, electrical, or electromechanical hardware in a lab, prototype shop, or manufacturing environment.

  • Can work from drawings, bills of materials, wiring diagrams, and procedures, and recognize when the instructions and hardware do not agree.

  • Use hand tools, torque tools, and measurement equipment carefully, with consistent workmanship and attention to units and acceptance limits.

  • Troubleshoot methodically, document observations, and know when to pause work and ask for engineering support.

  • Take ownership of build quality and records while adapting to changing designs and priorities.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience relevant to the selected specialty may include:

  • Building or testing actuators, motors, robotics hardware, servos, or other precision electromechanical systems.

  • Motor manufacturing, especially stator assembly, winding, insulation, termination, bonding, impregnation, or inspection.

  • Soldering, crimping, connector assembly, harness routing, adhesives, or fixture-assisted assembly.

  • Mechanical or electrical test setup, instrument checks, measurement capture, and documenting unexpected results.

  • Inspection, traceability, nonconformance handling, and structured rework.

  • Hands-on rework, basic machining, or prototype part modification using shop tools.

  • Use of calipers, micrometers, multimeters, LCR meters, insulation-resistance testers, or torque tools.

  • Improving prototype or manufacturing work instructions and build processes.

title: Program Manager, National Security Policy Operations
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI's mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We believe that achieving our goal requires effective engagement with public policy stakeholders and the broader community impacted by AI. The Global Affairs team builds trusted relationships that help external stakeholders understand advanced AI and ensure that their perspectives inform our work. Within Global Affairs, the National Security Policy team works across OpenAI to understand how increasingly capable AI systems affect security, governance, and democratic resilience, and to advance policies that support the responsible development and use of AI.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a highly organized and skilled Program Manager, National Security Policy Operations to join the Global Affairs team, reporting directly to Sasha Baker, who leads the National Security Policy team. This is a hands-on program management role focused on running the planning, coordination, and execution systems that enable the team to operate effectively.

This person will translate team priorities into executable plans, synthesize data and inputs into clear program updates, manage key programs and workstreams, and create the operating discipline that keeps decisions, dependencies, and follow-through on track. This role sits at the center of the National Security Policy team's planning, prioritization, information flow, and execution. Success means giving the team clear visibility into commitments, dependencies, decisions, and risks; reducing fragmented operational work; enabling faster and better-informed decisions; and ensuring priorities move reliably from scoping through completion. The ideal candidate takes deep pride in program management as a craft and is energized by enabling policy and technical experts to do their best work. The role works closely with policy experts but is not primarily responsible for setting policy positions or serving as the team's external policy lead.

This role may be based in San Francisco or Washington, DC. It will require travel as necessary,

and we offer relocation assistance to new employees.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Run portfolio planning and team operations, including intake, workplans, milestones, owners, dependencies, risks, and progress reporting. Surface capacity constraints, recommend sequencing and tradeoffs, and escalate decisions to the team lead, who sets priorities and makes resource decisions.

  • Build and maintain lightweight, repeatable operating systems for planning, meeting cadences, knowledge management, decision logs, and centralized tracking of developments, commitments, and follow-up.

  • Own the team's program metrics and central tracking of commitments, owners, deadlines, dependencies, decisions, and follow-up. Keep records current and reliable, and produce concise updates and practical dashboards that make progress, risks, and decisions clear to policy leaders.

  • Coordinate policy deliverables and external engagements from planning through follow-up. Assemble briefing packages; draft talking points, presentations, readouts, and updates; organize visits and convenings, including logistics; manage review cycles; and track action items through completion, with substantive input and approval from policy leads.

  • Own operational management of the team's contractors and consultants, coordinating onboarding, scopes of work, deliverables, contract renewals, invoices, and offboarding with Legal, Finance, Procurement, and other relevant teams. Track commitments and performance against agreed deliverables, and flag issues requiring the team lead's decision.

  • Coordinate across Global Affairs, Research, Safety, Security, Product Policy, Legal, Communications, and OpenAI for Government to manage dependencies, surface decisions, and advance shared priorities.

  • Continuously improve the team's operating model through feedback loops, retrospectives, and thoughtful use of AI, automation, and lightweight tooling.

You should thrive in this role if you:

  • Enjoy learning enough technical and policy context to coordinate work effectively and synthesize expert inputs into clear briefing materials and updates for technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Thrive in fast-paced, flexible environments where priorities evolve and good judgment matters.

  • Collaborate effectively across policy, technical, legal, operational, and business teams.

  • Can lead complex workstreams and keep stakeholders aligned through influence rather than formal authority.

  • View program management as a craft in its own right and take satisfaction in building durable systems, creating clarity, and helping teams deliver reliably.

  • Are passionate about the promise of AI and thoughtful about its potential national security and societal risks.

  • Are energized by enabling subject-matter experts and leaders to do their best work, and bring high standards, low ego, curiosity, and a strong service orientation.

We're looking for a blend of:

  • 5+ years of relevant experience in program management, project management, policy operations, strategic operations, chief of staff, government program delivery, or related roles.

  • Experience coordinating complex work across multiple stakeholders and building practical systems that help teams deliver. Experience supporting policy, government, national security, or technical teams is a plus.

  • A track record of independently driving complex cross-functional programs from scoping through delivery, managing stakeholders, dependencies, and risks while building durable systems and delivering measurable outcomes.

  • Strong analytical, writing, and communication skills, with the ability to synthesize quantitative and qualitative inputs into crisp decision materials, action plans, and executive-ready updates.

  • The ability to understand strategic context while remaining hands-on in detailed execution, influence without formal authority, and exercise sound judgment and discretion in fast-moving, sensitive environments.

  • Genuine care for the impact of AI on national security, democratic institutions, and society; familiarity with areas such as frontier risk, cybersecurity, biosecurity, critical infrastructure, defense and intelligence applications, or technical AI governance is a plus. title: Software Engineer, Enterprise Verticals
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Enterprise Verticals builds role-specific ChatGPT Work experiences for high-value enterprise workflows. We combine product engineering, plugins and skills, connectors, data, evaluations, and customer evidence to turn useful demos into reliable daily work.

This opening sits within the Technology vertical inside Enterprise Verticals. The group focuses on repeatable workflows for people at technology companies, beginning with functions such as data and analytics, sales, and design, and carries the shared platform needs—tool integration, permissions, quality measurement, and safe rollout—across those experiences.

We work closely with Design, Research, GTM, Security, and platform teams, as well as with customers and design partners. Success means that people can reach a trustworthy first result, understand what the system did, and keep using the workflow—not merely that a prototype exists.

 

About the Role

We are looking for a full-stack product engineer who can own ambiguous enterprise workflows end to end: understand a customer problem, shape the product, build across frontend and backend, work through platform dependencies, instrument quality, and learn quickly with design partners.

You will build across ChatGPT Work surfaces, services, plugins, connectors, and data or permission boundaries when the experience requires it. You will make quality and rollout observable through evaluations, product and operational signals, and clear fallback or rollback paths.

This is a product-engineering role for someone who can move between user problems and system details without losing ownership of either. The strongest candidates will be able to turn specific customer evidence into a generalizable product, explain scope and architecture tradeoffs, and carry a feature from an early prototype through a bounded production rollout.

 

In this role, you will:

  • Build and ship role-specific workflows across ChatGPT Work surfaces, services, plugins, and connectors.

  • Turn customer and design-partner evidence into clear product decisions, milestones, and measurable quality gates without overfitting to a single customer.

  • Partner with Design, Research, GTM, Security, and platform teams.

  • Create robust evaluations, observability, and rollback paths.

  • Own the full loop from prototype through bounded rollout and iteration.

  • Define explicit contracts and fallback paths with shared platform teams when a workflow depends on connectors, permissions, model routing, or other cross-team systems.

 

You might thrive in this role if:

  • You are a strong product engineer with excellent product judgment.

  • You are comfortable moving across frontend, backend, APIs, data, and systems integration.

  • You communicate clearly with customers and cross-functional partners.

  • You use evidence and tests to make ambiguous work observable.

  • You care about enterprise permissions, reliability, privacy, and rollout safety.

  • You have shipped a user-facing product through ambiguity and can explain the decisions, tradeoffs, and evidence behind it.

  • You can translate a concrete customer workflow into a general product without losing the details that make the first experience useful.

 

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience building and operating full-stack production products across a modern frontend stack (such as React/TypeScript) and backend services (such as Python, Go, Node.js, or comparable technologies).

  • Experience designing evolvable APIs, data models, and distributed or integration-heavy systems, including authentication, identity, permissions, secure data flows, and partial-failure behavior.

title: Applied AI Engineer, API Platform, Digital Natives
descriptionHtml:
About the team

The Applied AI Engineering team is responsible for ensuring the safe and effective deployment of generative AI applications for developers and enterprises. We act as a trusted advisor and thought partner for our API customers, working to build an effective backlog of frontier AI use cases for their industry and drive them to production through strong technical guidance.

As an Applied AI Engineer in the Digital Native segment, you’ll work with industry-leading technology companies like Stripe, Uber, and Reddit to bring new AI capabilities into the products their customers use every day. You’ll partner directly with experienced product and engineering teams to turn frontier model capabilities into new features and agentic experiences. The work combines rapid experimentation with the demands of established products: complex systems, real users, and high expectations for quality and performance. Lessons from these deployments inform OpenAI’s product and research teams.

title: Software Engineer, API Multicloud
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

API Multicloud partners with cloud service providers (CSPs) to bring OpenAI’s frontier models and APIs into the cloud environments where developers and enterprises already build. We own the API end to end across CSP platforms, from API integration and request routing through inference execution, capacity management, and day-to-day operations. Our mission is to make these capabilities available broadly and safely while preserving the reliability and developer experience customers expect from OpenAI.

Delivering that experience requires work across the stack: adapting API services and cloud-native integrations, bringing up model-serving environments, validating new releases, and operating the systems that connect customer requests to available capacity. We work directly with CSP engineering teams and partner closely with OpenAI’s inference, API, infrastructure, security, and Safety Systems teams. Together, we turn new model capabilities and partner requirements into dependable production services, with attention to performance, operational readiness, and efficient use of compute.

Our work contributes to OpenAI’s AWS partnership, including the launch of Daybreak Red and Daybreak Blue on Amazon Bedrock - and OpenAI’s newly announced Google Cloud partnership will bring our frontier models and Codex agentic workflows to Google Cloud’s Model Garden. These efforts let customers use OpenAI capabilities within the cloud infrastructure, security controls, and workflows they already rely on.

About the Role

We’re looking for experienced infrastructure engineers to design, build, and operate the systems that run OpenAI’s API across CSP platforms. You’ll help establish the cloud deployment platform: configuring and launching model-serving environments, planning capacity, improving caching and utilization, and making new releases safe and repeatable. Working closely with inference engineers, you’ll connect advances in model serving to the infrastructure and operational practices needed to run them reliably in production.

The role calls for strong distributed systems judgment and comfort moving across API services, cloud infrastructure, deployment tooling, and production debugging. You’ll work directly with CSP engineers to navigate differences in infrastructure, native services, and operating models, resolve integration issues, and build reusable solutions that reduce repeated work as we expand. Your decisions will affect how quickly new capabilities reach customers, how reliably they run, and how efficiently we use cloud resources.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and build cloud infrastructure and distributed services that connect API requests, routing, and model-serving deployments.

  • Stand up and operate model-serving environments in partnership with inference engineers, bringing new models and serving capabilities into production.

  • Plan and manage cloud capacity, improving utilization, caching, request performance, and cost efficiency as demand grows.

  • Create repeatable build, release, and validation processes that catch functional and performance regressions before launch.

  • Develop reusable infrastructure abstractions that let API capabilities run consistently across CSPs while accommodating provider-specific requirements.

  • Partner with OpenAI’s inference, API, infrastructure, and security teams and CSP engineers to bring up the API serving stack on new platforms, resolve operational issues, and shape shared technical priorities.

  • Own production health through observability, incident diagnosis, reliability improvements, and practical automation.

Your background might look something like:

  • 7+ years of experience leading cloud infrastructure or distributed systems projects from architecture through launch and ongoing production ownership.

  • Strong distributed systems fundamentals and the ability to reason about performance, reliability, and failure modes.

  • Hands-on experience building and operating services on a major CSP, including deployment systems, networking, storage, and cloud-native integrations.

  • Strong production coding and debugging skills, with the ability to move confidently through unfamiliar services and infrastructure.

  • Experience with capacity planning, performance optimization, or operational tooling for production systems at scale.

title: Software Engineer, Platform Systems
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Platform Systems team at OpenAI operates at the intersection of cutting-edge AI and large-scale distributed systems. We build the engineering and research infrastructure required to train OpenAI’s flagship models on some of the world’s largest, custom-built supercomputers.

Our team develops core model training software and works deep in the stack - spanning collective communication, compute efficiency, parallelism strategies, fault tolerance, failure detection, and observability. The systems we build are foundational to OpenAI’s research velocity, enabling reliable, efficient training at frontier scale.

We collaborate closely with researchers across the organization, continuously incorporating learnings from across OpenAI into the evolution of our training platform.

About the Role

As a Software Engineer, Platform Systems, you will design and build distributed systems that provide visibility into large-scale training workloads and help operate them reliably at scale.

You’ll work on failure detection, tracing, and observability systems that identify slow or faulty nodes, surface performance bottlenecks, and help engineers understand and optimize massive distributed training jobs. This infrastructure is critical to operating OpenAI’s training stack and is actively evolving to support new use cases and increasingly complex workloads.

This role sits at the core of our training infrastructure, blending systems engineering, performance analysis, and large-scale debugging.

In This Role, You Will

  • Design and build distributed failure detection, tracing, and profiling systems for large-scale AI training jobs

  • Develop tooling to identify slow, faulty, or misbehaving nodes and provide actionable visibility into system behavior

  • Improve observability, reliability, and performance across OpenAI’s training platform

  • Debug and resolve issues in complex, high-throughput distributed systems

  • Collaborate with systems, infrastructure, and research teams to evolve platform capabilities

  • Extend and adapt failure detection systems or tracing systems to support new training paradigms and workloads

title: Software Engineer, Healthcare
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Healthcare team is working to ensure that advances in AI meaningfully improve health for everyone. We build AI systems that support patients, clinicians, and healthcare organizations while setting a high standard for deploying AI responsibly in a high-stakes domain.

On the Healthcare team, we are building products and infrastructure that bring OpenAI’s capabilities into healthcare organizations and clinical workflows. We serve health care systems, insurance companies, and the broad range of healthcare IT companies. Our products include connecting ChatGPT with healthcare data and systems and building reliable enterprise experiences that can operate within complex security, privacy, compliance, and interoperability requirements.

We work closely with product, research, design, security, privacy, GTM, and our healthcare customers to turn powerful AI capabilities into dependable products that clinicians and healthcare organizations use in their everyday work.

About the Role

We are looking for backend and full-stack software engineers to build the systems behind OpenAI’s healthcare products.

You will work across backend services, APIs, data systems, integrations, and product surfaces to connect AI with healthcare workflows and enterprise data. You’ll tackle the technical challenges involved in making these systems secure, reliable, observable, and scalable enough for real-world healthcare environments.

This is a product-engineering role for someone who can move between customer problems and complex system architecture, and who is comfortable owning ambiguous problems end-to-end.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and build backend and full-stack systems powering OpenAI’s healthcare products.

  • Build services, APIs, and data pipelines that connect OpenAI products with healthcare systems and enterprise data.

  • Develop integrations with electronic health records and other healthcare data sources.

  • Design systems that meet demanding requirements around privacy, security, permissions, compliance, and data governance.

  • Own features and systems from early architecture and implementation through deployment, monitoring, and iteration.

  • Build reliable systems capable of handling complex data flows, partial failures, and evolving integration requirements.

  • Partner closely with product, research, security, privacy, GTM, and healthcare organizations to translate real-world workflows into scalable products.

  • Improve the reliability, performance, observability, and operational maturity of production healthcare systems.

  • Take ownership of ambiguous technical problems and drive them toward practical, durable solutions.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Are a strong backend or full-stack engineer who enjoys building durable production systems.

  • Have 5+ years of experience writing maintainable, production-quality software.

  • Have strong experience with backend services, APIs, data systems, or distributed systems.

  • Are comfortable reasoning about system architecture, data models, authentication, permissions, and integration boundaries.

  • Have experience owning production systems at scale, including observability, testing, incident response, migrations, and rollout.

  • Can move between product requirements and technical architecture without losing ownership of either.

  • Operate with high agency and are comfortable taking ambiguous problems from definition through production.

  • Enjoy working directly with cross-functional partners and customers to understand complex workflows.

  • Care deeply about reliability, privacy, security, and correctness.

  • Are motivated by the opportunity to improve healthcare through AI.

Nice to have:

  • Experience building enterprise SaaS products or platforms.

  • Experience with distributed systems, backend architecture, or large-scale data pipelines.

  • Experience building integrations with complex third-party systems or APIs.

  • Experience with authentication, identity, permissions, or enterprise security.

  • Experience working in regulated industries such as healthcare, finance, or enterprise infrastructure.

  • Experience with healthcare interoperability, EHR systems, or healthcare data standards.

  • Experience building HIPAA-compliant products or systems.

  • Experience building applied AI or conversational products.

  • Previous experience in healthcare or health technology.

title: Senior Manager, Occupancy Planning & Workplace Strategy
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Real Estate & Workplace (REW) team creates and operates the spaces that support our people and our mission. Within REW, the Strategic Occupancy Planning team connects business needs, workplace strategy, and space data to help shape where and how our teams work.

We partner closely with business leaders, Finance, People, Workplace Operations, and Design & Construction to anticipate growth, optimize space utilization, and deliver a thoughtful, scalable workplace experience.

About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced Occupancy Planning & Workplace Strategy Manager to lead strategic space planning for our Go-to-Market (GTM) and General & Administrative (G&A) organizations.

In this role, you’ll translate evolving business needs into actionable occupancy strategies, capacity scenarios, and workplace recommendations. You’ll serve as a trusted partner to business leaders, balancing growth projections, operational requirements, and employee experience to inform decisions about how our teams use space.

You’ll own planning across a complex, evolving portfolio while leveraging CAFM/IWMS systems and data analytics to drive accurate, scalable decision-making. This role requires a combination of strategic thinking, hands-on technical expertise, and strong cross-functional partnership to turn planning recommendations into operational outcomes.

This role is based in San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week, with approximately 10–20% travel.

In This Role, You Will

  • Own strategic occupancy planning for GTM and G&A organizations, translating headcount forecasts, business priorities, and workplace needs into actionable space plans.

  • Develop and evaluate capacity scenarios, neighborhood strategies, team adjacencies, seating models, and space allocation recommendations to support organizational growth.

  • Partner with business leaders and executive stakeholders to understand evolving requirements, communicate trade-offs, and align workplace strategies with business objectives.

  • Collaborate with Finance, People, Analytics, Design & Construction, and Workplace Operations to reconcile forecasts, assess capacity constraints, and guide planning decisions through implementation.

  • Translate workplace needs into practical stacking, blocking, and move plans, ensuring recommendations account for operational feasibility, timing, and employee experience.

  • Leverage CAFM/IWMS platforms and analytical tools to maintain accurate space inventories, floor plans, seating allocations, and utilization data.

  • Identify and resolve space data discrepancies, establish quality controls, and partner with internal system owners and external vendors to improve data reliability.

  • Develop dashboards, planning workflows, and reporting tools that improve visibility into occupancy trends, capacity risks, and portfolio performance.

  • Drive continuous improvement in occupancy planning processes, including opportunities for automation, system enhancements, and scalable planning practices.

  • Support workplace change initiatives by partnering with cross-functional teams to ensure clear communication, coordinated execution, and successful transitions.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You

  • Bring 5–8+ years of experience in occupancy planning, workplace strategy, space management, or a related field, with experience independently managing complex, multi-team or multi-site portfolios.

  • Have a strong track record of translating business growth, headcount projections, and workplace requirements into practical, data-informed space strategies.

  • Possess hands-on experience with CAFM/IWMS platforms, including space inventory management, floor plans, seating allocations, data reconciliation, and reporting.

  • Are highly analytical and comfortable developing scenarios, evaluating trade-offs, and translating complex data into clear recommendations for senior stakeholders.

  • Excel at building trusted relationships with business leaders and cross-functional partners, influencing decisions without direct authority.

  • Can balance long-term strategic planning with hands-on execution in a fast-paced environment where priorities and requirements evolve quickly.

  • Have experience supporting workplace transitions, flexible seating strategies, organizational growth, or large-scale space planning initiatives.

  • Communicate clearly and effectively, whether presenting recommendations to executives, documenting planning assumptions, or coordinating implementation across teams.

  • Are comfortable navigating ambiguity, identifying opportunities for process improvement, and building scalable solutions.

Experience with OfficeSpace or comparable CAFM/IWMS platforms, CAD or floor-plan tools, business intelligence platforms, system migrations, and vendor management is a plus.

title: Silicon Design Lead
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Silicon Design Lead to drive architecture, microarchitecture, and implementation of key IP and subsystems for our AI hardware platforms. You will translate functional, performance, and security requirements into efficient silicon designs, owning technical decisions from architectural definition through implementation and integration.

Part of this role will focus on hardware security implementation in close partnership with OpenAI’s Security team. While the Security team owns the overarching security architecture and requirements, you will translate those requirements into silicon microarchitecture and implementation, balancing security capabilities with performance, power, area, and design complexity. The other part of this role will focus on driving general silicon architecture/microarchitecture. 

In this role, you will:

  • Own architecture, microarchitecture, and implementation of silicon IP and subsystems, from requirements and design specifications through integration and validation.

  • Define hardware interfaces, data flows, and microarchitectural tradeoffs to meet functional, performance, power, and area requirements.

  • Partner closely with OpenAI’s Security team to translate security architecture, requirements, and threat models into implementable hardware capabilities.

  • Design and integrate hardware security mechanisms, including encryption, key management, access controls, isolation, and data protection across silicon subsystems.

  • Evaluate architectural and implementation tradeoffs to ensure security capabilities meet functional and performance requirements.

  • Collaborate with silicon architects, RTL, verification, firmware, and software teams to drive subsystem design, integration, and validation.

  • Review and contribute to RTL implementations, ensuring designs align with architectural intent and system requirements.

  • Evaluate existing and third-party IP, identify architectural or implementation gaps, and drive solutions across subsystem boundaries.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have strong experience in silicon IP or subsystem-level architecture, microarchitecture, and implementation.

  • Have owned hardware IP or subsystem designs from architectural definition through implementation and integration.

  • Have experience implementing hardware security features such as memory encryption, key management, access controls, isolation, or secure boot.

  • Understand how to translate functional and security requirements into hardware architectures, interfaces, and microarchitectural specifications.

  • Have working knowledge of RTL design and coding proficiency in Verilog or SystemVerilog, with the ability to read, review, and contribute to RTL.

  • Can evaluate performance, power, area, and complexity tradeoffs across silicon designs.

  • Work effectively across security, silicon architecture, RTL, verification, firmware, and software teams to drive designs from concept through execution.

  • Ideally, have broader SoC-level architecture or integration experience, though deep IP or subsystem-level expertise is sufficient.

To comply with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidates for this role may need to meet certain legal status requirements as provided in those laws and regulations.

title: Global Candidate Experience Manager
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Candidate Experience team ensures that every interaction candidates and interviewers have with OpenAI reflects excellence, fairness, and humanity. This team owns global coordination, interview logistics, onsite experience, Interview Programs, and the operational workflows that support all recruiting functions, from Executive and Research to Technical, GTM, and G&A. The Candidate Experience team supports a wide range of hiring modalities (from executive and research to high-volume technical roles), and we need someone who understands how to adapt across them. As OpenAI scales globally, this team plays a critical role in designing experiences that are both bespoke for highly specialized searches and scalable across rapidly growing teams and offices.

About the Role

As Global Candidate Experience Manager, you will manage CE managers and Interview Programs program managers, with global responsibility for candidate experience, coordination and interview program delivery. You will lead through the team’s managers, leads and program owners while staying close enough to daily work to understand where it breaks. You will own service quality, capacity planning, interviewer readiness, program delivery and continuous improvement across high-volume and highly bespoke hiring.

We are looking for a hands-on operating leader who can build useful AI-enabled workflows, forecast and allocate capacity, and drive complex programs from diagnosis through launch and sustained adoption. You should be comfortable reviewing a queue with coordinators, testing a workflow with technical partners, and translating a broad goal into clear owners, milestones and decisions. Your aim is to strengthen the team’s judgment and autonomy while improving candidate care.

You can move between global operating design and frontline detail, reprioritize as demand changes, and deliver high-quality work quickly despite ambiguity. You know when to standardize and automate, when a human should remain accountable, and how to explain practical tradeoffs among speed, quality, workload and fairness.

In this role, you will:

  • Manage and develop CE managers and Interview Programs program managers; support their leads and coordinators through clear priorities, delegated decisions, timely feedback and fair accountability.

  • Stay close to daily work through queue reviews, workflow walkthroughs and direct team feedback. Diagnose system, capacity and skill problems, and personally lead selected projects with clear ownership.

  • Own CE service delivery across high-volume and confidential Executive/Research hiring. Improve scheduling, routing, handoffs and onsite experience, with clear exception and escalation boundaries.

  • Build and maintain a capacity model covering demand mix, handling time, productive hours, skills, regional coverage, leave, rework and backlog recovery.

  • Set priorities across CE service and Interview Programs with recruiting leaders. Make staffing and service tradeoffs early, accounting for regional coverage, workforce continuity, interviewer bandwidth and fair coordinator workloads.

  • Drive programs and projects end to end: define the problem and success measures; manage owners, milestones, dependencies, risks, launch readiness and adoption.

  • Own Interview Programs’ operating model, priorities and delivery through accountable program owners, including readiness, onboarding, calibration support, question governance, integrity escalation and loop health. Preserve technical approval, hiring and investigation decisions with their designated owners.

  • Personally shape and test practical AI-enabled workflows with Recruiting Optimization and People Technology; use approved data, evaluation cases, human review, monitoring and rollback.

  • Measure net improvements after review and rework, and turn successful pilots into adopted processes with training, documentation and accountable owners.

  • Run a focused service-health cadence using queue age, SLA attainment, demand/capacity variance, scheduling efficiency, quality/rework, candidate feedback and interviewer load.

  • Partner with Recruiting, Executive Operations, People Technology, People Analytics, Workplace, IT and HR Operations to remove cross-functional bottlenecks.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Strong operations leadership: Led high-performing teams in People Operations, Recruiting Operations or another operations function, with clear accountability for service quality and results.

  • Experience at scale: Managed high-volume operations in a high-growth environment, adapting staffing, workflows and priorities as demand and complexity increased.

  • Excellent program management: Delivered complex, cross-functional programs from problem definition through launch and sustained adoption, with clear owners, milestones, dependencies and measures of success.

  • People leadership: Managed and developed managers and program owners through effective coaching, delegation, feedback and accountability.

  • Hands-on execution and bias to action: Stays close to frontline work, uses data to diagnose problems and moves work forward with sound judgment—even when the path is unclear.

  • Practical AI experience: Personally built, configured or tested AI-enabled workflows and can explain what improved, how they evaluated it and what they learned.

Nice to Have

  • Experience running multi-region coverage or supporting a mix of high-volume and confidential, bespoke hiring.

  • Contingent-workforce planning, including vendor coordination, handoffs and continuity through departures.

  • Ashby and Guide experience, or deeper experience with question governance, integrity escalation and interviewer readiness.

San Francisco headquarters. Hybrid schedule - Monday to Wednesday in office.

At OpenAI, our User Safety & Risk Operations (USRO) team helps protect our products and users from abuse, fraud, safety risks, and other forms of misuse. We operate at the front line of real-world safety and risk management, translating user and operational signals into timely decisions, effective interventions, and improvements to our systems.

This role sits on a team focused on building operational capacity for new, ambiguous, and fast-moving areas of work. The team defines what needs to be built, creates the operating model to support it, and works with partner teams to make the work scalable and durable over time.

About the Role

We are seeking a Device Safety & Risk Operations Specialist to build the safety operating model for a new category of consumer hardware. This is a senior individual-contributor role for someone who can turn emerging product risks and incomplete requirements into practical workflows, controls, launch plans, and durable systems.

You will define how product-safety incidents, critical escalations, regulated cases, and privacy-sensitive issues should be identified, investigated, escalated, resolved, and learned from. You will also establish operational requirements for case management, data access, decision logging, quality assurance, monitoring, and cross-functional response. You will stand up priority workflows through launch and early operations, then help transition them into durable homes across USRO and partner teams.

The right person combines deep operational judgment with strong technical and hardware product fluency. They can move from executive-level risk framing to detailed workflow design, tabletop exercises, launch readiness, frontline guidance, and post-launch improvement.

Location / work model: San Francisco, CA; hybrid, 3 days/week in-office.

Please note: This role may involve exposure to sensitive or concerning material. Strong discretion, judgment, and resilience are essential.


In This Role, You Will:

  • Build the end-to-end safety and risk operating model for new consumer hardware, from early requirements through launch and early-life operations.

  • Define incident taxonomies, severity levels, decision rights, escalation criteria, response pathways, and closure standards.

  • Develop operational playbooks for product-safety incidents, critical escalations, safety advisories, corrective actions, and other high-risk events.

  • Design workflows for regulated and privacy-sensitive cases, including restricted handling, evidence requirements, auditability, and partner escalation.

  • Translate safety and operational needs into requirements for tooling, case management, data access, monitoring, logging, and automation.

  • Establish clear ownership boundaries across Product, Engineering, Legal, Privacy, Product Policy, Support, Product Quality, and other operational partners.

  • Build launch-readiness plans, tabletop exercises, training, quality controls, reporting, and post-launch monitoring.

  • Use operational data, customer signals, product telemetry, and case outcomes to identify patterns and improve upstream products and systems.

  • Determine where AI and automation can improve triage, evidence assembly, consistency, and response while preserving appropriate human judgment.

  • Stand up priority workflows, operate them through launch and early-life stabilization, and transition them into durable homes across USRO and partner teams.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You:

  • Have 8+ years of relevant experience in device safety, product safety, consumer hardware operations, technical program management, or a related field.

  • Have built a complex safety or risk program from an ambiguous starting point through launch and scaled operation.

  • Understand the realities of handling high-severity incidents, regulated workflows, sensitive customer information, and time-critical escalations.

  • Can translate product, engineering, legal, privacy, and policy constraints into workflows that operational teams can execute.

  • Are technically fluent and can reason through data flows, telemetry, access controls, audit logs, case systems, automation, and failure modes.

  • Use data to assess workflow health, identify emerging patterns, evaluate quality, and make risk-based decisions.

  • Can establish clear accountability across teams with overlapping responsibilities and different risk tolerances.

  • Know how to balance launch speed with safety controls, monitoring, rollback criteria, and longer-term system development.

  • Communicate clearly with operational, technical, legal, and executive audiences when evidence is incomplete or tradeoffs are difficult.

  • Are highly practical and willing to build the workflow, not only define the strategy.

  • Experience supporting consumer hardware, connected devices, or other products used in shared environments.

  • Experience with product-safety investigations, recalls, field failures, safety advisories, or hazardous-product handling.

  • Experience designing workflows involving privacy-sensitive sensor, diagnostic, media, or household data.

  • Familiarity with warranty, repair, reverse logistics, identity recovery, fraud, or ownership disputes.

  • Experience building vendor training, quality-assurance, incident-response, or specialist-review programs.

The OpenAI for Government AI Architect team partners with public sector organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact. We work with government agencies, public institutions, and partner organizations serving the government to identify where AI can advance critical missions, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption.
